News.title: Forget your watering can – ‘spoon-feeding’ method will bring your parched lawn back to life this summer
News.content:
BRITS may have been enjoying a summer basking in the sun but hosepipe bans have taken a toll on lawns.

There is, however, a little-known method that could transform your yellowing grass into a lush oasis once again.



Nothing says unsightly garden quite like dry, yellow patches of lawn.

And, as this dry spell continues throughout the UK amid hosepipe bans, you can’t rely on the rain to revitalise your garden.



However, there is help at hand, and it’s a surprisingly simple process.

It’s called “spoon-feeding fertilisation”, and experts regard this as the best lawn-feeding method for keeping your grass healthy and green all-year round.

It involves doing exactly what its says – literally “spoon feeding” small amounts of fertiliser on your garden regularly.

It’s recommended to drop no more than 0.5 lbs of nitrogen per 1,000 sq ft every 4-6 weeks.

There are downsides to the process, however, as outlined in a blog post by the experts at Evergreen Outdoor Services.

The major downside is the frequency of applying the fertilizer to a lawn.



“Staying on a consistent schedule is crucial,” they added.

“Missed applications can disrupt nutrient availability and impact overall lawn health.”

Gardeners should water their lawn lightly right after fertilising – just enough to wet the soil.

Aim to do this consistently every 4–6 weeks and enjoy a healthy, green, and strong lawn.

News.title: ‘Temu Barbie’ jailed for killing ex in acid attack after she teamed up with drug gang to target him in deadly plot
News.content:
LOCKED UP ‘Temu Barbie’ jailed for killing ex in acid attack after she teamed up with drug gang to target him in deadly plot

A MUM has been jailed for killing her ex-husband in an acid attack after teaming up with a drug gang to target him in a deadly plot.

Dad-of-two Danny Cahalane was rushed to hospital after he was targeted by two men at his home in Plymouth, Devon, last February.



He could not be saved and died from his “horrific” injuries on May 3, 2025.

His ex-wife Paris Wilson, 35, stood trial with eight others over the brutal attack.



She was today jailed for nine years after being convicted of manslaughter.

The court heard how former probation worker Wilson revealed Danny’s location to his boss Ryan Kennedy – known as Frost – before the killing.



Jurors heard Danny was “middle management” in a drug-dealing operation and owed Frost £120,000 after gambling away his profits.

Following their “acrimonious” split, Wilson became a “go-to” for the Dubai-based gangster as he plotted to get his money back.



She told Frost she would reveal Danny’s location to the drug dealer on the understanding he would “make her wealthy”.

The killer also believed her ex-husband, who she shared a child with, “deserved to be hurt”.

Winchester Crown Court heard this was despite Wilson knowing that Frost was a “threat” to Danny.

Just days before the killing, she told Danny: “I hope you and your (girlfriend) both end up with acid in your face.”

She also messaged her mum about the daughter she shared with Danny, saying: “I think he is keeping her so Frost doesn’t go near him.”



Another message read: “Like Frost is losing his mind….Frost is saying he will pay me if I find where he is today…he said he will pay me a few grand and double what Dan owes you and give you an oz…so 600 and a oz.”

The court heard Wilson also told her mum Frost was “minted” and his crime gang “can’t handle any more of his lies”.

Referring to Danny’s new partner Michaela, Wilson, she continued: “They said they’d grab her and get her to take them to him..and she’s a c*** tbh mum so I don’t care.”



She added: “I’m worried about my karma, but at least nobody but Dan gets hurt, and he did f*** massively with my life…and he deserves it.”

Jurors were told Danny had got into debt with Frost originally after he gambled with profits from the drug-dealing operation.

Prosecutor Joanne Martin KC said: “That left, in Danny’s words, Danny in the s***. He told police he was in significant debt and he tried to organise a repayment plan but it didn’t work.”

The month before he was attacked, Frost messaged Danny telling him: “You’re gonna die, you just need to die. You’ve done me £80k. I’m going to give them 40k extra to take the eyes out of your head.”

Danny replied: ‘You’re talking about switching me off. I have 46 covered. Sorting for you. Been long.”



Over the next two days, Frost continued to message the victim and send him threats.

On January 18, he text again saying: “I’m just paying someone the bill to get you done. On my life, I ain’t messaging you again, I’ll find you by tomorrow.”

The prosecutor said Frost had become “incensed” at Danny’s “stalling” and failure to repay the money and organised a kidnap attempt on January 19 2025.

Jurors heard three men confronted Danny and tried to open his car door – causing him to flee.

The dad was described by witnesses as as looking “wide eyed” and terrified.



After the kidnap plan failed, Frost messaged him saying: “Close call? Mate I’m telling you they gonna burn gaffes down and your gonna die”.

The court was told there was “no doubt” Wilson set Danny up because “she told Frost exactly where he would be” that day and “only she could have known that he was dropping off their daughter that morning at her house”.

Ms Martin said: “Paris Wilson knew that Frost meant business.

“She knew the level of threat that Frost was issuing to Danny.”

On February 21 last year, jurors heard two men broke into Danny’s home and attacked him with sulphuric acid – burning his entire body.



He was rushed to hospital but died ten weeks later from his “horrific” injuries, it was said.

Ms Martin said: “There can be no doubt that Mr Cahalane was murdered, whoever threw acid over him must have intended to at the very least cause him really serious bodily harm.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Co-defendants Abdulrasheed Adedoja and Israel Augustus were found guilty of murder, while Ramarnee Bakas was convicted of manslaughter.

Two brothers – Arrone Mukuna, 24, and Jean Mukuna, 23, were found guilty of attempted kidnap along with Wilson.

News.title: New Chancellor sets date for Andy Burnham’s first Budget and vows to move ‘money and power’ out of London
News.content:
CHANCELLOR John Healey said his first Budget will “move money and power out of Westminster” and into “every postcode around Britain”.

Announcing the Budget on Wednesday October 28, Mr Healey said in a video message: “This Government is working fast to restore hope and back Britain’s communities.



“In the past two weeks, we have begun to kickstart growth in every postcode. We have backed British jobs, British skills and British businesses.

“And we have provided just a bit of breathing space for those families and businesses that feel so squeezed, that feel without hope.



“Today, I’m confirming the date of my first Budget as Chancellor will be Wednesday 28th October.

“This will be a Budget that moves money and power out of Westminster and into every postcode around Britain.



“It will be built on fiscal discipline. It will meet our fiscal rules. It’ll give businesses and families some of the stability they need to plan for the future.

“Now, let’s get on with the job.”



Looking back at Andy Burnham’s first two weeks as Prime Minister, Mr Healey – who served as Defence Secretary under former premier Sir Keir Starmer – said the new government was “working fast to restore hope and back Britain’s communities” and had “begun to kickstart growth in every postcode”.

But he will face significant challenges as he finds more money for Mr Burnham’s devolution priorities and increased defence spending amid warnings the Iran war will further squeeze the public finances.

Mr Healey’s announcement comes days after he vowed to go on a “buy British” blitz on a scale the country has never seen before.

The new Chancellor said every pound the government spends will be focused on creating new jobs and backing businesses in the UK.



In his first interview since Andy Burnham put him in charge of the Treasury, Mr Healey said he wants to turbocharge UK plc.

And he vowed to “lift that pessimism” that has descended on Brits clobbered by the cost of living crisis and give people “hope for the future”.

His boosterist words are in contrast to the more gloomy tone Sir Keir Starmer’s regime adopted about the economy in its first months in government.

Speaking exclusively to The Sun on Sunday, Mr Healey said: “We will make every government department a growth department – backing Britain.



“You will see this as a determined drive that you have not seen before from a British government.

“Buying British not if possible, but by design. So every procurement pound supports British jobs, British apprenticeships and British skills.

“Driving wealth creation so the policy decisions we take in government help raise levels of investment and profit and innovation in British business.”

In his old job as Defence Secretary, Mr Healey used his budget to buy kit from UK defence firms and create British jobs.

Out of the 1,200 major defence contacts handed out, 86 per cent went to British firms.



Mr Healey wants to roll that “Buy British” approach out across the government, and sees the new big devolution push as the perfect way to do that.

“I will certainly be talking up the resilience and the potential of British business,” he adds.

“I am as concerned about the cost of business as I am the cost of living.

“I am really concerned that where we make government policy and government decisions, these can help raise the levels of investment, innovation and profit in British business.”

Mr Burnham has used his first week as PM to announce a series of eye-catching cost of living policies to provide “more breathing space” to Brits struggling with their bills.



Bus fares will be capped at £2, VAT taken off electricity bills and pubs and clubs will get a business rates tax cut.

Westminster insiders have dubbed this cost of living blitz a “Tesco approach to government” after the supermarket’s famous catchphrase that “every little helps”.

Each individual announcement is only small – designed to ease the pain of spiralling bills but not break the bank.

Taken together, they are designed to show that Downing Street “gets it” and are serious about helping families struggling with their bills.

“This is about demonstrating Andy Burnham’s view about how to lift the pessimism that people feel about their own prospects and the places they live”, Mr Healey said.



“Andy Burnham talks about lifting the everyday pressures people feel.

“When you see us taking those steps this week – that is what we are concerned about trying to do.

“Give people a sense of hope for the future and a glimpse of the new economy and new hope we want to build for the future of this country.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mr Healey sees boosting British business and easing the cost of living crisis as two sides of the same coin.

Providing good British jobs is the best way of ensuring people can buy a home and pay their bills, he believes.

News.title: Will there be another heatwave? Latest Met Office weather forecast for August as UK temperatures drop
News.content:
COOLER conditions could be on the way for parts of the UK this weekend, after temperatures peaked at 35.2C on Wednesday, 29 July.

But after half of England declared drought earlier this week, it’s predicted that only a little rain will be coming for the driest parts of the country.



As we head into a new month, will heatwave conditions return? Here is everything you need to know.

Will there be another heatwave in 2026?

With four official heatwaves recorded this year, would it be naive to rule out a fifth?



The Met Office’s long-range forecast suggests the conditions required for another official heatwave are possible later in August, particularly in the south of the country.

But a few hot days do not automatically mean a heatwave.

For a heatwave to be officially declared, specific Met Office criteria must be met.

A location must record a period of at least three consecutive days where the daily maximum temperature meets or exceeds the official heatwave threshold.

This threshold varies across the UK to reflect different regional climates.

For example, the threshold is 28C in London and surrounding counties, but drops to 25C for Scotland, Northern Ireland, and much of northern England.



If temperatures hit these targets for three days in a row, a fifth heatwave will go on the record.

What is the latest forecast for August?

Forecasters have confirmed that heading into early August, temperatures will be much cooler and closer to the seasonal average.

The Met Office has even said that Friday, July 31 will feel “chilly” for many, bringing a scattering of showers to the North.

While northern Scotland may even see temperatures dip slightly below average, Saturday, August 1 will bring a cool start with plenty of dry weather, though an isolated shower is still possible.

What is the Met Office’s long-range forecast?

Looking further ahead using the Met Office’s long-range forecast, August is set to be a month of two halves.



Tuesday, August 4 – Thursday, August 13

“A generally rather changeable period looks likely, with many places likely to see some much needed rain or showers at times but also some more sunshine.

“Initially, some heavy rain looks likely across the northeast, with some showers elsewhere.

“After a drier, brighter few days, further unsettled conditions may develop for a while, these perhaps more likely towards more southern parts of the UK.

“Thereafter, further spells of dry, warm, sunny weather and cooler, wetter and breezier weather look likely as we head towards mid-August.

“Temperatures will likely be a little above average overall, and there is the potential for some very warm or hot spells, especially in the south, although perhaps not the heat we have seen in recent weeks.”



Friday, August 14 – Friday, August 28

“Dry and settled conditions look likely to dominate much of this period with high pressure patterns tending to affect the UK.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This may be interrupted at times by Atlantic frontal systems, especially in the north, or thunderstorms in the south.

“However, overall, rainfall amounts will likely be below normal. Temperatures will probably be above normal and some spells of hot weather and heatwaves are possible, especially in the south.”

News.title: MasterChef winner, 37, found dead at home after ‘heart attack’ as friend discovered body in bedroom
News.content:
TRAGIC LOSS MasterChef winner, 37, found dead at home after ‘heart attack’ as friend discovered body in bedroom

A MASTERCHEF winner has died unexpectedly of a suspected heart attack just five years after rising to fame.

Eren Kaşıkç, 37, who won the Turkish edition of the cooking show was found dead in his bedroom on July 29.



His body was later discovered at his home in Istanbul by his business partner, Mikail Malkoçoğlu.

An investigation has been launched into his sudden death.



Kaşıkç shot to fame after winning the 2021 season of MasterChef and later returned for the show’s All Star series.

The alarm was raised by the TV personality’s family after they could not reach him.

Paramedics pronounced him dead at the scene and his body was taken for an autopsy to establish the exact cause.

Initial assessments indicated there is a “strong possibility” the chef died of a heart attack, according to Malkoçoğlu.



Known by his nickname Kızıl Sakal, meaning Red Beard, he opened his own restaurant Kızıl Sakal Sandwich & Burger in Istanbul following his victory.

Plans were in the works to open a new location.

A funeral is set to take place before a burial at his family’s home in the province of Tokat on July 31.



Born in Kirikkale in 1989 and originally from the northern province of Tokat, Kasikci was married and had one daughter.

Kasikci built his experience working in the kitchens of several Istanbul hotels before moving to the Aegean island of Gokceada, where he became head chef at a surf hotel.

MasterChef Turkey judge Mehmet Yalçınkaya said: “My dear brother, you always said ‘God exists, there is no sorrow,’ my dear brother, you had a heart that wouldn’t even hurt an ant.

“You never had your eye on worldly possessions. My heart aches, a fire has fallen into my soul. May God grant you paradise. I’m sorry, gok.”

Fellow judge, Danilo Zanna said: “My dearest Eren… I was always so happy to have known you.



“Your smiling face, sincerity, and beautiful heart will always remain in my memory.

“The beautiful memories you left behind and the mark you left on people’s hearts will never be erased.

“Our deepest condolences. We will never forget you.

“I offer my condolences and prayers for strength to your family and everyone who loved you.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“May your beautiful heart rest in peace.”



The investigation into his death continues.

News.title: Can I clean my windows using a hosepipe during a hosepipe ban?
News.content:
A NEW hosepipe ban has been introduced for two million Brits today (July 31), after half of England declared drought conditions.

Over 23million Brits are currently under the restrictions across England and Wales, with the latest ban from Essex and Suffolk Water set to come into force next Monday.

When water companies introduce a hosepipe ban, keeping your home tidy can feel like navigating a legal minefield.



Many householders wonder what is and isn’t allowed under the restrictions, especially when it comes to keeping grime off glass.



If your windows are looking grubby, here is everything you need to know about the rules on window cleaning during a hosepipe ban, and how to get the job done legally.

Can I clean my home’s windows using a hosepipe?

If a hosepipe ban is in place in your area, using a hosepipe attached to the mains supply to wash down your home (including windows, walls, paths, or patios) is prohibited.

This rule applies whether you are using a standard garden hose, an pressure washer (jet wash) attachment, or a specialised hose-fed brush.

Water companies put these measures in place under Section 76 of the Water Industry Act 1991 to conserve public water supplies during dry spells.

Breaking the ban is a criminal offence that can trigger a fine of up to £1,000.

But this doesn’t mean your windows must stay filthy until the rain returns.

The ban specifically targets hosepipes and high-pressure equipment connected to mains water.



You can legally clean domestic windows yourself using a traditional bucket and sponge filled from the tap, a watering can or bucket using rainwater collected from a water butt, or handheld spray bottles paired with a squeegee.

Naturally, indoor glass isn’t affected – unless you were planning on bringing the hose into the lounge…

Can I clean my business’ windows?

If you run a business or manage commercial premises, the rules are slightly different, but you still need to exercise caution.

Standard hosepipe bans primarily target domestic water use, meaning non-essential home activities like watering private gardens or washing residential windows.

Commercial premises carrying out business operations are generally exempt from standard temporary domestic restrictions.



If your business relies on clean windows for operations or health and safety, using water for those core business purposes is typically permitted.

But if an employee simply grabs a standard garden hose to spray down a shopfront, it can cause confusion with neighbours and water inspectors.

While commercial activities have legal leeway, water companies still urge businesses to minimise non-essential water usage during droughts.

To stay responsible, consider using buckets or hiring professional commercial window cleaners who use dedicated water-wise systems.

Can window cleaners work during a hosepipe ban – can I hire one?

Professional window cleaners are fully permitted to continue working during a hosepipe ban, and you can legally hire one to clean your home’s windows.



Because window cleaning companies operate as a registered commercial trade, they are exempt from domestic hosepipe bans.

When a business uses water to provide a service to customers, the domestic restrictions do not apply to them.

Modern professional window cleaners also rarely plug into your mains water or blast standard garden hoses.

Most professionals use van-mounted pure water systems that feature dedicated internal water tanks filled and filtered off-site, using zero hosepipe water from your property.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And most water-fed poles used by professionals deliver purified water with high efficiency, using far less water than a domestic hosepipe.



If you want crystal-clear glass without risking a £1,000 fine or sweating over a bucket, hiring a professional window cleaner is completely legal.

News.title: Distraught mum, 28, handed animal remains instead of her unborn baby’s ashes by heartless funeral director
News.content:
A DISTRAUGHT mum was handed animal remains instead of her unborn baby’s ashes by a heartless funeral director.

Among the bodies left to decay inside Robert Bush’s funeral home of horrors were the remains of four unborn babies, a court was told.



Police cautiously stepped into a back room at his Legacy Independent Funeral Directors and discovered an unimaginable scene.

On racks three stories high were the bodies of 35 people, mostly uncovered and in various states of decomposition.



One body lay naked on a stretcher on the dirty floor alongside four sealed cardboard coffins.

But most harrowing of all was discarded brown paper bags next to the door.



Lucy Ness has spoken of her pain at being left with “nothing to remind me of my child” and the anguish of not knowing what happened to her ashes, despite hoping that they are with someone who is looking after them.

The 28-year-old put her trust in funeral director Robert Bush after suffering a miscarriage two days before her 12-week scan in April 2021.

Several weeks later he presented her with a baby urn filled with ashes he claimed were of her unborn child.

The urn sat in her living room for three years until police launched an investigation into Legacy Independent Funeral Directors and Bush was arrested.

Officers discovered that Bush did not collect Ms Ness’s baby’s ashes from the crematorium until two days after he had already given her the urn.



They found the bag that had contained her baby’s ashes at Bush’s funeral home but it was open and had been emptied.

“It’s the big unknown of what’s happened to mine, if he’s given them to someone else…

“I’ll never find out, that’s the hardest part,” Ms Ness said.

Her trauma increased when weeks before Bush was sentenced, Ms Ness said police told her that a specialist had examined the remains and believed part of them appeared to be from an animal.

Ms Ness described being “distraught”, saying: “It just seems like one problem after another, with all this, it’s taken a toll on me mentally.



“I’m not the person I used to be, I feel like I’m such a shy person, I don’t have any trust any more.

“I always like to think my baby’s out there with someone else, but the unknown is the worst thing about it.

“He had a duty of care and he’s not followed through with that.”



“He had a duty of care and he’s not followed through with that.”

A police sergeant opened another paper bag and initially thought, perhaps hoped, he was looking at a baby bird.

But on closer inspection there were two hospital wristbands wrapped around the waist with the words: “Baby of Jasmine BEVERLEY, born on 13/05/22 at 05:04.”

Jasmine gave birth to baby Sunny on May 13, 2022, aged 18 weeks.

She was given ashes by Bush and held a funeral but, two years later, police revealed the heartbreaking twist.



The ashes she had cared for were in fact animal remains.

She told the court in a victim impact statement: “I trusted Rob with the most precious and important person in my life.

“Losing Sunny was the most devastating experience of my life.

“With time, support and the love of my family, I slowly began to rebuild my life and find a way to live alongside that grief.

“It was a long and difficult journey to reach a place where I could function again as a mother, partner and person.”



She turned and addressed Bush directly: “The reality I now live with is that my baby boy Sunny has spent more time in your possession than he ever did with his own family.

“I have to live with the fact that my son was kept for so long without my knowledge, and that when he was eventually found he was in brown paper bag on the floor.

“As a mother, that is something that will stay with me for the rest of my life.”

Hull Crown Court was told how Bush, 48, stockpiled dead bodies and gave their grief-stricken families the ashes belonging to strangers.

He raked in over £3.5million during an 11-year con which targeted hundreds of families at their most vulnerable and has now been jailed for 20 years.



Bush sold non-existent funeral packages, reused “scratched and dented” coffins and even trousered charity whip-rounds.

Profits were prioritised over people and relatives duped “on an almost industrial scale” so he could continue living the high-life.

He discarded and abandoned bodies at his funeral home in the city and left them to rot whilst he jetted abroad on luxury holidays.



His vile scam was eventually exposed by chance whilst he was sunning himself on a luxury holiday in Arizona, US.

He asked another funeral director and his colleague to help one of his staff move a body from a care home.

They agreed but were left stunned when his employee suddenly confessed: “You two don’t know the half of it. Bodies have been there for years.”

The casual worker described the inside as “a horror scene” with cooling units switched off to cut costs and the smell unbearable.

The men accompanied him to the premises to investigate and later flagged down a passing police car to raise the alarm.



Cops ventured inside and found a large number of bodies – including the remains of four unborn babies – on the racks inside a cold storage area.

Bush admitted 30 counts of preventing the lawful and decent burial of a body, fraud by false representation and theft of up to £13,500 donated to 12 charities, including The Salvation Army and Macmillan Cancer Support.

Ahead of his sentencing today, Lucy said she “hopes Bush gets life” but does not think seeing him sentenced will help, adding: “I don’t think mentally I’ll ever be able to recover from this.”

She said she felt “very numb” thinking about Bush, adding: “I’m not a nasty person, I’ve never not liked anybody but I don’t wish him well, I really hope something bad happens to him.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I hope he gets put through torture like what he’s put me and the other families through.



“He’s not a nice person, what he’s done is absolutely disgusting.”

News.title: When is the solar eclipse in August 2026? Date, what time it’s happening in the UK and how to watch
News.content:
SKYWATCHERS are being urged to mark their calendars for what is being billed as the best solar eclipse the UK has seen in decades.

Here is everything you need to know about the once-in-a-lifetime solar spectacle and how to view it safely.



What time will the eclipse happen in the UK?

A deep partial solar eclipse will sweep across the UK on Wednesday, August 12.

Astronomers are calling it the most striking eclipse Britain has witnessed since 1999.



The path of totality passes over northern Russia, the Arctic, Greenland, Iceland, the North Atlantic, large areas of Spain, and also a small corner of north-eastern Portugal.

The path of totality is the narrow track across Earth’s surface where the Moon completely blocks the Sun, briefly plunging observers within it into total darkness.

In the UK, observers will only see a percentage of the sun blotted out, but it will still be the vast majority of its solar disc.

The moon will start to pass the sun at around 6.15pm, with maximum eclipse roughly an hour later between 7.05pm and 7.15pm, and the event finishing just after 8pm.

Exact timings and coverage vary by location.

The BBC‘s Sky at Night Magazine made a handy chart for the eclipse, complete with locations, timings and coverage:



Valencia, Spain – total eclipse – 8.33pm CEST – 100% coverage

Bilbao, Spain – total eclipse – 8.27pm CEST – 100% coverage

Zaragoza, Spain – total eclipse – 8.29pm CEST – 100% coverage

Valladolid, Spain – total eclipse – 8.30pm CEST – 100% coverage

Madrid, Spain – partial eclipse – 8.31pm CEST – 99.97% coverage

Barcelona, Spain – partial eclipse – 8.29pm CEST – 99.8% coverage

Bragança, Portugal – partial eclipse – 7.30pm WEST – 99.9% coverage

Lisbon, Portugal – partial eclipse – 7.36pm WEST – 94.5% coverage

Porto, Portugal – partial eclipse – 7.32pm WEST – 98.2% coverage

London, UK – partial eclipse – 7.13pm BST – 91.3% coverage

Cardiff, UK – partial eclipse – 7.13pm BST – 93% coverage

Edinburgh, UK – partial eclipse – 7.05pm BST – 91% coverage

Belfast, UK – partial eclipse – 7.08pm BST – 93% coverage

Dublin, Ireland – partial eclipse – 7.10pm IST – 94% coverage

New York, NY, USA – partial eclipse – 1.54pm EDT – 9.5% coverage

Boston, MA, USA – partial eclipse – 1.55pm EDT – 16% coverage

Chicago, IL, USA – partial eclipse – 12.28pm CDT – 0.1% coverage

Anchorage, AK, USA – partial eclipse – 8.21am AKDT – 27.9% coverage

St John’s, NL, Canada – partial eclipse – 3.35pm NDT – 53.2% coverage

Montreal, QC, Canada – partial eclipse – 1.45pm EDT – 18% coverage

Winnipeg, MB, Canada – partial eclipse – 12.02pm CDT – 5.4% coverage

Because the eclipse occurs in the evening in the UK, the sun will already be low in the western sky, meaning viewers will need a clear, unobstructed view towards the horizon.

The last time any part of Great Britain saw a comparabe eclipse was March 20, 2015, when areas of Scotland saw as much as 98% of the sun obscured.

Gibraltar, a British Overseas Territory, will see a total eclipse on August 2, 2027.

The next true total solar eclipse visible from the British Isles will not occur until September 23, 2090.

How can I watch it safely?

It is never safe to look directly at the sun during a partial eclipse, even briefly.



Certified eclipse glasses should be worn at all times if you intend to gaze skywards..

They should be checked carefully for scratches, tears or other damage before use, and children should be supervised throughout.

Though they can help protect the naked eye, eclipse glasses must never be used to look through a camera, binoculars or a telescope.

These instruments concentrate sunlight and require their own purpose-made solar filters.

A safer alternative for those without glasses is to view the eclipse indirectly through a pinhole projector, which the Royal Observatory Greenwich says can be made using two pieces of paper, a colander, or even the natural gaps between tree leaves.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Royal Observatory Greenwich will also stream the eclipse for free from 6.15pm via YouTube and Facebook.

Those hoping to make a night of it should also stay up well into the small hours, as the Perseid meteor shower peaks overnight between August 12 and 13, with the best viewing window between midnight and 5.30am.

News.title: Robert Bush sentence - live: Judge jails funeral director who caused 'pain beyond comprehension'
News.content:
Former Legacy funeral director Robert Bush gave bereaved families the wrong ashes and left bodies decomposing in what one relative described as 'the most horrendous horror story'

Vile former undertaker Robert Bush - who gave bereaved families the wrong ashes and left the bodies of 35 people, including a stillborn baby, decomposing - has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Bush, 48, from Otley, West Yorkshire, hung his head low and repeatedly blinked as he listened to the sentencing remarks at Hull Crown Court - but there were no tears or visible signs of emotion.

Judge Mr Justice Hilliard told the sentencing hearing that he has never "known offences affect so many people and so many people so deeply". When he told the court that Bush had shown regret and that it seemed genuine, many victims' families shook their heads. One woman broke down in silent tears.

Outside court, Karen Dry, whose parents' funerals were organised by Bush, called for a public inquiry into how his crimes were possible, saying: "We all deserve dignity in death and this was totally denied to our loved ones."

Bush was sentenced for 67 offences spanning 12 years and affecting hundreds of victims at his business, Legacy Independent Funeral Directors, in Hull. His victims included the mum of a stillborn baby boy, who discovered that her child's remains had been left on a floor for two years.

You can follow live footage of the sentencing here.

News.title: Suffolk wildfire live: Dunwich Heath blaze rages as evacuees told situation 'unstable'
News.content:
A wildfire ravaging Dunwich Heath in Suffolk is still "unstable" according to the local council with the number of firefighters at the scene increasing

A wildfire that has already destroyed a massive area of land in Suffolk and forced scores of people to evacuate remains "unstable" days after it first ignited, the county council has warned.

The blaze at Dunwich Heath has devastated wildlife habitats which could now reportedly take up to 25 years to recover after it went up in flames at about 5pm on Wednesday before engulfing an area equivalent to about 140 football pitches near Sizewell B nuclear power plant.

People evacuated from a local caravan site have now been given a short window to collect their belongings but Peter Langford, emergency planning officer for Suffolk County Council, warned them: "It is still a fast moving situation. From the fire perspective, is still an unstable situation.

"In fact, they've increased a number of pumps back there and they're just about to bring in the helicopter as well." On Thursday afternoon, an EDF spokesperson said the fire was "not affecting operations at Sizewell B power station".

Another wildfire that ignited near Colchester today has now been extinguished after dozens of firefighters rushed to tackle the flames.

News.title: Chancellor John Healey announces date for first Budget under Andy Burnham
News.content:
Chancellor John Healey announces date for first Budget under Andy Burnham

The newly appointed Chancellor, who replaced Rachel Reeves earlier this month, said it will be a Budget that 'moves money and power out of Westminster, and into every postcode around Britain'

View Image Chancellor John Healey with PM Andy Burnham during a recent meeting to No10 North (Image: Christopher Furlong/PA Wire)

John Healey has announced the first Budget under Andy Burnham's premiership will be held on October 28.

‌



The newly appointed Chancellor - who replaced Rachel Reeves earlier this month - said it will be a Budget that "moves money and power out of Westminster, into every postcode around Britain".

‌



The Treasury chief added: "It will be built on fiscal discipline. It will meet our fiscal rules. It’ll give businesses and families some of the stability they need to plan for the future. Now, let’s get on with the job.”

‌



In a video message posted on Friday, Mr Healey, who was one of Mr Burnham's first Cabinet announcements last week, insisted the new government had already provided promised "breathing space" on the cost of living.

During Mr Burnham’s first week in government, the new PM announced an end to VAT on household electricity bills and reintroduced a £2 bus fare cap across England.

Mayors to keep slice of income tax and business rates for local projects in devolution revolution READ MORE :

‌



They also unveiled plans to slash business rates for pubs and small music venues by 20% in a major boost for the struggling sector.

Mr Healey added today: “This government is working fast to restore hope and back Britain’s communities. In the past two weeks, we have begun to kickstart growth in every postcode. We have backed British jobs, British skills and British businesses.

“And we have provided just a bit of breathing-space for those families and businesses that feel so squeezed, that feel without hope.”

Article continues below

But he will face significant challenges to fund public services and further ease the burden on cash-strapped families amid warnings the Iran war will further squeeze the public finances.

Mr Healey, who resigned from Keir Starmer's government as Defence Secretary in June amid a major row with the ex-PM over military spending, must also find £5billion to fund extra spending in the defence investment plan (DIP) announced earlier this month.

He is also yet to set a timetable for reaching 3% of the UK's gross domestic product (GDP) on defending the nation.

News.title: Manchester election results LIVE: By-election set to go to second count as Labour 'confident'
News.content:
Reform council chief threatens to report café owner who gives free meals to hungry kids to police

A café owner who served up free meals to hungry children after food vouchers were removed has been told he will be reported to police by a Reform council leader.

Barry Ashley, who runs the Grumpy Cook in Hastings, stepped up after East Sussex County Council decided not to issue school holiday meal vouchers to struggling families over the summer. He has criticised the move, which he branded “shameless”, accusing the council of turning its back of children in poverty.

He has since been told by Andy Woolley, who heads the authority, that he will be reported to police along with Labour MP Helena Dollimore. Mr Woolley claims to have been personally attacked online and accused the pair of inciting hate and potential violence by naming him in their criticism.

The dispute follows the council's decision not to continue offering the vouchers, which are a lifeline to families. An appalled Mr Ashley responded by announcing he would offer free meals to children who need feeding at his not-for-profit cafe.

A number of local businesses have donated to help, and Mr Ashley told The Mirror he has been providing more than 70 free meals a day. Ms Dollimore has launched a petition calling for the vouchers to be reinstated, branding the council's actions "totally unacceptable" and accusing it of putting children at risk.

Mr Ashley said: "Hastings is one of the poorest towns in the country. And it is by every measure it's a deprived town. One in three of the children are living in poverty.

"And the vouchers, just to take those away without considering what they should be putting in place, without doing any risk assessment, without doing any impact assessment, it's beyond bizarre."

Click here for the full story

News.title: Hundreds gather to remember mum and daughters killed in Great Denham home in moving service
News.content:
Hundreds gather to remember mum and daughters killed in Great Denham home in moving service

Heartfelt tributes were paid to a mum and her two daughters as nearly 500 mourners gathered to remember them following their tragic deaths earlier this month

View 4 Images Nothabo Zandile Tshuma and her daughters Natalie and Nala were remembered at an emotional memorial services (Image: Bedfordshire Police/PA Wire)

Hundreds of people gathered to remember a mum and her two daughters found dead at home in a moving service.

‌



A heartfelt memorial service for Nothabo Zandile Tshuma, 42 and her daughters, Natalie, 15 and Nala, 5, at Bedford's Corn Exchange following their tragic deaths earlier this month was attended by nearly 500 mourners. An inquest, which opened on Tuesday, heard Zandile died from head injuries while Natalie and Nala both died from blunt force head injuries.

‌



Ndodana Mkhanyisi Tshuma, 45, remains in custody in South Africa after being arrested in Johannesburg on suspicion of murdering his wife and two daughters. The memorial service brought together family, friends, colleagues and teachers, who shared memories of the trio and paid tribute to the lives they lived.

‌



View 4 Images Nala's teacher described her hugs as "legendary" (Image: Family Handout )

Zandile’s cousin, Michelle Ncube, told mourners: “Words cannot begin to describe the depth of our loss. We grieve the loss of the future that have been stolen from them and from us.” Remembering her cousin, she said: “She blessed us with her dry wit, her intelligence. She loved gardening. But she didn’t just nurture flowers, she nurtured people.”

Michelle said Zandile had been “completely devoted” to her daughters and that “everything she did was with their future in mind”. A message from Zandile’s sister, who lives in Zimbabwe, was also shared with the congregation. She wrote: “She was more than my sister…sharing a bond through a lifetime of memories. [The loss has] created a void in our hearts and our family that words can hardly describe…life will never be the same without them.”

‌



View 4 Images Natalie was remembered for her love for sports (Image: Family Handout )

Natalie was remembered by Bedford Girls’ School headmistress Gemma Gibson, who said: “When we think of Natalie as a young girl, we picture her smile first…it simply reflected the beautiful person she was. She was a composed and thoughtful pupil who loved learning…but it was her kindness that left the biggest impression.”

Natalie represented the school 107 times in sports including lacrosse, tennis and hockey. Gemma added: “She will forever be loved and remembered by all of us at Bedford Girls’ School.” Nala’s class teacher, Nikki Woodworth, also paid tribute, saying “her hugs were legendary”.

‌



The memorial was organised by Jabu Ncube, who had known Zandile for 20 years after the pair met at university. He said: “How do you find words to confirm something that is unspeakable? How do you find words to comprehend something that is incomprehensible? I have the task of finding the words.” He urged those gathered to: “Remember them as the angels that they are.”

View 4 Images Ndodana Mkhanyisi Tshuma fled the country and was later arrested in Johannesburg (Image: Bedfordshire Police/PA Wire)

Zandile’s colleagues at Forensic Risk Alliance, where she worked in the forensic data analytics team in London, also paid tribute. One colleague, Toby, said she showed “exceptional professionalism…sharp intelligence and a passion for her work with kindness”.

Article continues below

Ndodana Mkhanyisi Tshuma was arrested on an unlicensed firearms charge in Johannesburg on July 10 after fleeing the UK. He appeared in court accused of illegally possessing firearms. South African courts will decide whether a British extradition request meets the legal requirements for his transfer to the UK and The Crown Prosecution Service said it had authorised three murder charges against him.

Funerals for Zandile, Natalie and Nala are due to take place in Zimbabwe next week.

News.title: Anthropic’s AI Claude hacks three organisations after escaping during test
News.content:
Anthropic’s AI Claude hacks three organisations after escaping during test

San Francisco-based Anthropic said its AI Claude found a weakness and connected to the internet to launch cyber attacks on three organisations

View 3 Images Anthropic discovered its Claude AI system had hacked into three organisations on its own (Image: Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images)

A US tech firm revealed its artificial intelligence model hacked into three organisations after escaping an isolated test environment.

‌



Anthropic said AI Claude found a weakness and connected to the internet to launch the cyber attacks. It comes just days after rival OpenAI said that its models had breached the systems of other companies, including AI tools hub Hugging Face.

‌



The announcement prompted Anthropic to check whether its own systems had carried out similar attacks. It says it uncovered three cases which have since been reported to the affected companies. Anthropic, which did not name the organisations, urged other AI labs to perform similar reviews to better understand the risks of their models' capabilities.

‌



View 3 Images Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei founded the company with his sister Daniela Amodei in 2021 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Anthropic said in a statement, it reviewed more than 140,000 tests to find evidence Claude - its family of AI models - had managed to get online even though it was supposed to be in an isolated test environment, cut off from the internet.

The tests included exercises in which Claude was tasked with obtaining "secret" information hidden on another machine on the closed-off network.

‌



It was then told to get the information by breaking into the machine and finding it - a common way that experts assess a model's hacking capabilities. A "misconfiguration" on systems run by Anthropic and its testing partner left the models with live internet access.

View 3 Images Rival tech firm OpenAI said that its models had breached the systems of other companies, including AI tools hub Hugging Face (Image: Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto/REX/Shutterstock)

Treating it all as still part of the same exercise, Claude then connected to the internet and breached the systems of three real organisations rather than just test ones, the San Francisco-based firm said. Anthropic said the earliest incidents date back to April and that it is "approaching the fixes as if the responsibility were ours alone."

‌



Neither Anthropic nor the organisations that were breached had noticed the intrusions at the time. Anthropic said it could have reviewed its records more thoroughly and added that the findings gave the firm "cautious optimism" that such risks can be overcome with more investment and tighter measures.

Prof Gina Neff, head of the Minderoo Centre at the University of Cambridge, said the review showed "AI models doing what people told them to". She said: "The moral of this story is not to fear robots that will take over, but the companies behind powerful AI agents who are making the decisions about what is safe for the rest of us. It also shows why independent testing and government oversight is crucial."

A string of AI-driven cyber-attacks has fuelled calls for tighter safeguards and oversight of the technology, over concerns about the risks posed by increasingly powerful autonomous systems.

Article continues below

US President Donald Trump said this week that Washington is considering measures to rein in AI tools after recent cybersecurity incidents.

OpenAI has taken responsibility for at least two hacking incidents involving its platforms breaching the rules of what they were directed to do.

News.title: Crete wildfires live: Greece emergency as hurricane-force winds fan Rethymno flames
News.content:
A state of emergency has been declared in parts of Crete and elsewhere in Greece as firefighters battle intense wildfires, with hurricane-force winds fanning flames

A state of emergency has been declared in parts of Crete and elsewhere in Greece as firefighters battle intense wildfires.

The blazes in the Rethymno region of southern Crete have scorched around 4,500 hectares since Wednesday. Hurricane-force winds - which reached speeds of up to 125km/h (78mph) yesterday - grounded firefighting aircraft and hampered efforts to contain the flames. Firefighters resumed operations on the ground today without the use of aircraft for the third day in a row.

Thousands of people, including tourists, have been evacuated with fires are also raging on Paros, Andros and Kalymnos islands, parts of the Peloponnese and western mainland Greece.

Advice has been issued by the UK Government for Brits caught in areas affected, stating: "Be cautious if you are in or near an area affected by wildfires: follow @112Greece for official updates; follow the guidance of the emergency services; call the Greek emergency services on 112 if you are in immediate danger; contact your airline or travel operator who can assist you with return travel to the UK."

Fresh wildfire outbreaks in Greece, Portugal and Turkey come on top of devastating wildfires that are tearing through parts of France and Spain. Since yesterday, firefighters have responded to 169 wildfires across Turkey.

News.title: Urgent warning as man who 'could be contagious' vanishes from Preston hospital
News.content:
Urgent warning as man who 'could be contagious' vanishes from Preston hospital

Dean Hesketh has not been seen since leaving the Royal Preston Hospital and there is increasing concern for him with people told not to approach.

View Image An image from CCTV footage of Mr Hesketh (Image: Lancashire Police)

Police have launched an urgent appeal to help find a missing man who may have a "contagious health condition".

‌



Dean Hesketh is understood to have not been seen since leaving the Royal Preston Hospital at around 11.15am on Tuesday and police say there is increasing concern for him.

‌



The 51-year old also uses the names Tim, Dean or Anthony Gledhill and anyone who sees him is urged to get in touch with police to "make sure he is safe".

‌



Blackpool Police says that he has links to Preston, Penwortham and Blackpool but it adds for people not to approach him due to the possibility of him having a "contagious" condition.

Poland scrambles fighter jets to intercept Russian spy plane near NATO airspace READ MORE :

Mr Hesketh is described as being 5ft 4in with black hair and blue eyes and is of a slim build.

‌



In the last sighting of him, which can be seen in the image released by police, he was wearing a khaki green and black jacket, black trainers and a Lyle and Scott jumper. He was also wearing a blue surgical face mask.

The appeal from Blackpool Police on Facebook read: "We’re asking for your help to find Dean Hesketh, who is missing. Dean, 51, also uses the names Tim, Dean or Anthony Gledhill. He was last seen leaving Royal Preston Hospital at 11:16am on 28th July. Enquiries to locate Dean are ongoing, and we are growing increasingly concerned for him.

"Dean is 5ft 4in with black hair and blue eyes and is of a slim build. He was last seen wearing the clothing you can see him in in this footage – a khaki green and black jacket, black trainers and a Lyle and Scott jumper. He was also wearing a blue surgical face mask. Dean has links to Preston, Penwortham and Blackpool.

Article continues below

"We ask that if you see Dean you don’t approach him, as he may have a contagious health condition. If you do see Dean it’s really important that you get in touch with us on 999 as soon as you can, so that we can make sure he is safe. If you have information or footage that could help us find him please call 101 quoting log 1051 of 28th July."

News.title: Burnham says Infantino 'wrong man' to lead Fifa as third confederation opposes World Cup plan
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Gianni Infantino was "the wrong man" to lead Fifa after a senior adviser to the president resigned and a third confederation opposed his plan to sell stakes in competitions to private investors.

Burnham was critical of the proposal when it was first announced, and told reporters on Friday: "This was an outrageous suggestion.

"The idea that it could even be brought forward shows that, in my view, [he] is the wrong man to lead the organisation."

Burnham was speaking hours after the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) said it "stands in solidarity" with counterparts in Europe and North, Central America and the Caribbean.

The AFC added Infantino's plan could not "realistically achieve the necessary broad consensus and unity required to move forward".

"The Fifa World Cup is the pinnacle of global football and derives its strength from the participation of all Confederations and the world's leading football nations," it said.

"Any proposal that risks undermining the unity and universal character of the competition must be reconsidered."

Shortly after that statement, Carlos Cordeiro - Infantino's senior adviser on global strategy and governance - resigned, saying the proposal was "a bad deal for football" and would "mortgage football's future".

The AFC's statement means Infantino's plans are unlikely to be approved by Fifa members if put to a vote.

Infantino had indicated the proposals would need a straight majority to go through - meaning 106 of its 211 members needed to vote in favour for the proposal.

Uefa - the body that governs European football - has 55 votes. Concacaf, which oversees football in North, Central America and the Caribbean, has 35 and Asia has 46.

Should all member associations back the stance of their governing body, that would mean 136 nations are against Infantino's plan.

News.title: England and Wales on course for driest July on record
News.content:
England and Wales are on course for their driest July since records began 190 years ago.

The Met Office reports that England has seen just 5.6mm of rainfall up to 30 July â just 8% of its long-term meteorological average for the month and less than half of the previous record of 13.4mm set in 1911.

For Wales it is 7.9mm of rainfall, also 8% of its long-term average for the month and almost a third of the previous record of 22.6mm, again set in 1911.

The UK as a whole is currently on track for its third driest July, and driest nationally since 1868.

News.title: Southport killer charged with prison attacks and possessing weapon
News.content:
Southport killer Axel Rudakubana has been charged with three attacks while in prison and possessing a weapon.

Police say the offences took place at HMP Belmarsh over six months from May to October 2025.

The 19-year-old murdered Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven, Bebe King, six, and Alice da Silva Aguiar, nine, and injured eight other children and two adults in an attack at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class in July 2024.

He was given a 52-year sentence in January 2025. Earlier this month he was moved to a secure psychiatric hospital.

Rudakubana is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court remotely on 11 September.

He has been charged with the following four offences:

Assault on an emergency worker on 6 May 2025

Attempted grievous bodily harm on 8 May 2025

Unauthorised possession of an offensive weapon in prison on 26 June 2025

Assault on an emergency worker on 28 October 2025

In May 2025, it was reported boiling water had been thrown on a prison officer at Belmarsh. They were taken to hospital and discharged on the same day.

When Rudakubana was jailed, the judge was unable to impose a whole life order due to him being under-18 when he carried out the attack. He will likely never be released.

On 23 July, the MoJ confirmed Rudakubana was transferred from HMP Belmarsh to Broadmoor, a high-security psychiatric hospital in Berkshire.

Under the Mental Health Act, the MoJ is likely to have had no choice but to accept doctors' recommendations about whether Rudakubana could be held safely in prison.

The decision to transfer him was criticised by a lawyer representing the families of victims.

News.title: Passenger on British Airways mayday flight describes fear and shout of 'I don't want to die'
News.content:
A passenger on a British Airways flight that issued a distress call on approach to Heathrow Airport earlier this month has described the rising fear in the cabin and a lack of information from the crew.

Edward Killiwick had been travelling back from a friend's birthday party with his partner Julie, on the flight from Dusseldorf in Germany on 6 July.

He said passengers were told that the landing had been aborted, and then he felt a "very violent manoeuvre" and "did think we could crash". He and his partner had to comfort a woman who "completely lost it and started screaming, 'I don't want to die'".

The flight landed safely, but the incident is being investigated with assistance from BA.

The UK's Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) said it was "investigating a serious incident", and France's accident investigation authority, the BEA, said on Wednesday that the plane, an Airbus A320, had issued a distress call.

Edward said: "The violent manoeuvre almost felt like it was avoiding another aircraft. You could feel the engines going at full power.

"It was a bit odd going around in a holding pattern with no information. I thought if they're not talking, then they're not in a good place."

He said they were in a holding pattern for about 15 minutes.

The BEA said that as the plane approached Heathrow, there was a data system failure which triggered a stall warning.

The crew then flew the aircraft in a different mode called "alternate law", which removes some automated flight protection systems. Another stall warning then occurred at 3,000 feet â which experts say was likely to have been just miles away from the airport.

The urgency call the crew had already made was upgraded to mayday, indicating imminent danger.

A British Airways spokesperson said the airline was assisting the AAIB with its investigation and was not legally able to comment further at this stage.

Edward said: "I was definitely scared. After the violent manoeuvre I thought, there is definitely something very badly wrong here. I did think we could crash.

"I did think it was a possibility, and I think everyone else did."

News.title: Sainsbury's agrees to sell Argos for £120m
News.content:
Sainsbury's has agreed to sell Argos for Â£120m after a long process of trying to offload it as the supermarket chain aims to focus on its main food business.

Sainsbury's said it would be "business as usual" for Argos customers, staff, and suppliers. Shoppers will see no change as Argos will still operate in Sainsbury's shops, sell Habitat products, and offer Nectar points.

The buyer, Swift Partners, is a company that has been created to buy the brand and includes former Co-operative Group boss Richard Pennycook.

There are 667 Argos shops across the UK, with 201 operating as standalone stores and 466 operating within Sainsbury's. It also has more than 450 collection points.

Founded in 1973, Argos opened shops where customers browsed its catalogues and placed their orders, with products being delivered to tills from warehouses connected to the stores.

The Argos catalogue, once described by comedian Bill Bailey as the "laminated book of dreams", used to be a physical book.

Argos no longer prints this hefty tome, with its full range now available online instead. In store, customers can browse the product collection on tablet computers.

Sainsbury's has been trying to sell Argos - which has been seen as an underperforming brand - for some time.

Sainsbury's bought Argos â together with Habitat and all the other retail brands owned by Home Retail Group â in 2016 for Â£1.4bn. It then sold Argos financial services, which runs the Argos card, for around Â£720m in 2024.

In September last year, its talks to sell the rest of Argos to Chinese online retailer JD.com fell through.

Sainsbury's chief executive Simon Roberts said that all of Argos's nearly 14,000 staff would be transferred over to Swift Partners as part of the deal.

He also confirmed that Argos would continue to operate in Sainsbury's shops; Nectar will continue to be used across both Argos and Sainsbury's; and Sainsbury's will continue to sell Habitat products

Swift Partners' Pennycook said he believed "strongly in Argos's future and see real opportunities to invest and build on its progress".

The deal is expected to be completed in February next year.

Pennycook said there was the potential to open new standalone Argos shops â and did not rule out the possibility of the return of its print catalogue.

News.title: Healey announces his first Budget will be on 28 October
News.content:
Chancellor John Healey has announced the date of his first Budget will be Wednesday, 28 October.

In aâ¯video message,â¯ he said: "This will be a Budget that moves money and power out of Westminster, and into every postcode around Britain.

"It will be built on fiscal discipline. It will meet our fiscal rules. It'll give businesses and families some of the stability they need to plan for the future. Now, let's get on with the job."

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said his government will stick to Labour's fiscal rules on spending and borrowing as well as the party's 2024 manifesto pledges not to increase income tax, VAT or national insurance contributions.

News.title: Glasgow gets starring role in Spider-Man: Brand New Day film
News.content:
Any comic book fan knows that Spider-Man's secret identity is Peter Parker, a science nerd who gained superhero powers after being bitten by a radioactive spider.

But in the latest installment from the Marvel cinematic universe, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Parker - played by Tom Holland - is not the only star in disguise.

The action takes place in New York City but much of the movie, which premiered in London this week, was filmed more than 3,000 miles away in Glasgow.

Filming almost brought the city centre to a halt last summer, when fans gathered to watch Holland in an action sequence in full superhero mode.

Parts of the nearby Merchant City were also dressed up to resemble the Big Apple.

It was the latest in a long line of Hollywood blockbusters to have been filmed in the city in recent years.

And next month Glasgow is expected to double as Gotham City, when filming starts on the sequel to The Batman.

Screen Scotland said the Victorian architecture, wide avenues and grid layout make it an "incredibly versatile stand-in" for many US cities.

News.title: Disgraced funeral boss who failed to bury bodies jailed
News.content:
A funeral director who failed to bury or cremate people and gave bereaved relatives the ashes of strangers has been jailed for 20 years.

Some 35 bodies and more than 100 sets of ashes were found by police raiding Legacy Independent Funeral Directors in Hull in March 2024.

Former undertaker Robert Bush admitted 67 offences, including denying 30 people a decent and proper burial, theft from 12 charities, and fraudulent trading over a period of 12 years.

Sentencing him at Hull Crown Court, Judge Justice Hilliard told the former undertaker he had "caused anguish and pain on a scale beyond comprehension".

This story contains details some might find distressing.

The court heard Bush defrauded nearly 200 families out of Â£500,000 and had acted out of "financial greed".

Hilliard warned that no-one who had used Legacy's cremations services "at any time can be absolutely certain they received the ashes of their loved one".

"He must have a heartless side to him - which allowed him to treat the living and the dead in the way he did, and he was very confident he would get away with what he was doing."

The judge added: "I don't think I have ever known offences affecting so many people and so deeply."

News.title: Andy Burnham to give regional mayors share of income tax
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham will give all mayors of city regions in England a share of income tax revenue for the first time, as part of his drive to transfer power from Westminster to local leaders.

Burnham will also allow English strategic authorities to keep some cash from business rates collected in their areas, and gain greater control over services such as housing, transport, skills.

The government has not yet decided the exact portion of taxes mayors will get, with more details to be announced when Chancellor John Healey delivers his first budget in the autumn.

Opposition parties said the plans lacked detail and could lead to areas with weaker economies losing out on funding.

But Burnham said the move would "make good" on his pledge to "bring power home" to "every postcode in the country".

"Under our plans, more of the taxes raised in a community will stay in that community," the prime minister added.

First Secretary of State Louise Haigh told BBC Radio 4's Today programme areas without mayors would also benefit from investment because devolution powers would be held by new strategic authorities across England.

Strategic authorities bring together local councils to control regional issues such as transport and economic development, with decisions taken collectively by council leaders rather than a single elected mayor.

But Labour backbencher Perran Moon said the government's plans were "discriminatory" and could create a "two-tier system".

The MP for Camborne and Redruth in Cornwall said the area would never have a mayor or become a combined authority and so risked not having access to devolved powers that other areas would have.

"What we're asking government to do is to provide us with the same powers, the same funding that mayoral combined authorities have without the requirement of becoming a combined authority or having a mayor."

The government has also announced that mayors will be given a fast-track route to building new tramways, roads and light rail in their areas.

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said the threshold at which local leaders need to seek approval for projects will rise to Â£500m, up from Â£200m.

News.title: Thames Water boss says leakage targets 'not realistic'
News.content:
Water companies have performance commitments on issues such as leakage.

It is illegal to release raw sewage into rivers and seas during "normal" weather conditions, but firms are allowed to do so when it rains heavily, to prevent homes being flooded.

Thames is the UK's largest water company, supplying water and wastewater services to 16 million customers across London and parts of southern England.

Speaking to the BBC's Big Boss Interview podcast, Weston said the company treats 4.3 billion litres of waste a day, and "99.5% of the time" it gets treated successfully, although "sometimes something goes wrong".

"We want to do better when it comes to pollutions," he said, but added, "the targets that the company is expected to make are not realistic.

"[For example], we have to hit a certain level of leakage, but it is so far in excess of what we are capable of doing, I think anyone would be capable of doing, however much money you invested, that it is not going to be achievable."

The chance of getting to zero pollution was "very, very slim", he added.

Ofwat told the BBC: "With around a fifth of water put into supply still lost through leakage, companies must deliver on the commitments they have been funded to achieve.

"Water company targets are intended to be ambitious and drive better outcomes for customers and the environment."

A spokesperson for the Environment Agency said: "[We] and the public expect Thames Water to comply with the law," adding that the agency would continue to hold companies to account where performance falls short.

James Wallace, chief executive of campaign group River Action, said: "Thames Water's tactics of opacity and deflection fool no-one. Telling the public to save water while this wasteful profit-obsessed corporation leaks 570 million litres of treated drinking water every day is offensive.

"There is nothing 'realistic' about accepting sewage pollution as inevitable. The choice is simple: keep propping up a failed privatised financial model, or put Thames Water into special administration and rebuild it as a public utility serving customers, rivers and the public."

News.title: High Court upholds decision to allow Chinese mega embassy
News.content:
A High Court challenge against the construction of a Chinese mega embassy in London has failed.

The decision to uphold planning permission for the site on the old Royal Mint, near the Tower of London, has dismayed campaigners from the Royal Mint Court Residents' Association (RMCRA), which represents families and businesses in about 100 properties.

The RMCRA fear the site poses an espionage threat and will be used to enforce "draconian" Chinese laws in the UK and to target dissidents.

The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) and the London Borough of Tower Hamlets defended the claim, saying they "conscientiously and carefully had regard" to the residents' concerns.

The association was also concerned about the Chinese government creating a fire risk by ignoring safety obligations, which it said would not be enforceable because of diplomatic immunity.

A High Court hearing was held earlier this month and two judges have now dismissed RMCRA's challenge.

Mrs Justice Lieven, sitting with Lord Justice Dingemans, said there was "no doubt" that the government took into account that it was the Chinese government applying for planning permission.

She also said that the RMCRA was not disadvantaged by not receiving a copy of a "blast assessment" at the time of the planning decision, which detailed the effect of a possible terrorist explosion.

The judge said: "There was no unfairness to the claimant by reason of these documents not having been disclosed."

Speaking outside Parliament, Luke de Pulford of the Interparliamentary Alliance on China (IPAC), who has been supporting the RMCRA, confirmed solicitors had been instructed to appeal against the High Court ruling, funded by donations from the public.

RMCRA spokesman Mark Nygate said residents believed this was only an early skirmish in the battle against the mega embassy.

"We knew this was going to be a long haul and we intend to go all the way... as far as the Supreme Court," he said.

"This is a huge case with consequences that go far beyond planning law, far beyond the residents, far from the local community - this is about our country."

News.title: British man accused of spying on Cyprus RAF base for Iran
News.content:
A British man has been arrested on suspicion of spying on a UK military base in Cyprus on behalf of the Iranian military.

Rashad Sultanov, 44, of Islington, north London, is accused of carrying out "hostile surveillance" on RAF Akrotiri and sharing information with the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps.

Sultanov, who also holds Azerbaijani citizenship, was arrested by Cypriot police on 17 July and is in custody pending extradition proceedings.

The Crown Prosecution Service has said he will be charged under the National Security Act - the first time an alleged offence under the 2023 law has been investigated in an overseas territory.

News.title: BP puts North Sea business up for sale
News.content:
BP has said it is putting its North Sea business up for sale in a move that would end 60 years of production in the region by the oil giant.

The decision follows a review of BP's operations as it seeks to slim down the group. Its North Sea business has five production hubs - two in the central North Sea and three west of Shetland - and employs about 1,100 people.

Earlier this week, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he told US President Donald Trump he would take a "pragmatic approach" to the issue of North Sea oil and gas.

Trump, some trade unions, industry figures and some Labour MPs all back increased drilling in the North Sea.

"The UK has been our home for more than 100 years and will continue to play an important role in our future," BP chief executive Meg O'Neill said.

"We're proud of the jobs we create, the contribution we make to the UK economy, and the work we do to keep energy flowing every day," she said.

The company said it remained committed to operating the business safely and reliably throughout the sale process.

Its North Sea business produced 117,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2025, a small fraction of the oil giant's 2.3 million barrels of daily production.

O'Neill, who took the helm at BP in April, said earlier this year there was "untapped potential" in the North Sea.

However, in announcing Friday's decision she said: "As we focus our portfolio and direct capital to our highest-value opportunities, we believe our North Sea business will be better positioned as part of another company.

"It has world-class people, resilient assets and a proud heritage, and it is precisely these qualities that can attract an owner ready to back its next chapter. We are seeking an outcome that recognizes that value."

The sale could potentially bring in Â£2bn to BP. Last month, the FT reported the company was in talks with Ithaca Energy to sell its North Sea assets for around this amount, although the talks fell through.

BP employs around 13,960 people in the UK. Its global headquarters will remain in the UK.

News.title: TikToker faces police probe over secret filming using 'smart glasses'
News.content:
One of the most disturbing incidents occurs on Skye where he tells a UK-born Sikh shopkeeper of Indian heritage that there is "forced" diversity in Europe.

He goes on to refer to the Kalergi Plan - a far right conspiracy theory about a plot to "breed out the white race".

The woman, who was running the shop with help from her teenage daughter, politely suggests his comments are "slightly derogatory".

When he leaves, Margerison angrily describes her in his video commentary as "condescending" and complains that "they don't understand".

The woman, who was born in London and has lived in Skye for 20 years, told BBC Scotland News he initiated the conversation by asking "what are you doing here?" but edited this out of the published footage.

She said her encounter with Margerison, who is heavily built and well over 6ft tall, was "100% intimidating" and that she cried when she was later told by a friend that a secretly-filmed video had been published on TikTok.

"You're made to feel very small when you see a video like this," she said.

"And it's sad because everyone in the local community is really nice. This was really upsetting."

While in the Hebrides, Margerison also filmed an angry encounter with an elderly couple in a supermarket after they complained that he had "loudly and rudely" asked them to move out of his way.

He follows them around the store, at one point blocking their path, swears in front of them, accuses them of being "mental".

He also tells them he intends to post footage of them on TikTok which he says is "well within my rights".

News.title: Elderly victim of 'cruel' carer can't be left alone after being 'traumatised'
News.content:
An 81-year-old whose "cruel" carer was jailed after being caught on camera abusing her cannot be left alone because she is "traumatised," her daughter has said.

Louise Harris was given a three-month sentence after CCTV filmed her drunkenly screaming "I hope you die in your sleep... you horrible cow" at Elizabeth Anne Shipton in Pontardawe, Neath Port Talbot.

Elizabeth's daughter Tracy Faram Shipton called Harris's actions "horrific" and said her sentence for ill treatment and criminal damage was "laughable".

Despite this, the family is unable to appeal against it as, under the unduly lenient sentence scheme, external, the attorney general can only refer specific qualifying crimes to the Court of Appeal.

Harris, 42, was filmed on the family's video surveillance system, which was originally installed so Tracy and her brother could monitor their late father John in case he fell while caring for Elizabeth.

She had originally been charged with attempted robbery - a crime which would have qualified for sentencing to be appealed by the victim's family - but the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) dropped that charge.

"Mum can't be left on her own at all now," Tracy added.

A CPS spokesman said: "We keep all cases under review and on this occasion concluded that our legal test was not met, as there was insufficient evidence to prosecute the defendant with attempted robbery and theft.

"We have written to the victim to explain our decision in more detail."
