A defunct SpaceX rocket is set to collide with the moon this Wednesday, more than a year after it launched a pair of lunar landers.

The impact is expected to carve out a new crater and send a plume of dust and rubble into space, an event scientists and skygazers are keen to observe.

Space tracking expert Bill Gray estimates the rocket's upper stage will strike the lunar surface at an astonishing 5,400 mph (8,700 kph) – seven times the speed of sound – near the Einstein Crater on the moon’s sunlit western limb.

While the action unfolds in the early hours, observers in the eastern parts of the U.S. and Canada, along with much of South America, are anticipated to have the best views. The impact is expected to unleash energy equivalent to three tons of TNT.

Though this particular piece of space junk is not causing significant alarm, its trajectory underscores a growing concern about the increasing amount of debris in Earth's orbit and beyond.

open image in gallery A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifts off from pad 39A with a payload of a pair of lunar landers at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Fla., Jan. 15, 2025 ( AP Photo/John Raoux )

"Things are getting crowded up there," noted Gray, who plans to monitor the aftermath from New Brunswick, Canada. This incident marks only the second known accidental rocket crash into the moon, following a Chinese rocket segment that created craters on the lunar far side in 2022.

The collision, fortunately occurring on the moon’s near side, offers a unique opportunity for scientific study. While the initial impact flash will likely be too dim and brief to observe, the resulting stream of ejected material could extend for several miles and remain visible through telescopes for tens of minutes.

Benjamin Fernando of Los Alamos National Laboratory highlighted the unique lunar environment: "The gravity on the moon is low and there is no wind to blow the dust away."

He added that understanding such events is crucial for assessing "how much of a hazard debris impacts pose to future astronauts." Fernando predicts the impact will create a crater approximately 90 feet across and 16 feet deep, too small for Earth-based observation but detectable by spacecraft.

NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and South Korea’s Danuri lunar orbiter are poised to capture before-and-after images of the crash site. Danuri is expected to pass within a mile or two of the SpaceX rocket just two minutes prior to impact, according to Fernando and his team.

The abandoned rocket segment, measuring about 40 feet and weighing around 10,000 pounds, originally launched two private lunar landers on January 15, 2025. One, Firefly Aerospace’s Blue Ghost, achieved a successful lunar touchdown, while the other, from Japan-based ispace, unfortunately failed.

Scientists emphasize that observing well-tracked strikes by human-made objects provides invaluable data, unlike unpredictable meteoroid impacts. NASA intentionally crashed rocket sections and lunar modules during the Apollo era for seismic measurements, and in 2009, its LCROSS spacecraft was deliberately crashed to search for ice.

With the moon becoming a new frontier for exploration, experts stress the importance of improving debris monitoring and traffic control before more robots and astronauts arrive. The United States and China are currently in a race to land astronauts on the moon in the coming years, with companies like Elon Musk’s SpaceX and Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin competing to provide landers for NASA's future Artemis IV missions.

Retired astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell offered a pragmatic view, stating in an email, "This impact will not be a problem."

However, he cautioned, "But in a future where there are long-term bases on the moon, similar impacts would be an issue and we need not to leave rocket stages in chaotic orbits of this kind."

Gianni Infantino’s position as Fifa president is growing untenable as regional governing bodies continue to officially reject his plan to sell-off stakes of the World Cup to private investors.

Uefa’s 55 member associations insisted they would not participate in any Fifa tournament until plans for the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) were withdrawn and have confirmed that they will even boycott the next World Cup should they go through. Football Supporters Europe responded to this by posting “#InfantinOUT”.

Concacaf, the governing body for North America and the Caribbean, reiterated their own concerns over the lack of consultation and rejected the proposal, as did the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) who called for an “urgent review of its governance” at Fifa - piling more pressure on Infantino.

Fifa has so far refused to back down, insisting that “nobody is selling football” while asserting that their consultation process was “disrupted by incorrect media reports”, a move that felt like it was right out of the Donald Trump playbook.

But as once-loyal strongholds begin to turn on him less than a year out from the next Fifa presidential election in March 2027, could this be the end of Infantino?

Here are six candidates that could challenge Infantino for Fifa’s presidency:

Alexander Ceferin

open image in gallery Uefa president Alexander Ceferin has been a rival of Gianni Infantino over key issues ( PA Wire )

Calls are growing from Uefa member associations to back a candidate to run against Infantino, and the European governing body’s president Ceferin appears the most qualified.

A rival of Infantino, Ceferin most recently no-showed the World Cup 2026 final after the tournament was plagued by controversy, most notably the suspension of Folarin Balogun’s red card ban following a “review” request from Trump, which Uefa said “crossed a red line”.

The Slovenian lawyer has been incumbent since 2016 but is reportedly keen to continue in his current role. He had initially ruled out standing for a third term next spring, at least until 3031, but is now willing to seek re-election if no other candidates step forward.

As things stand, it appears he is not eager to challenge Infantino for Fifa’s presidency, which has led Uefa members to look elsewhere.

Nasser Al-Khelaifi

open image in gallery Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi ( Getty Images )

The Independent understands that Paris Saint-Germain president Al-Khelaifi is currently being mooted as a challenger to Infantino.

Al-Khelaifi, whose primary role is chairman of Qatar Sports Investment, holds many senior positions within the game. After the collapse of the doomed European Super League, he was elevated to the top of the game’s main club body, European Football Clubs, which expressed “serious concern” about Infantino’s sell-off plan.

It’s reported by talkSPORT that multiple Uefa federations, including Belgium and Poland, would back Al-Kehaifi, who sees him as having the best chance of toppling Infantino at next year’s presidential election.

However, Al-Khelaifi would need serious persuading to stand as he currently holds no ambition to run for office.

A representative for Al-Khelaifi said, via Politico: “Nasser has absolutely no ambition, no intention, no interest in the Fifa role, and he will continue to discreetly support all the institutions of world and European football.”

Dariusz Mioduski

Uefa members are also exploring the possibility of backing Legia Warsaw owner Mioduski.

The Polish lawyer has been mooted by senior federation officials within Bosnia and Herzegovina, Norway, Sweden, Germany and Spain, according to talkSPORT.

But as of now, he would not be the preferred candidate in his homeland, with Poland’s FA keen on Al-Khelaifi.

Victor Montagliani

open image in gallery Concacaf president Victor Montagliani has well-known aspirations to head up Fifa ( Getty Images )

Away from Uefa, Concacaf president Montagliani has been rumoured as a potential successor to Infantino, with his ambitions to one day become Fifa president well known.

The Canadian was unanimously re-elected to lead the confederation in 2023 and his current term is set to end in 2027. His primary focus thus far has been to seek re-election again next year.

But according to The i, Montagliani is “making moves” towards expediting his aspirations and challenging Infantino for Fifa’s presidency in next March’s election.

Montagliani’s Concacaf followed Uefa’s suit in coming together to staunchly reject Fifa’s proposal, but did not go far as to threaten a boycott.

Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa

open image in gallery Infantino (right) speaks to Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa ( Getty )

The AFC has also outwardly opposed Infantino’s plans in a heavy blow for the incumbent Fifa president, losing the support of what was once a loyal stronghold of the Swiss-Italian.

AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, a Bahraini football administrator who is also senior vice-president of the Fifa Council, branded Fifa’s lack of consultation with its members as “totally unacceptable” in a letter to the regional body’s 47 member federations on Thursday, a day before the confederation came together to reject the proposal.

That subsequent statement notably called for “an urgent review of its governance” to pile more pressure on Infantino. That begs the question: could Sheikh Salman be a potential challenger?

His term as AFC president comes to an end in 2027.

Arsene Wenger

open image in gallery Arsene Wenger is Fifa’s Chief of Global Football Development ( Reuters )

Now this one is a bit of a long shot, but it might be one to watch.

Legendary former Arsenal boss Arsene Wenger has become increasingly engrained in the political side of the game in his role as Fifa’s Chief of Global Football Development.

He’s not been scared to try and push through radical change in the past, with his “daylight offside rule” going on trial in Canada earlier this year.

And with some fans now expressing their dismay at his close association with Infantino and therefore this World Cup proposal, could Wenger stand up against the Fifa president to ensure his reputation isn’t sullied?

News.title: World Cup boycott latest: Infantino’s senior adviser quits after Fifa refuses to back down over Uefa protest
News.content:
Inside Uefa’s extraordinary World Cup boycott plans – and what Fifa might do next

Gianni Infantino is under mounting pressure from football federations as well as from within Fifa after Uefa’s boycott of the World Cup left his plans to privatise its tournaments in tatters.

Infantino’s long-term adviser Carlos Cordeiro, a key figure within Fifa, has quit in protest of Infantino’s proposals, while the Asian Football Confederation has become the third federation to reject them publicly, releasing a strong statement on Friday backing the stance of Uefa and Concacaf, while claiming that confidence in Fifa’s governance has been “undermined”.

It comes after Fifa hit back at Uefa, insisting that “nobody is selling football” and confirming that it will continue its consultation period ahead of a vote on 19 September. But after another federation joined Uefa’s side, Infantino looks unlikely to get the votes he needs and is instead facing growing opposition to his leadership.

On Thursday, Uefa announced that it would boycott the World Cup and all Fifa competitions if Infantino’s controversial plans to sell off stakes in its major tournaments to external investors are voted through.

“Uefa and its 55 member associations stand as one,” a statement said following an emergency Uefa meeting. “We unanimously and unequivocally reject Fifa’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other Fifa competitions to private investors.”

Chelsea have been fined £10m and given a suspended two-window transfer ban by an independent appeal board after admitting breaches of Football Association agent rules, the FA has announced.

The Blues were charged last September with 74 alleged breaches of the FA’s rules around agent regulations, dealing with intermediaries on transfers, and third-party investments in players. They primarily related to the seasons between 2010/11 to 2015/16, which came under the ownership of Roman Abramovich.

Chelsea self-reported the breaches after the change of ownership in 2022 and referred themselves to the FA. The club admitted to all 74 breaches but an independent regulatory commission imposed a six-point deduction, suspended until 2027, as well as a £10m fine.

Chelsea successfully appealed against the six-point penalty, which was instead replaced by the suspended two-window transfer ban. The club said on Friday that it welcomed the FA’s verdict, although the FA will continue to investigate “individual misconduct arising out of this case”.

A club statement said: “Chelsea Football Club is pleased to confirm that a final decision has been reached by The FA’s judicial bodies in relation to historical regulatory matters that were self-reported by the club.

“In 2022, the club self-reported potential historical rule breaches to all applicable regulators. Following that report, it has worked openly and transparently with all regulators, including voluntarily and proactively disclosing many thousands of documents.

“As previously announced, settlement agreements have been entered into with Uefa and the Premier League concerning the same self-reported regulatory matters and topics that have been addressed before.

“The club is pleased to confirm that, now The FA process has concluded, this brings all regulatory proceedings against the club to a close. We are grateful to Uefa, the Premier League and The FA for their engagement with the club throughout these processes.”

More follows

In the aftermath of the World Cup, despite the many issues that had plagued the tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada, Gianni Infantino spoke in tones that suggested he felt invincible. By delivering record revenues and the “most outstanding” World Cup ever, the Fifa president felt emboldened enough to embark on a victory lap, admonishing his critics from within the stronghold of his Fifa palace, while safe in the knowledge that the structures and mechanisms designed to keep him in power were secure.

Barely a week later, the walls around Infantino are crumbling before our eyes. In over-playing his hand and rushing through proposals to sell stakes in the World Cup and Fifa tournaments to private investors, Infantino has crossed a line from where there may not return. Uefa’s extraordinary decision to boycott the World Cup should Infantino get his way has been followed by two more federations, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf, rejecting his proposals. Uefa now has enough support to comfortably defeat Infantino if a vote of Fifa’s 211 member associations goes ahead next month.

open image in gallery The walls around Gianni Infantino are crumbling ( Getty )

Whether Infantino’s plans, understood by The Independent to have been in the works for over a year, even survive for that long is another matter. Infantino is also under mounting pressure from within Fifa itself. The president’s long-time adviser, Carlos Cordeiro, described as a heavyweight figure within the organisation, resigned in protest on Friday. “Football has been central to my life, and after more than 35 years in banking, I understand both the value of this asset and the consequences of giving part of it away,” he said in a statement. “That is why this proposal should be rejected.” If even the Fifa suits have seen enough, it tells you that Infantino has gone too far.

In their own statement in the early hours of Friday morning, Fifa provided some “clarifications” around their private investment proposals, insisting that their “planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports”. But it may not stop some of Infantino’s steadfast allies from switching sides. Asia will host the 2034 World Cup in Saudi Arabia and parts of the region have benefitted greatly from Infantino’s support since the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, but the AFC’s president, Shaikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa of Bahrain, has been Infantino’s most vocal critic outside of Europe. A withering statement on Friday accused Fifa of “undermining” the World Cup and called for an “urgent review” into its governance.

The AFC said it stands in “solidarity” with Uefa, while Concacaf (The Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football) also confirmed that it had “rejected the proposals” following their own emergency meeting. The Independent also understands that the vast majority of Concacaf’s 41 members have lost confidence in Infantino’s presidency. That is to be admired, as Infantino’s ploy of offering countries $40m for backing his proposals, or risk receiving only $10m for rejecting them were aimed at smaller nations who would have benefitted greatly from the windfall, an additional pot of gold to clear debts and fund overdue infrastructure projects. Infantino attempted to target those vulnerabilities but he has come up against organised, united opposition.

With Uefa, the AFC and Concacaf aligned, a voting bloc of around 150 member associations would comfortably defeat Infantino’s proposals, even if a few countries from those federations went against the whip. For Infantino, an embarrassing defeat appears inevitable. Further opposition from the confederations of South America and Africa, who have yet to publicly take a stance either way, would surely make his position untenable and spell the end of his presidency. Even so, it is already beyond clear that Infantino must go: a president who places his political interests and the financial incentives of private investors – within Donald Trump’s own family – above the sport is no leader. As Uefa said: “This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of Fifa’s duty as the custodian of world football.”

open image in gallery Spain are among the Uefa nations to have threatened to boycott the World Cup ( Reuters )

open image in gallery Infantino (left) has close ties with Trump ( PA Wire )

Even if his proposals are defeated, Infantino, though, will surely take another page from the Trump playbook in another respect: could you ever imagine Trump resigning over anything, no matter how egregious, let alone admitting to a miscalculation of such epic proportions? It says a lot that, in the midst of an apparent crisis, Infantino was accelerating his plans for an expansion to 64 teams for the next World Cup while his fiercest opponents, Uefa, were holding its emergency meeting on Thursday.

Infantino is acting like a tyrant and he must be stopped. Uefa and its allies will be rewarded for the strength of its opposition in recent days but they must now strike and put forward a candidate to challenge Infantino’s presidency when he stands for re-election in March next year. Uefa’s Alexander Ceferin, who has positioned himself as the anti-Infantino despite making anti-competitive changes to the Champions League under his leadership, would be an obvious candidate.

open image in gallery Aleksander Ceferin (left) and Nasser Al-Khelaifi are possible challengers to Gianni Infantino ( Getty )

The Independent, meanwhile, has reported that Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi, the chairman of Qatar Sports Investment, would also carry support. He could stand to gain from a further elevation of his status within the game. Other figures such as Lise Klaveness, the president of the Football Association of Norway, have been standing up to Infantino for some time. Klaveness in particular should be recognised for putting her head above the parapet long before the tide on Infantino turned within political circles.

Infantino’s plans for the ‘Fifa Forward Enterprise’ may appear to be on life support, but it will also take more to topple his empire. That said, football has spoken, and faces a window of opportunity that is must now seize if it wants to build a fairer game: the rejection of Infantino’s proposals has to now stand for the rejection of the man himself, and the Fifa he has helped shape.

News.content:

A man has been convicted of the "cold-blooded execution" of his former lover's new partner, whom he killed with a samurai sword.

Michael Bretton, 41, was found guilty of murdering Craig Hurcombe, 39, in Gurney Slade, Somerset, on 1 January.

Bristol Crown Court heard that Mr Hurcombe had been in a relationship with Kate Saunders, which ended in 2023. Ms Saunders and Bretton had subsequently met through an online dating website, leading to a casual relationship. However, when Ms Saunders and Mr Hurcombe rekindled their romance, Bretton became "clearly jealous".

Bretton, who worked in a chocolate factory, attended Mr Hurcombe’s work yard on New Year's Day to confront him. He used a samurai sword to kill Mr Hurcombe before burying his body in a shallow grave.

The defendant, from Shaftesbury, Dorset, denied murder, claiming Mr Hurcombe had died in an accident. However, a jury of seven men and five women unanimously convicted him after a two-week trial.

open image in gallery Craig Hurcombe was killed by Bretton in January ( Family handout )

Judge William Hart told the jury: "There is only one sentence available if a person is convicted of murder. That is life imprisonment but in order to pass sentence, I have to determine the minimum term that Mr Bretton must serve before he is eligible to be considered for release on licence."

The judge praised Mr Hurcombe’s family for their "dignity and restraint" throughout the proceedings, describing the case as "extraordinary". He added: "If you read about this case, you would think it is something from a crime novel."

Prosecutor Mark Cotter KC revealed that Bretton had fitted trackers to the cars of both Ms Saunders and Mr Hurcombe. He told jurors this behaviour escalated, culminating in the murder.

"It was a pre-meditated and cold-blooded execution, carried out with the use of a sword," Mr Cotter said. He added: "What is clear from the evidence is that Mr Bretton was obsessed with Kate Saunders and was clearly jealous of her renewed relationship with Craig Hurcombe."

The court heard Mr Hurcombe, from Devizes, went to work at Blanchard’s yard in Gurney Slade on the evening of 1 January. CCTV footage showed him waving to a camera at 6.26pm as he walked towards his lorry, believed to be shortly before his death.

Mr Hurcombe was reported missing by his mother on 10 January, and his body was discovered in a shallow grave in woodland at his work site on 14 January. Pathologist Dr Amanda Jeffery concluded he died from a single lengthy stab injury through his torso. A rusty samurai sword, having been in water, was later recovered from the River Stour.

Bretton was arrested on 12 January and made no comment during interviews, apart from denying wrongdoing. He maintained during the trial that Mr Hurcombe’s death was an accident.

Judge Hart is scheduled to sentence Bretton on Friday afternoon.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

What are you waiting for? |  Single and looking to find true love? Sign up today for Telegraph Dating and join more than 220,000 like-minded people. Join today

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibugyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibugyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibugyo species replaces Zaire.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

Sports.title: Chelsea signing Henderson and Welbeck because ‘they have a lot of young boys away with the fairies’, says title winner
Sports.content:
A SIX-TIME Premier League champion has blasted Chelsea’s young stars for being “a bit away with the fairies”.

Treble-winning midfielder Nicky Butt hailed Xabi Alonso‘s attempt to rein in an ill-disciplined dressing room by recruiting veteran duo Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.



Manchester United legend Butt was blunt about the state of the Blues.

He said: “They’ve got a lot of young boys in that training room that are a bit away with the fairies and doing what they want to do if I’m being honest.



“I’ve seen a few players like that in the training room.

“They’ll be there to get them to knuckle down a bit and I’m pretty sure Xabi Alonso will be thinking about wanting a bit of help in the background.”



Chelsea had the youngest average dressing room age in the league last season, and new manager Alonso was quick to make eyebrow-raising moves for two of the Prem’s senior citizens.

Welbeck, 35, has an incoming medical at Stamford Bridge, and Butt is firmly in favour of the Blues buying their first player over 30 since 2022.

Butt, speaking exclusively to Paddy Power, said: “The Danny Welbeck signing in particular is really good.”

“He’s a great squad lad, great to have on the bench, coming on, starting a few games, scoring your goals, and he’s a good professional.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

However, it came as “a bit more of a shock” to see Chelsea pursuing former England skipper Jordan Henderson.

The former Liverpool legend is the last English captain to lift the Premier League, and covered more kilometres per 90 minutes playing for Brentford last season than any Chelsea player.

Butt was full of praise for the 36-year-old: “Henderson is obviously a fantastic professional as well, been around the block, knows what he’s doing.”

The pair of seasoned pros last played together for England U21s back in 2010/11, and have both reportedly agreed two-year deals with the Blues.



Although the two signings still have enduring class to offer on the pitch, Butt believes the veterans’ true value will be their authoritative influence in the dressing room.

During England’s recent run to the World Cup semi finals, Henderson slotted into a player-coach role, and Butt thinks Chelsea have snapped him up for more of the same.

Sports.title: Fives candidates to replace Infantino as Fifa president including Arsene Wenger and chief who boycotted World Cup final
Sports.content:
FIFA could need a new president sooner rather than later after pressure increases on Gianni Infantino – but who would replace the current chief?

Infantino, 56, is facing calls to step down after his plans to sell part of the World Cup to private investors emerged.



If he isn’t ousted in the coming weeks or months, the much-maligned Infantino is only safe in his position until next year anyway.

Fifa members could vote for an alternative candidate at the 2027 election – but there’s a catch.



So far there is no contest for Infantino, who ran unopposed in 2019 and 2023.

He took over from the disgraced Sepp Blatter in the wake of 2015’s corruption scandal.



Infantino has already changed rules allowing him to stand for an unprecedented FOURTH term in charge – which would take him up to 2031 before stepping down.

Then he could potentially go into a role heading Fifa’s proposed new sister company in charge of making world football as much dollar as possible through its business connection and high-rolling investors.

There, he stands to earn a potentially staggering £1MILLION each week.

But none of this is guaranteed. Fifa could back down from their greedy shakeup after all 55 Uefa nations agreed to boycott upcoming events – including future women’s and youth World Cup.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Currently, Infantino is holding his ground. But senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro has RESIGNED over the controversy.

And Uefa are now thought to be preparing someone to stand against Infantino next year in the Fifa elections.

But who could take on the sport’s most powerful man? And if the net is cast wider than just Europe, are there any better solutions?

Alexander Ceferin

Perhaps the obvious name, Uefa president Ceferin is extremely well placed.



He has been in a battle with Fifa for years and has spoken out against them around high-profile situations including Folarin Balogun‘s overturned red card.

Ceferin didn’t even bother going to the World Cup final despite Spain being in it.

He is said to be happy in his position – which has been held since 2016 – which is expected to go on for a third term until 2031.

The Slovenian is described as happy to step up if nobody else will, but is not keen to move unless absolutely necessary.

Nasser Al-Khelaifi

That brings up PSG president Al-Khelaifi, who is one of the early favourites to challenge – and possibly succeed – Infantino.



He is also in charge of the European Football Clubs (EFC) and opposed the European Super League in 2021.

However, a representative of the Qatari is quoted as saying: “Nasser has absolutely no ambition, no intention, no interest in the Fifa role, and he will continue to discreetly support all the institutions of world and European football.”

Some reports suggest he could yet make a play.



Arsene Wenger

Former Arsenal boss Wenger has been on Fifa’s side for years, floating outrageous rule changes every now and then.

He is officially the Chief of Global Football Development and stays relatively quiet,

But with Wenger’s heft in the game and some backing, could he rise up against Infantino from within?



Victor Montagliani

Outside of Fifa and Uefa, Concacaf president Montagliani was a touted candidate for the presidency before all of this kicked off.

The Canadian has been claimed to have harboured interests in becoming top dog for a while as Infantino’s public popularity continued to wain in the build-up to – and during – the World Cup.

His term in North America and the Caribbean comes to an end next year and he is seeking another term.

But maybe he will go one up and rebel against Infantino instead.

Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa

Like Uefa and Concacaf – to a lesser extent – the AFC has spoken out against selling the World Cup.



And president Al Khalifa, from Bahrain, is an important figure with his fingers in at Fifa as well.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He is the senior vice-president of the Fifa Council and has joined the Infantino pile on.

Like Montagliani, he has a confederation election next year to think about as well as the possible Fifa one.

Sports.title: Man Utd files: Hollywood stars in frame to narrate Amazon doc and six academy stars removed from first team on website
Sports.content:
AMAZON is currently auditioning actors for the next James Bond but there is another casting choice more of interest to Manchester United staff: who will narrate their All or Nothing documentary?

Gary Oldman, a lifelong United fan, would have been an obvious choice but he has kept a lower profile at Old Trafford since the first round of Ineos redundancies in 2024.



Oldman’s solidarity was conspicuous by his absence for the 2024 pre-season tour in Los Angeles as he visited United on their previous visits to UCLA in 2017 and 2018.

Leon actor Oldman and fellow Oscar winner Daniel Day-Lewis made a very public trip in January to watch Millwall at the New Den, near Oldman’s birthplace of New Cross.



Succession star Brian Cox declared his allegiance to United on ITV during the World Cup, though he referred to the club as ‘Man U’.

Irish actor Barry Keoghan, memorable in The Banshees of Inisherin and Saltburn, would have cut-through with the Gen Z crowd.

On previous All or Nothings, the Manchester-bred Sir Ben Kingsley narrated Manchester City’s, Tom Hardy did Tottenham’s and Daniel Kaluuya lended his vocals to Arsenal’s.

City slickers

City are selling a £950 package for a VIP away trip at Old Trafford.

Details sent to fans via email reveal that the premium experience includes a ticket in the away end, secure parking at the Etihad, and return transport to the match.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



Guests will receive a pre-match lunch, an exclusive VIP gift, and a live Q&A hosted by former City players Shay Given and Shaun Wright-Phillips.

City said the away allocation will be drawn strictly from the club’s 15 per cent hospitality quota in the away end and will not reduce allocations for regular season ticket holders.

First teamers

IT was odd to see JJ Gabriel, a 15-year-old, added to the United first team section on the club website last week.

He was not the only one. Jacob Devaney, Dan Armer, Ethan Williams, Jaydan Kamason and Jim Thwaites were also included.

Someone has seen sense following the premature promotions as the sextet were removed from the section at the start of the week.



The initial update was to reflect their involvement in pre-season. That knee-jerk reaction has not happened before on United’s site during previous pre-seasons.

Normality has been largely restored, with the training goalie Dermot Mee now the only obscure presence in the senior squad. Chido Obi, Dan Gore and Ethan Wheatley have been removed and put into the under-21 section.

The Fletcher twins have their work cut out to justify their first-team status.

JJ Gabriel plan

THE word from United is that Gabriel was never going to play against Rosenborg in Trondheim.

Gabriel and fellow FA Youth Cup finalist Thwaites were the only outfield players who were unused substitutes in Norway as Michael Carrick made 11 substitutions.



United have to tread a fine line with Gabriel, who has generated firm interest from Barcelona. Gabriel cannot sign a professional contract until he turns 17 next year but United can secure a pre-contract agreement, as Arsenal did with the 16-year-old Max Dowman.

Gabriel has trained with the first team a number of times dating back to last October and his father publicly champions him on social media site X.

Just last week, Gabriel announced he’d signed a long-term contract with Nike, who commissioned a painting of the teen. To misquote Neville Southall, well done, he’s 15.

But United have been adept at ensuring youngsters do not get too much, too young.



De-ligtful

MATTHIJS DE LIGT has been out and about in the Cheshire village where he lives.

De Ligt enjoys a stroll to a nearby coffee shop, where he often takes a book to while away a couple of hours.

Onlookers have noticed how gingerly De Ligt has been walking, though. De Ligt underwent back surgery on May 15 and he has not played since November 30 last year.

De Ligt, 26, went on holiday to Ibiza earlier this summer and is certain to miss the start of the new Premier League season.



With five senior centre backs on their books, United are not planning to reinforce that department until next year.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez are both out of contract in 2027 but the club have the option to trigger one-year extensions with each player.

Maguire turns 34 next March while Martinez has missed 92 United matches in four seasons through injury. De Ligt has been sidelined for 37 of United’s last 53 games.



Domino’s Pizza

A PRE-SEASON victory in Norway ended on a high note for United—and with a surprisingly savory post-match recovery session.

Shortly after the final whistle sounded, a fresh pizza delivery made its way straight into the visiting dressing room to refuel the squad.

The players tucked into a few well-earned slices before making their prompt exit from the stadium.

Rosenborg’s Lerkendal Stadion features a fully operational Domino’s Pizza outlet built directly into its main concourse. It’s an official commercial partner of the Norwegian club.

Ev-ans stevens

UNITED first team coach Jonny Evans’ niece Sienna captained United’s girls’ side to glory in the Super Cup in Northern Ireland.



Sienna is the daughter of former United academy graduate Corry Evans, who won 69 caps for Northern Ireland.

Unlike her dad and uncle, who were more defensive players, Sienna is a striker.

United completed a girls double with the U14s beating Surf Select 4-0 and the U16s winning a penalty shootout against Shamrock Rovers.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Budget Energy SuperCupNI, formerly the Milk Cup, brought together 1,200 players from boys’ and girls’ teams, including clubs such as Liverpool, Rangers and Celtic.

Teams travelled from countries as far away as Mexico, Japan, Norway, the USA and the United Arab Emirates to play in more than 150 fixtures in the six-day tournament.

Sports.title: Arsenal legend sells £4m mansion to Oasis star Liam Gallagher – so his wife can go back to university
Sports.content:
AN ARSENAL legend has sold his luxurious mansion to Oasis star Liam Gallagher so his wife can go to university.

Gunners icon Tony Adams, 59, flogged the £4million property in December after initially listing it in early 2025.



The glamorous property is set on around five acres of land near Cirencester in the Cotswolds.

The former England defender, who appeared on Strictly Come Dancing in 2022, had owned the pad since buying it in 2002, for “half the price” he later listed it.



That fee brought with it a swimming pool, tennis courts, stables and even a separate two-bed cottage.

But after 25 years, a change of circumstances helped Adams make the decision to give the place up for a heartwarming reason.

Adams’ wife, Poppy Teacher, is pursuing a new passion at university, ushering in a ‘new era’ for the couple.

He explained, via the Mail: “This is a new era for us.

“We’ve sold the house and are returning to London. My wife is going back to school.”

His wife Poppy opened up on the reasoning behind the change of scenery and Adams’ touching reaction – despite his initial confusion.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“I told Tony I wanted to do early modern history and he said, ‘How do you monetise that?’ and I said ‘You don’t!’

“But I think he’s proud. He’s telling everyone I’m doing a PhD, but it’s a masters.”

“I’ve brought up the children, but now I need to use my brain again.



“Tony and I want to have a London life, do things like go to galleries.”

Meanwhile, Gallagher is loving life in the Cotswolds and even revealed that his new neighbours bring him cakes.

Asked if he had “any friendly neighbours”, the singer replied: “They’re absolutely incredible, they have not stopped baking me cakes and scones.”

Sports.title: Benjamin Mendy auctions off World Cup winners’ trophy just months after his sad, lonely new life was revealed
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY flop Benjamin Mendy has flogged his World Cup winners’ trophy in a desperate bid to raise cash.

The left-back, 32, got his hands on football’s biggest prize when France won the tournament in 2018.



But Mendy’s finances took a huge hit as he fought to be acquitted of eight rape charges.

And the ex-City man has now sold his replica of the World Cup trophy for £46,270.



Mendy, who also slapped a £5MILLION price tag on his Cheshire mansion in an attempt to avoid bankruptcy three years ago, put his prized possession up for sale through auctioneers Goldin.

The coveted item, which went under the hammer as part of the USA-based sports memorabilia specialists’ Global Football Auction Part Two, attracted a whopping 38 bids.

And the lucky winner also bagged a certificate signed by Mendy confirming the sparkling trophy – described as damaged due to a crack at the base and signs of wear – was genuine.

The defender made one substitute appearance as France won the World Cup for a second time.

Every member of the squad notched a replica of the famous trophy to add to their own personal collection.

But it emerged a matter of months ago that Mendy now lives a sad, lonely life in Poland after his wages have been slashed following his Etihad Stadium exit.



Having been on a contract which allowed him to pocket an eye-watering £500,000-per-month at City, he now earns just £10,000 every four weeks at Polish side Pogon Szczecin.

Mendy sold houses, supercars and designer watches for losses of more than £1m as he fought to clear his name in court.

The former Marseille and Monaco man faced two trials before being cleared of eight counts of rape, attempted rape and sexual assault in July 2023.



And Mendy then won his legal battle against City as he pushed for more than £11m in unpaid wages.

It was decided the Premier League giants had wrongly blocked his pay for 17 months while facing rape charges.

Mendy made a shock move to Lorient when his City deal ended, before joining FC Zurich and current employers Pogon Szczecin.

Sports.title: Chelsea secretly hit with SIX POINT deduction – but win appeal to have it overturned
Sports.content:
CHELSEA have dodged a points deduction thanks to a secret FA appeal – but have been hit with a £10million FA fine for dodgy agent deals under Roman Abramovich.

The Blues have also been handed a suspended transfer ban and the FA are still investigating individuals involved, but have avoided a sporting sanction from the FA, Premier League and Uefa.



Chelsea were charged with 74 breaches of FA rules relating to agent payments and third party transactions in September last year.

The charges related to deals between 2009-2022 under former owner, Roman Abramovich with moves for Eden Hazard, Willian, Ramires, David Luiz and Samuel Eto’o all implicated.



Chelsea admitted guilt on all 74 breaches, involving 32 players and 18 minors, which totalled to £47m in illegal payments.

After Chelsea beat Manchester United to the signing of Hazard, Sir Alex Ferguson claimed the Blues paid an agent fee of £6m.

None of the players involved are accused of any wrongdoing.

An initial decision from an FA regulatory commission imposed a suspended six-point ban on the Blues, which was replaced with a suspended transfer ban on appeal after the decision was made that the club gained no sporting advantage from the breaches.

Chelsea’s FA transfer ban is suspended until June next year.

Had the club properly reported the £47m in payments at the time, it is not believed they would have breached spending rules.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Chelsea’s current owners, Clearlake Capital and Todd Boehly, self-reported the club to the FA, Uefa and the Premier League following their 2022 takeover having discovered “incomplete financial reporting” during an audit of the club.

The FA decision praised the club for their “exceptional and unprecedented co-operation” during the process, which included interviews with employees past and present and the handing over of thousands of documents.

BlueCo, Chelsea’s ownership group, held back £150m of their £4.25bn purchase of the club as a buffer against financial penalties as a result.

Individuals related to the breaches are still under investigation by the FA, though SunSport understands no current Chelsea employees are under investigation.



In 2023 the club agreed an £8m settlement with Uefa over the rules breaches and were fined £10.75m by the Premier League earlier this year – a sanction which also came with a nine-month academy transfer ban and a suspended senior team transfer ban.

In a statement, Chelsea said: “Chelsea Football Club is pleased to confirm that a final decision has been reached by The FA’s judicial bodies in relation to historical regulatory matters that were self-reported by the club.

“In 2022, the club self-reported potential historical rule breaches to all applicable regulators. Following that report, it has worked openly and transparently with all regulators, including voluntarily and proactively disclosing many thousands of documents.

“As previously announced, settlement agreements have been entered into with UEFA and the Premier League concerning the same self-reported regulatory matters and topics that have been addressed before. The club is pleased to confirm that, now The FA process has concluded, this brings all regulatory proceedings against the club to a close.



“We are grateful to UEFA, the Premier League and The FA for their engagement with the club throughout these processes.”

An FA statement read: “A financial sanction of £10 million and a suspended two-window registration ban have been imposed on Chelsea FC for breaches of The Football Association [The FA] Football Agent Regulations, Regulations on Working with Intermediaries and Third Party Investment in Players Regulations.

“The FA charged Chelsea FC with 74 breaches of FA Rule E1.2 after its current ownership self-reported misconduct upon its purchase of the club. The FA is continuing to investigate individual misconduct arising out of this case.

“Chelsea FC admitted to the 74 breaches of FA Rule E1.2 prior to a hearing and an independent Regulatory Commission imposed a six-point deduction, which was to be suspended until 30 June 2027, and a £10 million fine.

“The club appealed against the suspended points deduction and an independent Appeal Board allowed the appeal and set aside this sanction following a further hearing. In its place, the Appeal Board imposed a registration ban for two complete and consecutive transfer windows which is suspended until 30 June 2027.



“The £10 million fine imposed by the Regulatory Commission was not subject to appeal and the full amount will be invested into grassroots football.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The Regulatory Commission and Appeal Board’s written reasons for their decisions can be found below. “

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s hottest romances over the years ahead of ‘wedding’ – from Kim K to BB’s Imogen Thomas
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo is rumoured to be marrying Georgina Rodriguez this weekend.

The footballer, 42, enjoyed a string of celebrity romances before he met his match.

From one night flings to secret smooches, the Portuguese superstar has had his fair share of steamy romances.



Although now a family-man, Cristiano Ronaldo was once linked with some of showbiz’s hottest women, including celebrities Paris Hilton and Kim Kardashian, as well as supermodel Irina Shayk.



But since 2016, the 42-year-old has shared a more tame existence with 32-year-old model Georgina Rodriguez, after the pair met at a Gucci store in Madrid.

Now, the couple have built a family of seven, with daughters Alana and Bella, son Cristiano Jr. and twins Mateo and Eva Maria.

In August last year, Georgina announced her engagement to the footballer via her diamond “boulder” ring.



Yet, as speculation grows that Ronaldo is set to wed his long-term sweetheart this weekend, it’s time to look back at some of this once-bachelor’s hottest romances.

Imogen Thomas

Big Brother star Imogen Thomas first shared a night of passion with the Portuguese superstar back in 2006, during his time at Manchester United, and the pair became linked with a brief romance.

The Welsh beauty queen was even rumoured to have rekindled with the football pro in 2011, although this was later denied by both parties.



Rita Pereira

One of Ronaldo’s first official girlfriends, the two met in Lisbon on vacation in 2006.

The now-prominent Portuguese actress dated the footballer for a few whirlwind months, before his rise to fame made it difficult for the pair to sustain their romance.

Gemma Atkinson

Then came 2007, and along with it, Gemma Atkinson.



The British star shared a four-month fling with the footballer after meeting at a Manchester United game, claiming he won her over with invitations for tea and watching British sitcoms.

Although his techniques may not have been too effective, as the couple parted not long after, their romance sparked headlines for months following it.

Bipasha Basu

Later that year, Ronaldo was spotted locking lips with Bollywood star Bipasha Basu at a Lisbon nightclub.

Bonding over the footballer’s unlikely love for Bollywood movies, the two remained close after their steamy encounter.



Paris Hilton

The A-lister first crossed paths with Ronaldo in 2009, when the pair were snapped getting close to one another over the course of two nights in LA.

The brief fling came shortly after Paris Hilton split from her long-term boyfriend Doug Reinhardt, but she quickly dropped Ronaldo too, maintaining they were just “good friends”.

Kim Kardashian

Kim Kardashian and Ronaldo made headlines in 2010, after a cozy meal together sparked a three-day holiday romance in Madrid.



Although the A-lister was wined and dined by the Portuguese player, and even shared a few nights at his villa, both parties went their separate ways soon after.

Irina Shayk

Then came Irina Shayk, a Russian supermodel who managed to keep the superstar committed for five long years.

Dating from 2010 to 2015, the two met at a fashion campaign and were often papped at high-profile events and jet-setting with one another.

The two were even engaged in 2011, when Ronaldo flew to New York on Valentine’s Day and proposed to her, but a wedding sadly never materialised.



Desiree Cordero

And just before Georgina was Spanish model Desiree Cordero, a brief fling in 2016 which was fraught with tension and rumours.

Describing the Miss Spain 2014 winner as “fame-hungry”, a swift split followed after Ronaldo became concerned by her “motives”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Now, Georgina and Ronaldo are speculated to be wedded at Quinta da Regaleira in Sintra, Portugal, although an official date for the lovebirds is still to be confirmed.

Until then, the couple appear to be enjoying family life in Mallorca, on a luxury holiday retreat.

Sports.title: Casemiro immediately risks Cristiano Ronaldo relationship with Lionel Messi statement
Sports.content:
CASEMIRO has risked leaving former team-mate Cristiano Ronaldo furious – after claiming Lionel Messi is “the god of football”.

The midfielder, 34, joined MLS side Inter Miami after leaving Manchester United at the end of last season.



And Casemiro will now have the chance to play alongside ex-Barcelona foe Messi, who was left in tears after narrowly missing out on World Cup glory, instead of trying to keep him at bay.

Inter Miami’s latest arrival revealed it is a dream come true to become team-mates with the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner.



But Casemiro’s honesty could put his relationship with Ronaldo in jeopardy.

The Brazilian said: “All players imagine playing with the best of all time. For me, without a doubt, I’m living a dream by playing with the best of all time.



“I want to enjoy it and help him keep winning because he is a winner. He is being joined by another player who wants to win and wants to compete.

“In the end, it’s always very close between winning and losing, but we want to compete. Of course, I’m here for him and to help him.

“He is one of the gods, if not the god of football. I want to enjoy being with him and keep winning with him.”

Casemiro and Ronaldo, 41, won the Champions League FOUR times while they were team-mates at Real Madrid.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And they were briefly back together when Casemiro sealed a £70million move to Man Utd.

The former Sao Paulo man revealed the chance to work closely with Messi convinced him to snub other offers when he quit Old Trafford.

Casemiro added: “Everyone knows that I left Man Utd on a free transfer and had many options.

“I had teams in Italy. I had many teams to play for and I am where I want to be.



“My family has certainly been very good to me in making this choice too. I am where I want to be and, of course, to play with the best.”

Casemiro, who made his Inter Miami debut in a narrow win over CF Montreal last week, has joined a long list of legends to have been team-mates with Messi and Ronaldo.

Sports.title: Casemiro makes Lionel Messi vs Cristiano Ronaldo feelings clear - 'he's a God'
Sports.content:
Casemiro makes Lionel Messi vs Cristiano Ronaldo feelings clear - 'he's a God'

Casemiro spent years playing with Cristiano Ronaldo and facing Lionel Messi - now after moving to Inter Miami he will team up with the Argentina icon

View 2 Images Lionel Messi has inspired Inter Miami to multiple honours (Image: CHANDAN KHANNA/AFP via Getty Images)

Casemiro insists he is heading to Inter Miami to "play with the best player of all time" as he prepares to team up with Lionel Messi for the first time.

‌



The Brazilian was a free agent after leaving Manchester United and, despite interest from LA Galaxy, has headed to Miami and waxed lyrical about the excitement he has to play alongside the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner.

‌



Casemiro spent nine years playing with Cristiano Ronaldo at Real Madrid, where they combined to win four Champions League titles together. That came at a time when Ronaldo and Messi were playing in the same league, vying for the same titles and individual accolades.

‌



The rivalry became tribal, both on and off the pitch, and no one ever spoke against their team-mate. Now, given he has no club connection to Ronaldo, nor are they compatriots, Casemiro has admitted that he sees Messi as "the God of football".

The Brazilian said: "For me, without a doubt, I am coming only to play with the best player of all time. I want to enjoy, I want to help him to keep winning because he is a winner. Another player is joining who wants to win, who wants to compete.

Bruno Guimaraes pushes for Arsenal transfer with Newcastle agreement imminent READ MORE :

"I am where I want to be in MLS. I left United as a free agent, I had options in Italy, other teams in different places, but I am where I want to be ... I want to enjoy being with him, helping him win and making him bigger. He's one of, if not the god of football and I want to help."

‌



The Argentine is having to deal with a second World Cup final loss of his career, but since he and Ronaldo left European football it is Messi whose legacy has been furthered.

He has helped Argentina finally end their World Cup drought and then claimed a second Copa America title of his career. Messi has now led Inter Miami to the MLS title for the first time. He also helped the Florida franchise win the 2023 Leagues Cup trophy and the 2024 Supporters' Shield.

View 2 Images Casemiro spent years playing with Cristiano Ronaldo at Real Madrid

‌



Casemiro was allowed to leave Manchester following the expiry of his contract but ended on a high following an up and down four years in the Premier League. He was initially a big hit, despite questions over his signing given his age profile and wages.

That was used a stick to beat him with when United's form - and his personal performances - nosedived. Casemiro stuck at it though and, during the team's renaissance under Michael Carrick last term, the midfielder came up with numerous big goals as the Red Devils finished third.

Sports.title: Andy Burnham says Gianni Infantino 'wrong man' to lead FIFA as he slams 'outrageous' World Cup plan
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham says Gianni Infantino 'wrong man' to lead FIFA as he slams 'outrageous' World Cup plan

The PM said the plan to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors was an “outrageous idea” as he said Infantino should follow his advisor Carlos Cordeiro in resigning

View 4 Images Andy Burnham has said Gianni Infantino is the “wrong man” to be leading FIFA (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/POOL PA via AP)

Andy Burnham has said Gianni Infantino is the “wrong man” to be leading FIFA following the row over proposals to sell a stake in the World Cup.

‌



The PM said the plan was an “outrageous idea” after Fifa appeared to double down, with Infantino giving football associations until September 19 to back his plan. The governing body says it has launched a consultation over setting up a separate $20billion (£14.9billion) company to run its competitions, which will be called FIFA Forward Enterprise.

‌



Infantino’s authority was dealt another blow after Carlos Cordeiro, one of his senior advisers, resigned with immediate effect in protest at proposals to sell a stake in the World Cup.

‌



View 4 Images Infantino is "wrong man" to lead Fifa says Burnham (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino ally quits as FIFA boss blasted over World Cup plans in angry statement READ MORE :

FIFA president Gianni Infantino was backed by The FA in statement that now looks laughable READ MORE :

And after being told of the development the PM said his opposition to the plans was “strengthening” saying the idea should “never even have been brought forward”. Asked if he thought Infantino should follow his advisor out of the door Burnham added he was “the wrong man to lead the organisation”.

Burnham’s comments make him the first leader of a major country to call Infantino’s position into question. European FAs have already threatened to boycott future Fifa tournaments while US Soccer chief Cordeiro criticised “a bad deal for football” and pointed out that the global governing body already sits on huge amounts of debt-free reserves.

‌



He said: “I cannot stand by while Fifa considers selling a stake in the World Cup. I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally. It is a bad deal for Fifa’s member associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.”

Cordeiro has worked for Fifa since 2021 as senior adviser to Infantino and also operated as a senior adviser to the White House taskforce on this summer’s World Cup. In resigning he said Fifa “already has the financial capacity to provide [additional financial] support from existing resources”. He added that Fifa would be “mortgaging football’s future without any compelling justification” if it sold off a permanent stake.

View 4 Images Spain celebrate their World Cup win with fans in Madrid (Image: Hugo Ortuno/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

‌



Earlier this week Uefa, European football’s governing body, said: "The World Cup is not for sale,” as 55 nations threatened to boycott Fifa competitions. They added: “No Uefa national teams will participate in any Fifa competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that Fifa will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.”

The FA backed the stance, saying: “We stand shoulder to shoulder with our European colleagues and fully support the collective view. We oppose Fifa's plans - the Fifa World Cup belongs to football and always will, while Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said: “Football belongs to the fans, not billionaire investors. Enough is enough.”

View 4 Images Fifa HQ in Zurich, Switzerland (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

The Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf have also voiced their opposition to the plans. Fifa had attempted to double down on its position stating “we will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA [member association] has the ability to express its vote based on facts”.

A statement from the Asian federation said: ‘“The AFC calls upon Fifa to undertake an urgent review of its governance and decision-making framework to ensure that proposals of global significance are developed through proper consultation, meaningful engagement and appropriate oversight by Fifa’s statutory bodies.”
