Sports.title: Real Madrid told to stop making 'fake stories' by Hull owner as they win transfer race
Sports.content:
Real Madrid told to stop making 'fake stories' by Hull owner as they win transfer race

Hull City are preparing to embark on their first Premier League season since 2017 after last year’s promotion and their owner Acun Ilicali has not been afraid to discuss their plans in the transfer market

View 2 Images Acun Ilicali has regularly spoken out on Hull's transfer busines (Image: Getty Images)

Hull boss Acun Ilicali has accused Real Madrid of making up ‘fake stories’ after the Tigers reportedly went head-to-head with the Spanish giants for striker Carlos Espi. The Yorkshire side are deep in preparations for their Premier League return, having sealed promotion under Sergej Jakirović.

‌



They have already been busy in the transfer market, albeit are still keen on adding a new forward to their ranks. Hull had identified Levante forward Carlos Espi as an option, albeit were beaten to the punch by Real Madrid, who swooped in to activate his €25million release clause.

‌



It was previously reported that Hull had tabled an offer for the striker, albeit owner Iliaci has clarified that is not the case.

‌



Taking to social media, he wrote: “Guys your club is big enough without making fake stories about Hull City. We never made any offer, we wish him the best in Real Madrid.”

Man Utd transfer talks confirmed as agent says deal is close READ MORE :

Iliaci’s jibe at Real Madrid is not the first time that he has spoken out on Hull’s summer business. After growing irritated with speculation surrounding his side, he wrote: “Dear Hull City family, We are reading dozens of false transfer rumours in many places.

“We are disturbed by the claims that we have been rejected and by the use of our club's name to gain attention. We have been working intensively for two months.

‌



“I believe we will build a team that we will all be proud of. To prevent false speculation and to give you more information, I am leaving you with our latest transfer situation, which includes some clues.”

The 57-year-old then followed that up with a series of national flag emojis, accompanied by percentages to signify how close various deals were. Hull have already completed four signings this summer, with Jack Butland, Hidemasa Morita, Matt Targett and Oscar Zambrano having joined the club, while Olympiacos goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis is expected to arrive soon.

View 2 Images Carlos Espi has signed for Real Madrid amid interest from Hull (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Hull have also taken out a £55m bridging loan, a move that has been criticised by some. But Ilicali believes it will give his side the best chance of competing throughout the coming season.

He said: “Why is it strange? We want this club to be financially strong to be able to make transfers.

"I respect that everyone is talking about this loan but, at the end of the day, what we are trying to do is be in a strong financial position so that we can spend money when we need to.

‌



"This club was supported with money from my company for four years. All I can ask is for our fans to not worry about any of the financial things. We can loan money and spend money. They should be confident that we are going to use the money in Hull City.

"All we have done is take the money that we are going to get anyway a bit sooner, so that we can be stronger in the transfer market. We will use it for the club's benefit. We need to make good transfers this summer so we need more money now.

"We have to be strong in the Premier League. It takes around two to three weeks to get some transfers [over the line] so we have to move quickly. In order to be quick, we need the money in advance."

Sports.title: Premier League manager sack race as Michael Carrick reign shows level of uncertainty
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has only been in charge of Manchester United for a matter of months - but has already outlasted a number of his rivals. The Red Devils boss was entrusted with the reins in January and after leading the club back into the Champions League, was handed a permanent deal.

Of course, in Premier League terms, a lengthy contract does not necessarily mean that a manager will be in situ for that long. In fact, it is very rare to see a manager see out his entire deal before either being sacked or poached by another club.

That has certainly been the case this summer, with as many as eight Premier League clubs having opted for changes in the close season, for one reason or another. The latest has been Newcastle, with Eddie Howe moving on after nearly five years.

That now leaves Carrick as the tenth longest serving manager in the top flight, despite having only been in charge for just 20 games. He could even move up that list throughout the season as more changes are made.

‌



So, how safe are Carrick and his Premier League rivals? Mirror Football takes a look…

Safe as houses

Let’s start with the man serving as the inspiration for this list: Carrick. The former midfielder did a stellar job at Old Trafford last season so looks unlikely to be going anywhere any time soon.

The same could overwhelmingly be said of Arsenal’s Mikel Arteta. The Spaniard ended the club’s long wait for a Premier League title last term, as well as leading the Gunners into the Champions League final. It would be a huge shock to see him going anywhere.

‌



Regis Le Bris and Unai Emery also enjoyed brilliant seasons for Sunderland and Aston Villa respectively - the latter winning the Europa League. The pair will likely remain in situ for the forthcoming campaign.

Speaking of brilliant campaigns, Frank Lampard led Coventry City to a place in the Premier League last term and was rewarded with a new contract only last month. Roberto De Zerbi should also be fine, having led Spurs to survival in his first campaign in North London and been handed the keys to the kingdom in North London.

Marco Rose, Alvaro Arbeloa, Andoni Iraola, Pierre Sage and Enzo Maresca were only appointed this summer so should not be in any danger - in the short term at least.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta looks very safe at Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Not in immediate danger

There are a few exceptions to that rule, however. Xabi Alonso replaced Liam Rosenior this summer and had he taken the reins at any other club other than Chelsea, he would be safer.

As it is, he’s underneath an ownership that is no stranger to a managerial change. Indeed, no Chelsea manager has surpassed 100 games in charge since Antonio Conte’s two-season spell was ended in 2018. Alonso is a talented manager but he could potentially be in danger should the Blues start the season poorly.

The same could also be said of Gary O’Neil. He only arrived at Ipswich in the summer having replaced Kieran McKenna. The former Wolves boss should be afforded patience but should the Tractor Boys start struggling, then they could consider a change.

Elsewhere, Fabian Hurzeler and Keith Andrews enjoyed brilliant seasons with Brighton and Brentford last term - the former leading the Seagulls back into Europe. But it feels that both Hurzeler and Andrews are just a bad run of form away from being put under pressure - there was a point last season when Brighton fans weren't particularly impressed with Hurzeler, before an excellent second half of the campaign.

‌



View 3 Images Xabi Alonso was only appointed by Chelsea in the summer (Image: Getty Images)

Not out of the woods

Despite there still being a few weeks to go until the season gets underway, there are some managers who might be looking over their shoulders already. Everton’s David Moyes is under pressure from fans after a disappointing end to last season. Should the Toffees start the new campaign in similar fashion, the Scot could find himself close to the sack.

Daniel Farke finds himself in a similar - if not identical position. The German has had a fantastic impact at Leeds but there have regularly been whispers about the club’s ownership wanting a new man for some time, and they've never quite gone away. Farke needs a good start to 2026/27 to ensure he is kept on.

The same could also be said of Sergej Jakirović. Despite leading Hull to promotion, the Tigers are not particularly known for patience when it comes to their managers so he might be one moved on early.

‌



And the former Crystal Palace boss Oliver Glasner finds himself in a similar position. The Austrian was only appointed by Nottingham Forest this summer but the hot seat at the City Ground can be compared to a game of musical chairs - just ask Ange Postecoglou and Sean Dyche. Endure a similar run of form and Glasner could well find himself without a job before the leaves even turn brown.

Sports.title: Man Utd asking for 'day-to-day' updates on striker transfer as £30m bid lands
Sports.content:
Man Utd asking for 'day-to-day' updates on striker transfer as £30m bid lands

Manchester United are reportedly on the market for a new centre-forward, as they look to bolster their attacking line for 2026/27

View 2 Images Manchester United have been linked with a move for Nicolo Tresoldi (Image: Isosport/MB Media, Getty Images)

Manchester United could turn Nicolo Tresoldi's head this summer, despite his commitment to Club Brugge. United have enjoyed a fruitful transfer window this summer thus far, with a number of top-class arrivals.

‌



As well as forking out for midfielders Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, goalkeeperKarl Darlow will likely play second-string to Senne Lammens after joining the club as a free agent. However, a number of problem positions could still do with rectifying before next month's seasonal curtain-opener.

‌



One of those departments comes in the form of strikers. While Benjamin Sesko held his own in the Premier League in his maiden season, he wasn't quite the 20-goal striker that United were seeking.

‌



Man Utd transfer talks confirmed as agent says deal is close READ MORE :

Having managed to find the back of the net just 11 times in 30 appearances, United could be on the lookout for someone to challenge Sesko's position. One name that has emerged as a possible signing is 21-year-old Brugge frontman, Tresoldi.

The Germany youth international has shone in the Belgian Pro League since his switch from Hannover 96 last summer, notching 23 goals and nine assists in all competitions during his debut campaign. And consequently, several Premier League sides are monitoring the situation with an eye towards a transfer.

United are believed to be among those clubs, alongside Chelsea - who are currently restructuring their first-team squad following Xabi Alonso's appointment as head coach. That said, United may face a considerable challenge should they be genuine in their interest in Tresoldi.

‌



The Cagliari-born striker has recently reconfirmed his dedication to Brugge for 2026/27 following his impressive performances in the Belgian Pro League last season. With three years remaining on his existing deal, club president Bart Verhaeghe has also made it clear that Tresoldi will not be departing - not even for a record-breaking sum.

View 2 Images Manchester United could bring in competition for Benjamin Sesko (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



With substantial financial resources available, INEOS could alter that situation. HNS claim that United are keeping tabs on Tresoldi's circumstances on a 'day-to-day' basis, while Roma are also pursuing the talent.

The publication also reports that the Serie A heavyweights have lodged an offer of £29.9million. Without a release clause in his deal until next year, the decision rests firmly with Brugge as they attempt to hold onto Tresoldi.

And notwithstanding their resolute position, that's not to suggest an extraordinary proposal couldn't shift matters. Supporters have witnessed clubs reverse their position repeatedly concerning a player's availability during transfer windows once a substantial multi-million pound bid arrives.

Sports.title: FIFA president Gianni Infantino was backed by The FA in statement that now looks laughable
Sports.content:
The FA fully backed Gianni Infantino's FIFA presidency bid back in 2016. The then-FA chairman, Greg Dyke, hailed him as a “straightforward guy” whilst ex-Manchester United chief David Gill maintained it was “a good day for football”.

Infantino triumphed over the former Asian Football Confederation president, Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa, by 115 votes to 88 and the FA were fully behind the former UEFA man landing the top job. A decade on and they're putting out statements condemning his grand plans to sell out stakes in the World Cup.

Dyke claimed at the time that Infantino's victory was a new start for FIFA. Gill had been one of Sir Alex Ferguson's key lieutenants at Manchester United but moved on to become the FA director who also sat on the executive committee at both UEFA and FIFA. He too was thrilled to see Infantino’s election.

Infantino vowed to "restore the image of FIFA and make sure everybody will be happy with what we do" when he was elected. A decade on from that opening statement and the former UEFA general secretary is now fighting for his job after his latest controversy.

‌



Infantino's spell as the man in charge of world football has been marred by moves seen in some quarters as little more than money grabbing, even if the Swiss-Italian once claimed that "it’s your money, not the money of the FIFA president".

When he was appointed as FIFA's president the organisation was at an extremely low ebb following a spell under Sepp Blatter marred by corruption. Infantino vowed to change that perception, but as the years have gone on his moves have appeared more and more self obsessed.

His latest move, a desire to sell stakes in FIFA's tournaments, the main one being the World Cup, to outside investors is seen purely as a financial coup.

‌



View 3 Images Former FA Chairman Greg Dyke was fully behind the election result ten years ago

None of the major federations around the world, led by UEFA, want anything to do with it and, given it would need member approval, it looks like the proposal is already dead in the water. UEFA branded the proposal "irresponsible and indefensible" while labelling Infantino's offer of £30m to FIFA's 211 members to endorse his new enterprise - while warning nations they wouldn't get that cash if it ultimately passed but they voted against him - as "governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game."

Even before this drastic World Cup plot, Infantino had been the man who presided over an expanded World Cup, which opened doors to lesser nations, but also helped raise more cash for FIFA given the additional games. The World Cup we've just seen was overshadowed by ludicrious ticket prices, which Infantino continued to defend.

He's also masterminded a new Club World Cup, which went from seven teams to 32. That again was seen by some as FIFA trying to create a rival to the Champions League, UEFA's tournament which remains the most revered club competition in the world. The expanded Club World Cup showed little regard for player welfare given the amount of games.

‌



All of which makes Infantino's desire to bring FIFA out of the doldrums all the more laughable 10 years on, with the former UEFA man's legacy looking increasingly tarnished.

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino said he would "restore the image of FIFA"

He claimed: “We enter now a new era. We’ll restore the image of FIFA and make sure everybody will be happy with what we do.”

Speaking to those who voted for him he vowed: “I want to be the president of all of you. I travelled through the globe and I will continue to do this. I want to work with all of you to restore and rebuild a new era where we can put football in the centre of the stage. Fifa has gone through sad times, moments of crisis. But those times are over.”

‌



Despite the factions that now exist, the FIFA president once hailed: “I’m a candidate of the whole world and football. We have to build bridges, not walls.”

The irony now being that the walls are firmly caving in with three federations issuing statements to combat his World Cup plans, some calling for change. All whilst Infantino loses those around him as the faith in him diminishes.

Sports.title: Chelsea handed £10m fine and suspended transfer ban
Sports.content:
Chelsea have been fined £10m and given a suspended two-window transfer ban by an independent appeal board after admitting breaches of Football Association agent rules, the FA has announced.

An earlier independent commission had imposed a suspended six-point deduction, which was set aside and the suspended transfer ban imposed in its place.

The FA confirmed the imposition of sanctions on the west London club on Friday, who admitted to a total of 74 breaches of FA regulations covering agents, working with intermediaries and third-party investment in players.

The club's new owners self-reported the breaches to the football authorities in May 2022, when they were in the process of buying the club from Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Kaveh Solhekol explains why Chelsea have been punished for breaching FA rules of payments to agents and intermediaries under previous ownership.

The transfers which raised potential concerns during the takeover process are believed to include deals for players such as Eden Hazard, Samuel Eto'o and Willian.

The six-point deduction, suspended until June 30 2027, was imposed by the independent commission which initially heard the case but the club appealed against that.

An appeal board instead replaced the points penalty with the suspended two-window transfer ban.

The £10m fine imposed by the Regulatory Commission was not subject to appeal and the full amount will be invested into grassroots football.

Chelsea have previously entered sanction settlements in regard to this matter with the Premier League and UEFA.

A club statement read: "Chelsea Football Club is pleased to confirm that a final decision has been reached by The FA's judicial bodies in relation to historical regulatory matters that were self-reported by the club.

"In 2022, the club self-reported potential historical rule breaches to all applicable regulators. Following that report, it has worked openly and transparently with all regulators, including voluntarily and proactively disclosing many thousands of documents.

"As previously announced, settlement agreements have been entered into with UEFA and the Premier League concerning the same self-reported regulatory matters and topics that have been addressed before. The club is pleased to confirm that, now The FA process has concluded, this brings all regulatory proceedings against the club to a close.

"We are grateful to UEFA, the Premier League and The FA for their engagement with the club throughout these processes."

Sports.title: 'I want it so badly!' - Emotional Tamburlini faces nervous Solheim wait
Sports.content:
An emotional Chiara Tamburlini faces a nervous wait to see if she has qualified for Team Europe’s Solheim Cup side after missing the cut at the AIG Women’s Open.

Tamburlini came into the final women's major of the year second in the Ladies European Tour's Solheim Cup points list, with the top two in those standings after this week securing their spot in Anna Nordqvist's side.

The Swiss player arrived at Royal Lytham & St Annes with a slender 1.1-point lead over Helen Briem, with Tamburlini posting a four-bogey finish to her opening-round 75 and confirming her early exit with a three-over 74 on Friday morning.

Briem and France's Agathe Laisne also missed the cut to end their automatic qualification hopes, but Tamburlini is still left relying on other players' performances over the weekend to see whether she will make her Solheim Cup debut.

"I want it [Solheim Cup spot] so badly but sometimes the things you want so badly almost hinder your performance more," Tamburlini, reduced to tears, exclusively told Sky Sports.

"Obviously really disappointed to not be playing the weekend. I really hope I'll still get the spot and I feel like if I do, it'll be a really good motivation for the next couple of events as well.

"Solheim Cup was one of my goals for this year but it's also my first year on the LPGA Tour as well. Trying to establish myself on this tour has been quite difficult this year, so hopefully I get this spot to give myself a bit of a kick.

Image: Tamburlini has dropped to world No 100 after a disappointing campaign

"Not looking great as well with keeping my LPGA card at the moment. Worst case, there's always other options as well. I'm trying to take a little bit of pressure off myself with that. We'll see what happens this weekend on the side of Solheim."

The 26-year-old has finished no higher than 17th on the LPGA Tour this season and has now missed the cut in four of her last six starts, although Tamburlini insists her play is better than her 2026 results show.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tamburlini claimed her maiden Ladies European Tour title at the 2024 Joburg Ladies Open, one of three wins that season

"I feel like honestly over the last seven or eight weeks I've been really close with everybody in my team again," Tamburlini explained. "I feel like we're connecting more again - it was a bit difficult in the beginning of the year, being more in the US.

"I know the scores don't show it, but I feel like my game is so much more solid. I'm starting to recognize my game a lot more again from how it was the last two years really, which is nice - obviously disappointed to not see the results.

"I feel like my game is, as stupid as it sounds, it's not that terrible really. The margins, we all know it, are so small."

Tamburlini was part of Europe's team trip to Bernardus Golf after the Evian Championship earlier this month, but remains hopeful of returning as part of the 12-strong line-up that takes on Team USA from September 11-13.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the final day from the 2024 Solheim Cup, as Team USA secured a 15.5-12.5 victory over Europe in Virginia

"Just being there made me realise again even more really how much I want it," Tamburlini admitted. "It's been nice to get a bit closer to all the older girls as well that I haven't really played with much.

"They've been all super welcoming as well and open for questions and everything, which has been really nice.

Lottie Woad could move above her in the standings with a top-three finish, while Maja Stark and Carlota Ciganda are among the others who could deny Tamburlini an automatic spot over the coming days.

"I will probably end up looking at the leaderboard [over the weekend] a lot," Tamburlini insisted. "Right now, I'm saying my goal is to not look at it too much!"

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look back at some of Anna Nordqvist's best shots from her previous Solheim Cup appearances

The Solheim Cup qualification campaign ends on Sunday evening, with the top two on that Ladies European Tour points list by the highest-ranked players available in the Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings earning automatic spots.

Nordqvist will then name her four captain's picks on Monday afternoon, live on Sky Sports. Nanna Koerstz Madsen and Leona Maguire are among the past players in possible contention to be selected, along with former major champion Georgia Hall.

Sports.title: 'Sort yourself out, Harry' - Nasser urges Brook to mature after captaincy snub
Sports.content:
Nasser Hussain has urged Harry Brook to mature after the England white-ball skipper was snubbed for the Test captaincy despite England cricket chief Rob Key confirming the decision was not related to his workload.

Test vice-captain Brook - who oversaw six wins in seven white-ball fixtures against an India side ranked No 1 in the world in July - was overlooked in favour of veteran Joe Root, who undertakes his second spell as Test captain after holding the role between 2017 and 2022.

With the Test team set to embark on a new chapter under incoming head coach Stephen Fleming, former England captain Hussain has rued what he feels is a "missed opportunity" for Brook to take the reins, amid a lack of other suitable candidates.

"I think Harry Brook is a very good captain," Hussain said on the Sky Sports Cricket podcast.

"He's become England's white-ball captain and he's doing it very well.

"But with him are all these off-field antics and that immaturity - you need the mature Harry Brook to come out, and it's been lacking.

"That's why I'm a little bit disappointed in Harry himself, that I think there's a very good captain in there. I think it's a missed opportunity.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brook hit eight stunning sixes after being dropped by India, finishing on 95 not out for England

"One of the things in [new head coach Stephen Fleming's] in-tray will be to sit with Harry Brook and actually say, 'we've had to [give the captaincy] to someone that may not actually want to do it'.

"The lad that will do anything for English cricket in Joe Root is doing it again for English cricket because we couldn't trust you to do the job.

"Sort yourself out, Harry, because I think you should be the next England Test cricket captain."

Key: Brook captaincy snub wasn't related to white-ball workload

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brook reflects on England's ODI series victory over India and what it meant to the team

Key, the managing director of England men's cricket, has confirmed the decision to reappoint Root as Test captain was unrelated to Brook's white-ball workload.

The Test vice-captain - who outgoing skipper Ben Stokes had backed to be his successor - made controversial headlines after being fined £50,000 for an incident involving a nightclub bouncer ahead of an ODI in New Zealand last winter.

"I just don't feel like this is the right time for Harry Brook to be the Test captain," Key told Sky Sports News.

"That was the reason for that decision. I also think it's tough to do all three, but that didn't really come into it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The best of the action from the fourth T20I in Bristol as England demolished India to secure a first-ever series win over their opponents in the format

"We just felt that it was the right time for [Joe Root] and he's the right man.

"Brook's time will come. He's done a brilliant job. He's taken the T20 team to number one in the world. They've just beaten the world champions in 50-over cricket.

"That's a year and a half into a project with him and Brendon McCullum. We've got three formats now where I'm so optimistic about what we can do in all three."

No concerns over Root's return, says Key

Key also backed Root to have a successful second spell at the helm, with England's all-time leading Test run scorer set to lead the team out for a record-extending 66th Test as captain, after deputising for an absent Stokes in the second Test against New Zealand at The Oval.

Root returning to the position had seemed highly unlikely given that, upon stepping down in 2022 after one win from his final 17 Tests as skipper, he revealed his relationship with the role had become "very unhealthy" and cited the "toll" of his years in charge.

"Stephen and I have spoken at length about that and we both feel that Joe Root is by far away the best person to do this job," Key said.

"Last time he did it, I mean I came into this job and it's only then - when you see behind the curtain - do you realise what Joe Root had to put up with.

"His batting was outstanding and I feel I'm so excited to see Joe have the chance to captain the team without all of the distractions."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking after the New Zealand Test win in 2022, Joe Root explained why he had taken the decision to step away from the Test captaincy

Root's batting average dropped from 53.35 to 46.71 during his previous spell in charge, but Key has dispelled any doubts over whether Root has the drive to lead his country once again.

"I think he was really keen when he did it at The Oval. He was relishing that opportunity," said Key.

"He now has a chance to go and show probably just how good a captain he can be.

"Joe Root scores runs and you feel the last time that he did it his game got better and better under the toughest of circumstances.

"No concerns [over a possible drop in form]."

Sports.title: 'Genuine concern' expressed for Saltburn members amid 'Clicky Ponting' scandal
Sports.content:
The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League has expressed its "genuine concern for the welfare" of Saltburn Cricket Club members as it continues its inquiry into the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating controversy.

Video footage of a Saltburn player, who has been named as Brian Devine, allegedly clicking his fingers to get a caught-behind wicket in a recent second-team game against Norton sparked outrage and went viral on social media.

The NYSDL launched an investigation on Monday, while Saltburn have suspended Devine for the "foreseeable future" and said they were treating allegations of cheating "with the utmost seriousness".

In a further statement, the League said on Friday that it had met with Saltburn officials and had received guidance from the England and Wales Cricket Board to ensure it follows "a due and appropriate process that has to be comprehensive and fair to all".

The League added: "Whilst we understand, to some degree, the interest this issue has generated in the press and media it is imperative that now this process is under way that the rights of all parties are observed, including the overriding principles of natural justice and a right to a fair hearing for any individual or any entity concerned. Anything less risks prejudicing any formal actions which may follow.

"Finally we would want to place on record our genuine concern for the welfare for those at Saltburn Cricket Club and ask for all to take that into account - there are many people at the club and one of our aims will be to provide them with any well-being support we can."

The video footage was met with global condemnation, with the incident making headlines in Australia, New Zealand, Canada, India and the USA among other countries, while it has been dubbed 'Clicky Ponting' in reference to former Australia captain Ricky Ponting.

Saltburn, 17 points clear at the top of Division Two after winning the match by 159 runs, conceded Wednesday's second-team cup match against Marton in the wake of the controversy.

In response to the video footage on social media, Middlesbrough's second XI captain Rory Cotterill claimed there were two more incidents of cheating in his side's 29-run defeat to Saltburn last month.

Image: Saltburn Cricket Club is at the centre of the sporting scandal

More video footage has since emerged, which allegedly shows Devine, then playing for Pudsey St Lawrence in the Bradford Premier League, repeatedly clicking his fingers while opponents were batting.

Pudsey St Lawrence said in a statement on Thursday: "At no stage was the club aware of any alleged misconduct by Mr Devine, nor were any concerns or complaints raised with the club by opposition teams or umpires who officiated the fixtures in question.

"The club expects its players to uphold the highest standards of integrity and sportsmanship and takes any credible concerns extremely seriously."

The Bradford League added in a statement: "We are aware of the video footage circulating, but it is not our policy to undertake retrospective investigations."

Sports.title: 'It would be a brilliant story' - Key open to Stokes making Ashes return
Sports.content:
England cricket chief Rob Key has left the door open to Ben Stokes coming out of international retirement to play in next summer's home Ashes series against Australia.

Stokes gave up the England Test captaincy and retired from international cricket following his side's 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand in June, which followed a 4-1 Ashes loss to Australia over the winter.

The 35-year-old's decision came after he had been made unavailable for selection for the second Test against New Zealand, after breaching a midnight curfew when out celebrating England's win in the series opener.

There was speculation in the aftermath of the saga that Stokes had been left disappointed by the way he was treated by England's hierarchy, who on Thursday reinstated Joe Root as captain and appointed Stephen Fleming as Brendon McCullum's successor as Test head coach.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stokes reflected on his England career after his final Test match

Asked if the door was still open to Stokes returning to face Australia next summer, England managing director Key told Sky Sports News: "It would be a brilliant story if he does."

Quizzed on whether Stokes had intimated a return, Key said: "No, he hasn't but I wouldn't be surprised. Anything's possible with Ben."

On whether the bridge had been burnt in terms of his own relationship with Stokes, Key added: "No, not at all. Not as far as I'm concerned."

Key: I'm still the right man for the job

Image: Key reasserted his passion to continue leading English cricket after a run of seven defeats in the last nine Tests

Key also reaffirmed his desire to continue in his own position, which has come under scrutiny during a turbulent summer for English Test cricket.

England's managing director has overseen the sacking of a head coach, the retirement of a captain, a plethora of behavioural issues amid allegations of a drinking culture and a run of seven losses in the last nine Test matches.

Asked whether he still had the passion to lead England cricket, Key said: "Yeah, definitely.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day five of the third Test between England and New Zealand

"I'm optimistic about what we can do.

"The players that are going to take us forward into this next generation are the ones I believe that can go on to become world-class cricketers. There's a couple in there at the moment. There's so many that could go on to become a world-class team

"The key now is to not only have success but sustain it and keep repeating it. That's the system we're trying to put in place.

"In Stephen Fleming and Brendon McCullum, I think we've got the best two coaches"

Fleming's lack of red-ball experience not a concern, says Key

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Key explains why former New Zealand captain Stephen Fleming has been selected as head coach of the England Test side

Key also batted away doubts over incoming head coach Fleming's lack of experience with international or red-ball cricket.

Fleming's sole head coaching role since retiring as New Zealand Test captain has been at the helm of the Chennai Super Kings in the IPL, recently vacating the post he has held since 2009 before taking on the England job.

"I think he's [been] one of the most experienced coaches of international cricketers for the last 18 years," said Key.

"You think about that job that he's done in the IPL and you do not forget Test cricket, how to go about it, how to play it with the career that he had as a player, more importantly as a captain as well.

"It's not like for the last 18 years whilst he's been in the IPL he's not been across Test cricket. We've had dealings in the past when our players have gone to Chennai and they've all spoken so highly - I've not met anyone that hasn't spoken highly about Stephen Fleming as a coach.

"I think he's hugely experienced in not only the franchise world, dealing with international cricketers and dealing with Test cricket in particular."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fleming scored an unbeaten 66 in the first innings of the deciding Test as he captained New Zealand to a 2-1 series win in 1999, which saw England fall to last place in the rankings. Can he reverse their fortunes now as Test head coach?

Key also advocated refining an already-established approach to Test cricket, rather than making rash changes to the progress made by the Test team under Stokes and McCullum.

"This is a team now that has lost an entire generation of cricketers bar Joe Root," he said.

"We've had to rebuild the bowling attack. They've lost over a thousand wickets in the last few years and there is so much potential there.

"I believe Stephen Fleming is the best person to get the basics bowlers running and consistently hitting a line and length with all of that potential, all the attributes that they have.

"A refined approach is needed, not a change of approach."

Sports.title: Staveley, Ghodoussi company makes offer for West Ham stake
Sports.content:
Amanda Staveley and husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi's PCP Capital Partners have made an offer to buy a 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham.

Sky News' Mark Kleinman broke the news on Thursday that the couple were preparing a bid for a share that belongs to the family of the late David Gold. That offer has now gone in.

Sky News also reported that the club's current investors have first refusal on whether they would like to match the offer.

Sources close to the situation insisted to Sky News that Daniel Kretinsky, who raised his share in the club earlier this year, remains interested in a deal.

However, West Ham's ownership structure means he does not want to acquire all of the Gold-owned stake, which would make him the club's majority owner.

If there is an agreement with both parties, the Gold family will make a statement - not PCP - out of respect to all other shareholders.

Image: The family of the late David Gold currently own the 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham

Sky Sports News understands there will be no public comment from PCP for the same reason while negotiations are ongoing.

Staveley and PCP have held discussions with a number of Premier League clubs since leaving Newcastle, including Tottenham, but are now focused on the Hammers.

What has happened at West Ham so far this summer?

It has been a busy summer for West Ham after their relegation from the Premier League. There were questions over whether Nuno Espirito Santo would continue as head coach - and it was soon confirmed that he would.

Joint-chairman David Sullivan also stepped down after "serious historic allegations" emerged regarding his conduct, which he denies.

In terms of transfers, Matheus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville have been the biggest outgoings. But perhaps their best bit of business will be keeping captain Jarrod Bowen.

It was also reported on Friday that West Ham are in talks with Celtic for midfielder Arne Engels.

Sports.title: AC Milan and Italy legend Baresi dies aged 66
Sports.content:
Former AC Milan and Italy defender Franco Baresi has died aged 66.

The former Milan captain is widely regarded as one of the finest defenders in football history and spent his entire career with the club, playing 719 times in 20 seasons as a professional.

During that time Baresi won six Serie A crowns, with his first Scudetto coming as a teenager during the 1978-79 campaign and he lifted five further titles in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

The defender also won three European Cups, two Intercontinental Cups and four Italian Supercups during his career and his contributions to Milan saw the club retire the No 6 jersey.

On the international stage, Baresi was part of the Italy squad that won the World Cup in 1982, as well as featuring in the 1994 World Cup, which ended in a penalty-shoot-out defeat to Brazil in the final.

A post on the official Milan X account said: "The entire history of AC Milan is in tears following the passing of Franco Baresi.

"His example and integrity will be forever etched into the club's DNA, just as his iconic No 6 shirt is.

"The condolences AC Milan extends to Franco Baresi's family at such a difficult time are shared by every Rossonero, who feels this loss as their own."

In a further statement on the club website, Milan added: "Announcing the loss of someone who embodied the heart and soul of AC Milan, is incredibly difficult.

"But everyone at the club and all the Milanisti must live up to Franco Baresi's memory. We must be strong and gather every bit of energy, even at this saddest of times.

Image: Franco Baresi made 719 appearances for AC Milan

"We lost Franco only a few months after his last public appearance in a packed San Siro, at the Milan Winter Olympics opening ceremony, an event on the world stage he helped make unforgettable.

"In memory of Franco, we stand united, knowing he'll guide and push us throughout our Rossoneri journey. Forever. Because Baresi is forever."

Baresi made 81 appearances for Italy and Italian Football Federation president Giovanni Malago described him as an "extraordinary champion".

"Italian football has lost one of its legends," Malago said in a statement on the FIGC website.

"An extraordinary champion who wore only two jerseys throughout his career: AC Milan and the Azzurri. A romantic choice, one that earned him a place in the hearts of fans and millions of Italians."

AC Milan great Paolo Maldini - who spent 25 years with the club - described Baresi as the "greatest player" he played with.

Image: Baresi in action for Italy at the 1994 World Cup

Maldini said on Instagram: "You taught me to fight until my very last breath, and showed me the meaning of devotion to the jersey and the value of being a true leader. You did this through your example, every single day: few words, but countless actions.

"You protected me when I was a child, guided me as a young man, and inspired me as an adult. You were the greatest player I ever had the honour of playing with.

"Sending a warm embrace to your entire family, especially your wife Maura and your sons, Edoardo and Giannandrea.

"We will miss you, captain. But the light of your star will continue to guide us forever."

Former Italy goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon shared his memories of his debut for Parma competing against Baresi.

"On November 19, 1995, I made my Serie A debut against Milan. I was 17 years old, and on the other side was the captain of that team: Franco Baresi," Buffon posted on X.

"For a boy my age, finding myself on the field against champions like him was something incredible. From that day on, I had an even clearer understanding of what it meant to represent football with class, leadership, and respect.

"Goodbye Franco. Rest in peace."

Sports.title: Are Bournemouth set to strike defender gold again with Silva?
Sports.content:
There was a time when Antonio Silva's rise to the top appeared an inevitability. He was only 18 years old when he scored his first Champions League goal for Benfica in a 4-3 win over Juventus. He played at the 2022 World Cup for Portugal soon after that.

Since then, Silva has been linked with Europe's biggest clubs but it is Bournemouth who look set to sign him after agreeing a deal with Benfica. In truth, excluded from Portugal's squad this summer, his momentum has stalled. But, aged 22, there is time for this move to ignite his career.

Sure, there are grander destinations. But Bournemouth have emerged as one of the best recruiters of talent - proving themselves particularly adept at developing defenders. Silva is entitled to believe he can be the next to flourish for the Cherries.

Illia Zabarnyi and Dean Huijsen left for Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, respectively, just one year ago. Marcos Senesi has since moved to Tottenham. Silva is special enough to impress every bit as much as his predecessors on the south coast.

Speaking to Joao Nuno Fonseca, Silva's coach during his days with Benfica's development team, there is confidence that Bournemouth boss Marco Rose may have a gem in his hands. "Marco will not have any problems with him," Fonseca tells Sky Sports.

"Antonio is a very good person and the type of player that is easy to coach. He is very attentive. At Benfica, he listened to every detail that we gave him. He was very mature and that had a huge impact because it is difficult to reach the first team at Benfica."

Silva did that swiftly in part because of this mentality. "You give him feedback and he applies it directly in games. He understands everything." It made for a precocious talent in his teenage years, boasting an appreciation of time and space that belied his years.

"The key aspect of his game is his anticipation. Antonio reads the game really well. He is an anticipation-based defender rather than a reactive one. You see a lot of reactive centre-backs. He is not one of those. Antonio understands what will happen next."

Fonseca notes that the feet are good too. But it is the mind that saw Silva rise so quickly. "The technical skills are there, of course. But the key difference is understanding the game, in possession and out of possession. He knows what to do in those moments."

He praises the timing of his tackles. "He is one of the best in this technical aspect." And Silva's statistics show a defender who is aggressive in winning interceptions and aerial duels. Important qualities given that Bournemouth will expect him to be proactive.

In possession, Silva has the confidence to play forwards rather than simply recycling possession. "He is a modern ball-playing centre-back, very comfortable receiving the ball on either foot." There is variety to his use of the ball, chipped passes and more.

"One of the best things he has is the diagonal switches that he can do without looking," says Fonseca. "He is very, very talented at that." Expect that to be a significant feature at Bournemouth, who are looking to retain elements of Andoni Iraola's vertical approach.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch some of Bournemouth's best team goals under Andoni Iraola

It is why Rose is regarded as the continuity candidate. Iraola is on record as an admirer of the former Borussia Dortmund coach who honed his ideas in the Red Bull school where looking forward and pressing high up the pitch are viewed as non-negotiables.

"I think it will work fantastically because of the way Antonio reads situations," says Fonseca. "Marco will demand anticipation, a defender who looks for forward passes that break the lines and find those spaces in behind. Antonio will adapt very quickly."

The Premier League will still be different. Even after four years at Benfica - perhaps especially after four years at Benfica - it will feel a step up. "This move is fantastic for him because he will evolve and mature much more as a player in the Premier League."

Did he stay in Portugal too long? "He needed to move earlier, in my opinion," concedes Fonseca. "He stayed longer than expected. The decision that he made not to leave Benfica last year did not help him because he needed exposure to new experiences."

He explains: "We used to say at Benfica that while life starts at Benfica it does not end at Benfica. You need to move forward if you want to play on the world stage." But a season with Jose Mourinho, an unbeaten league campaign no less, is hardly a waste.

And Fonseca does not place too much weight on the decision of Roberto Martinez to omit him from the World Cup squad in favour of his Benfica team-mate Tomas Araujo. "The decision of the Portugal head coach does not mean he is not capable," he says.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look at the changes at Bournemouth as the club prepares for the Europa League

"Antonio is very capable and is completely ready to play in the Premier League. But it will be a different challenge for him. The challenge in England is week by week, not just waiting for the European games like he could at Benfica. The focus must be there."

Maybe there will be mistakes, lessons to learn even for a 22-year-old player who has already racked up an astonishing 181 appearances for Benfica in all competitions. "In the Premier League, the margin of error is very small. He needs to have that in mind."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at some of the best bits from Bournemouth's Rayan last season

But the overriding feeling is that this is an opportunity for Silva - and will be a coup for Bournemouth. "Antonio is a very complete centre-back who would help any team in the world. At this moment, it is going to be Bournemouth." A stepping stone to greatness?

"He has all the qualities to make the next move, but he cannot think like that. This move is the most important of his career. He will be in the Premier League. If he wants to move forward, he needs to focus completely and give 100 per cent for Bournemouth."

That is perhaps the lesson of Silva's journey so far. The hype came early. The next step is set to arrive later than expected. But at 22, there remains ample time for him to fulfil the promise that made him one of European football's most coveted young defenders.

Bournemouth have shown repeatedly that they can provide the perfect environment for talented centre-backs to take that next leap. Antonio Silva is now poised to have the opportunity to prove that his journey to the top remains on course. It is simply set to take a different route.

Sports.title: Infantino increasingly embattled after senior adviser resigns over World Cup sell-off plans
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino’s authority has been dealt a fresh blow after Carlos Cordeiro, one of his senior advisers, resigned with immediate effect in protest at proposals to sell a stake in the World Cup.

In the latest embarrassment for Infantino, who saw European FAs threaten to boycott future Fifa tournaments on Thursday, the former US Soccer chief Cordeiro criticised “a bad deal for football” and pointed out that the global governing body already sits on huge amounts of debt-free reserves.

“I cannot stand by while Fifa considers selling a stake in the World Cup,” Cordeiro said in his resignation statement. “I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally. It is a bad deal for Fifa’s member associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.”

Cordeiro has worked for Fifa since 2021 as senior adviser to Infantino. He also operated as a senior adviser to the White House taskforce on this summer’s World Cup.

In resigning he said Fifa “already has the financial capacity to provide [additional financial] support from existing resources”. He added that Fifa would be “mortgaging football’s future without any compelling justification” if it sold off a permanent stake.

In addition, Cordeiro questioned the lack of transparency in Fifa’s process. “Why this deal?” he asked. “Why now? What oversight exists? Who benefits? Was there a competitive process? What governance will be in place? What will investors ultimately gain, and at what cost to football?”

It adds to the pressure growing on Infantino and Fifa, which is facing calls for an urgent review of its governance after insisting that the planned World Cup sell-off will continue despite the threat of a boycott from all 55 European nations.

View image in fullscreen Carlos Cordeiro with Donald Trump and Gianni Infantin at the White House in 2018. Photograph: Evan Vucci/AP

In a strongly worded statement issued on Friday morning, the Asian Football Confederation backed Uefa’s and Concacaf’s opposition to the creation of a new commercial company, Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), saying it “cannot realistically achieve the necessary broad consensus and unity required to move forward”, and urging Fifa to “undertake an urgent review of its governance and decision-making framework”.

Fifa had attempted to double down on its position overnight, releasing a statement at 4am UK time saying “we will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA [member association] has the ability to express its vote based on facts,” but it is now clear Infantino is facing united opposition to his proposals from around the globe.

Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC constitute 143 of Fifa’s 211 members, so if their coalition remains united there is no prospect of Infantino getting the votes he needs. The 56-year-old’s position as Fifa president is also under threat for the first time since he was elected in 2016, unless he backs down quickly.

While stopping short of matching Uefa’s boycott the AFC went further than Concacaf in clearly stating that the FFE proposal should be dropped. “The AFC stands in solidarity with Uefa and Concacaf in expressing serious concerns over Fifa’s proposal to introduce private investment into Fifa’s flagship competitions and the decision-making process around FFE,” its statement read. “The fact that the situation has reached the point where the real possibility of a Fifa World Cup boycott has entered public discourse should concern everyone who cares about the future of our game.

“Football should never have been placed in such a position. Against this backdrop, and in light of the clear positions expressed by Uefa and Concacaf as well as the unprecedented divisions that have emerged across the football world, the AFC believes that the proposed FFE cannot realistically achieve the necessary broad consensus and unity required to move forward.

“The Fifa World Cup is the pinnacle of global football and derives its strength from the participation of all Confederations and the world’s leading football nations. Any proposal that risks undermining the unity and universal character of the competition must be reconsidered.”

The AFC echoed Uefa and Concacaf’s complaints about a lack of consultation from Fifa, making clear that it is not the first time confederations and the Fifa council have been excluded from major decisions, most notably hosting arrangements for the 2030 and 2034 World Cups.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The AFC sees this moment as a catalyst for strengthening institutional practices,” the statement continued. “While every Fifa MA must have the opportunity to consider and determine proposals affecting the future of world football, meaningful democracy is not measured solely by the opportunity to vote.

“It begins with transparent governance, timely consultation, informed deliberation and genuine participation throughout the decision-making process.

“The AFC calls upon Fifa to undertake an urgent review of its governance and decision-making framework to ensure that proposals of global significance are developed through proper consultation, meaningful engagement and appropriate oversight by Fifa’s statutory bodies.”

View image in fullscreen The hosts for the 2030 World Cup were announced at the Fifa Congress in Zurich in 2024. Photograph: Sergio Pérez/EPA

Fifa had attempted to blame media reporting for the widespread opposition to its scheme, but it is now clear that will not wash with most of its member associations.

“We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation,” a Fifa statement read. “Our planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports. We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA has the ability to express its vote based on facts.

“FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all Fifa member associations have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries, and that this does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of Fifa or football itself.

“Nobody is selling football. This is not something Fifa would ever entertain. Everyone has the right to express their opposition and to seek further clarification but no single entity can claim to represent all 211 MAs around the world. Each MA should be allowed to review the proposal and have a say in shaping their own future. These are the democratic principles of Fifa.”

If Fifa was to refuse to back down, the first step of the threatened European boycott would come at next month’s Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland, with senior Women’s World Cup qualifiers to follow in October.

Sports.title: Fifa rapidly accelerates plan to expand World Cup to 64 teams from 2030 tournament
Sports.content:
Fifa is pushing ahead with plans to expand the World Cup to 64 teams from 2030 and has opened a tender to research companies to assess the economic benefits on a hugely accelerated timescale.

In another twist during a week of astonishing revelations about the global governing body’s plans to reshape football, the Guardian has seen a “research brief” outlining a consultation process to assess the potential increase from the tournament’s current 48 teams. A period of just four weeks has been allocated for the successful party, which will be selected on 14 August, to analyse the proposed expansion. Fifa has required that the analysis is delivered by 11 September, indicating that a decision could be taken this year.

The study will raise further questions about Fifa’s governance just days after Gianni Infantino’s plans to sell off chunks of the World Cup to private investors were revealed. Uefa have already pledged to boycott future tournaments if Fifa do not shelve the scheme and there is likely to be further anger about the proposal to push forward with the 64-team expansion. In another indication of Fifa’s questionable governance it is understood that member associations were not informed about the tender before it was issued.

The invitation to tender explains Fifa is “considering the strategic implications of a possible expansion of the Fifa World Cup beyond the current format”. It asks for an impact assessment regarding tournament revenue and “the change through the eyes of the football ecosystem”. Agencies must submit their proposals for delivering the research by 7 August.

Infantino said earlier in July that an expansion was “an issue that will be looked at and discussed in the relevant committees after this World Cup”. Speculation had been growing in football’s corridors of power that Infantino would back such a move. It has been pushed by the South American governing body Conmebol whose president, Alejandro Domínguez, raised the idea again after the 2026 tournament had finished.

The 2030 World Cup will be jointly hosted by Morocco, Portugal and Spain but individual games are scheduled in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay to honour the tournament’s 100th anniversary. An expansion would make it likely that each of those countries could, as a minimum, host an entire group.

Uefa and Concacaf have been vocal in their opposition to expanding the World Cup further, and Fifa’s decision to push ahead regardless may intensify opposition to the world governing body.

Fifa’s research brief asks for analysis of how different stakeholders might support or resist any expansion, also requesting conclusions about player welfare, product quality and the international calendar. It instructs the relevant agency to identify “the estimated revenue the ticketing, sponsorship and media rights revenues that would be generated in total and specifically by the 64-team format”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Should Fifa confirm a switch to 64 teams it would mean a short lifespan for the 48-team format, which made its debut this summer. Between 1998 and 2022, 32 teams competed at each World Cup. Eyebrows will be raised about the short time allocated to assess a change of such gravity, which would also have implications for the number of suitable future hosts or regions.

Fifa were approached for comment.

Sports.title: Arsenal target Bruno Guimarães not on Newcastle’s flight to pre-season camp
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimarães was not on Newcastle’s flight to Murcia on Friday lunchtime as Eddie Howe’s former players prepared to meet their new head coach in southern Spain.

As Guimarães, who is believed to be in Brazil, appeared to inch closer towards a transfer to Arsenal, Matthias Jaissle was completing his managerial move from Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ahli. Howe’s successor is expected to arrive at the club’s pre-season training camp in the La Manga complex at some point this weekend.

By the time, shortly after midday, that the team’s charter plane took off for the Mediterranean, Newcastle had still to provide formal confirmation of Howe’s departure. It is understood they have been negotiating a financial settlement with their former manager in addition to payoffs for four key members of his backroom staff including the outgoing No 2, Jason Tindall.

Although Howe had told Newcastle of his intention to leave earlier this month, leaks surrounding Jaissle’s imminent appointment appeared to catch all parties by surprise. The players learned of Howe’s departure during a day off on Thursday but had the situation fully explained to them by Ross Wilson, the club’s sporting director, at the training ground before heading to Spain.

At the same time, Newcastle’s incoming German head coach was understood to be finalising a four-year contract at St James’ Park after an £8m compensation package was agreed with Al-Ahli. Jaissle is already in Europe after remaining in Portugal rather than returning to Jeddah with his squad following the conclusion of a pre-season training camp on the Algarve on Wednesday.

The 38-year-old former RB Salzburg manager is assembling his own backroom staff and now has only three weeks before his first Premier League season begins with a home game against Liverpool.

One of his first tasks will be to hold talks with Guimarães, regarding the Brazil midfielder’s future. Guimarães - who was very close to Howe - is booked on a flight to Spain on Sunday but there are suggestions he could opt to board a London-bound plane instead, should Arsenal offer Newcastle a sum in the region of £75m.

View image in fullscreen Joelinton could be on his way to the Saudi Arabia league this summer. Photograph: Siu Wu/EPA

Although Manchester United are exploring the possibility of attempting to sign Lewis Hall, Jaissle has reason to be more confident of keeping the influential left-back. Newcastle are said to be determined to retain one of their best young players but could be more receptive to any bid from Saudi Arabia for Joelinton. Guimarães’s compatriot is believed to be keen on a move to the Middle East.
