World.title: Fadiel Adams to appear before Madlanga Commission
World.content:
PRETORIA - Member of Parliament (MP) Fadiel Adams is expected to appear at the Madlanga Commission on 11 August.

The commission's spokesperson, Jeremy Michaels, confirmed that he was issued with a notice in October last year.

"This commission is a fact-finding mission; Yes, there are serious consequences which continue to flow from the work of the commission. But our job is to investigate allegations made by Nhlanla Mkhwanazi on 6 July last year. Those allegations have a profound implication on South Africa as a country and out communities..." Michaels said.

Michaels said that, as the commission goes about its work, it must consider its legal framework, which includes ensuring that the inquiry is fair and that it conducts its business in a manner that also gives those implicated persons a chance to respond to allegations against them.

Adams was arrested and released on R10,000 bail in May.

He faces charges of fraud and defeating the ends of justice.

The charges relate to alleged interference in high-profile political killing investigations.

World.title: Tyla drops Lagos show as South Africa, Nigeria row over immigration
World.content:
ABUJA - South African singer-songwriter Tyla has removed a scheduled show in Nigeria as tensions hamper relations between the two countries.



No reason was given for the change to her tour, but it came after some Nigerians on social media had called for a boycott of the show.



For months, South Africa has been the scene of protests -- some of them violent -- against African immigrants that demonstrators have blamed for crime, unemployment and a strain on public services.



Nigeria has become particularly outspoken on the issue, and tension was evident as high-ranking officials from Abuja and Pretoria met this week at the Nigerian Ministry of Foreign Affairs.



Tyla, known for hits such as "Water" and collaborations with American artists Cardi B and Travis Scott, had on Monday announced stops for a world tour for her second album, "A*POP", including Lagos, Nigeria's economic capital, as well as New York, Paris and Cape Town.



As of Friday morning, the Lagos leg -- which had been timed to coincide with Nigeria's year-end concerts frenzy season known as "Detty December" -- had been removed from the line-up on her website.



Representatives for Tyla did not immediately respond to a request for comment.



South Africa, one of the continent's most industrialised economies, has long been a magnet for both undocumented and documented immigrants.



But the nation is also saddled with high unemployment, weak social services and high crime, with immigrants being scapegoated for the country's broader social ills and government failures, analysts say.



South African police say at least four foreign nationals have been killed in attacks linked to the anti-migrant protests, though some African governments repatriating citizens have reported a higher toll.



More than 160,000 people have fled the country, according to an AFP tally based on figures from African governments repatriating their citizens, including about 1,500 Nigerians.



Pretoria's handling of the protests has been heavily criticised as anti-immigrant groups have burst into people's homes and dragged them into police vans.

AFP

World.title: Anglo nears end of De Beers sale, but Wanblad won't put price on it
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Anglo American CEO Duncan Wanblad has declined to confirm reports that De Beers could be sold for around $1 billion, saying the diamond business remains in a competitive sale process and that the final price will only be known once negotiations are complete.

"We are absolutely still in a competitive process," Wanblad said.

"We are nearing the end stages of that process, but it's not done until it's done. And these negotiations are ongoing at the moment."

In an exclusive interview with eNCA after Anglo American reported strong interim results, Wanblad said the company was in the advanced stages of divesting De Beers as part of its strategic overhaul, alongside the sale of its steelmaking coal and nickel businesses.

"So, I actually don't know realistically what the actual end price is going to be until we actually get through these negotiations."

He described the group's restructuring as being well on track, with a renewed focus on copper-led growth.

Asked whether a $1 billion valuation would be disappointing for a company once regarded as the crown jewel of Anglo American, Wanblad said there was "no sadness" or regret.

"There's no sadness here. There's no regret here. This is an excellent business. It is in the process of transition. It's being shaped and reshaped as market forces require it to do."

He acknowledged that the global diamond industry has faced significant pressure, particularly from the rise of lab-grown diamonds, forcing De Beers to adapt to changing market conditions.

Wanblad said De Beers remains an excellent business with a rich history but argued that valuations change over time and that new ownership would give the company the best opportunity to succeed in the evolving natural diamond market.

World.title: SAFA confirms Hugo Broos departure
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The South African Football Association (SAFA) has bid farewell to Bafana Bafana head coach Hugo broos as Bafana Bafana coach after a 5-year stint with the national team.

The Belgian leaves on a high after the team reached the World Cup knockouts for the very first time at this year's Fifa World Cup.

He also managed to lead Bafana to two Afcon qualifications, including a bronze-medal finish at the Ivory Coast competition in 2023.

World.title: They told him he'd never own a BMW. Now he does
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A Johannesburg security guard who was humiliated by customers and told he would never own a BMW has, in a remarkable twist of events, been gifted one.

A video that has since gone viral on social media shows two customers at a BMW dealership in Kempton Park mocking Teboho Kabayi after he asked them to specify where they were going inside the building.

"We can hire you to come and wash our cars. This is not your BMW. You must know your job," one of the men is heard telling Kabayi before adding that he would never own a BMW.

The video sparked widespread outrage, with social media users rallying behind Kabayi and praising the calm and professionalism he displayed during the confrontation.

World.title: Greek visa scheme gives Turks easier entry to islands in EU
World.content:
SAMOS - For Ikra Altumsek, and many other Turkish tourists, a visa-on-arrival scheme to visit several of Greece's Aegean islands has greatly simplified travel to this corner of the EU, previously off-limits without a hard-to-get Schengen visa.

"I think Samos was the perfect place to start," the 21-year-old university student said, wheeling her luggage alongside her mother as they waited for a ferry off the Greek island of Samos.

They were heading back to Kusadasi, on Turkey's Aegean coast after a sun-drenched vacation -- Altumsek's first trip abroad.

With its turquoise waters, quiet coves, traditional villages and waterfront restaurants, Samos -- situated just opposite the Turkish coast -- combines beaches and natural beauty with a rich cultural heritage, including ancient sites linked to Pythagoras, one of the most famous figures of the ancient Greek world.

Turkish-flagged boats carrying tourists are a constant presence along the waterfront, arriving and departing throughout the day, highlighting the steady flow of Turkish visitors to the Greek island.

"Τhe food is delicious. I have a 17-year-old son, and he keeps asking me, 'Mum, when are we going to Greece to eat?'," said Nevin Cagliguney, 51.

World.title: Cables and cooling bring AI windfall to Indian suppliers
World.content:
MUMBAI - At a bustling factory in western India, technicians work around the clock to turn glass into hair-thin fibre-optic strands destined for data centres powering the global artificial intelligence boom.

Indian manufacturers are cashing in on the AI infrastructure buildout by supplying cables, power systems and cooling equipment -- even as investors worry the country is falling behind in the race to develop the technology.

Analysts at Nomura describe it as a classic "picks and shovels" trade, a riff on how selling tools during a gold rush can earn people more than searching for the precious metal.

World.title: Casemiro keen to team with Messi at Miami
World.content:
MIAMI - Brazil star Casemiro sang the praises of new Inter Miami teammate Lionel Messi on Thursday, calling his former La Liga rival a "god of football."

"Of course if I'm here it's because of him and to help him and Inter Miami," the former Real Madrid midfielder said of the Argentine star who now captains Miami.

"I want to enjoy being with him, help him win, make him even greater. He's one of the gods, if not the god of football," Casemiro said as he was officially introduced by his new Major League Soccer club.

Casemiro, who arrived in MLS after a four-year stint at Manchester United, has already played his first minutes for the Herons in a 1-0 win over Montreal on Saturday.

Argentine star Messi sat that one out less than two weeks after his country's World Cup final defeat to Spain.

Casemiro said he was looking forward to playing alongside, rather than against, Messi, after their many battles in the Spanish league clasicos between Real Madrid and Barcelona.

“I know he’s impossible to stop. I never managed it," Casemiro said. "I always needed help from my teammates. And in the two training sessions I’ve already had with him, it’s already clear he’s impossible to stop."

Miami co-owner Jorge Mas beamed as he handed over Casemiro's pink jersey and denied there had been any impropriety in signing him despite MLS's investigation into possible "tampering".

The probe focuses on MLS's system of "discovery rights," which must be acquired by a cub before they can start negotiating with some high-profile players.

Casemiro was on LA Galaxy's list, and Mas said he had contacted the club before starting talks with the Brazilian.

"The rules are the rules, and we abided by those rules to the letter of the law," Mas said, saying Miami hadn't entered talks with Casemiro or his representatives before talking to the Galaxy.

World.title: Tiktoker Mauti changes plea, freed on bail in case involving Ruto's children
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

TikToker Hesbon Mauti was charged for posting a video threatening to kill and defile President William Ruto's children. [Nancy Gitonga, Standard]

TikToker Hesbon Mauti Thomas, accused of posting a video containing remarks threatening President William Ruto’s son George Ruto and daughter, has been released on a Sh5,000 cash bail after changing his plea to not guilty.

Mauti appeared before Milimani Principal Magistrate Geoffrey Onsarigo on Friday, July 31, 2026, where the charge of offensive conduct conducive to breaches of the peace was read afresh to him.

The accused, who had initially pleaded guilty to the charge on Thursday, changed his plea after his lawyer Cliff Ombeta applied for the matter to be reopened and for the charge to be read again.

The court allowed the application, after which Mauti denied the charge and pleaded not guilty.

According to the charge sheet, Mauti is accused of posting a video on June 25, 2026, through his TikTok account PROVIDENT@bonifaceaminga, containing remarks that prosecutors say were likely to cause a breach of the peace.

The charge sheet alleges that Mauti altered words in the video to make remarks targeting President Ruto’s son George Ruto and his daughter, while demanding that their parents be paid Sh2 million.

Mauti is charged with offensive conduct conducive to breaches of the peace contrary to Section 94(1) of the Penal Code, Chapter 63 of the Laws of Kenya.

After denying the charges, his defence team told the court that Mauti is a young man and a law student at Chuka University whose fees are paid by a church.

The lawyers further informed the court that Mauti is an orphan and has no parents to assist him in securing his release, asking the court to grant him a lenient cash bail.

“We are looking at the charges and when we look at it and the consequences that come from that, and if it goes on this particular way we know what the sentence is and what the consequences are. The court has got the right before passing the sentence to be able to reconsider when he changes his plea,” his lawyers told the court.

The defence also told the court that they had advised Mauti that the earlier position he had taken by pleading guilty carried serious consequences and offered to represent him in the matter.

The prosecution did not oppose his release on bail.

Magistrate Onsarigo granted Mauti a cash bail of Sh5,000 and directed him to provide one contact person.

The matter will be mentioned on August 18, 2026, for pre-trial directions.

World.title: Ruto calls for national dialogue to shape Kenya's vision
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Ruto said recent economic reforms had laid a stronger foundation for future growth. [File, Standard]

President William Ruto has invited Kenyans to take part in what he described as the country's most significant national conversation since the adoption of the 2010 Constitution, saying the discussions will help chart Kenya's next long-term development agenda.

Speaking on the country's development trajectory, the President said the conversation should move beyond partisan politics and election cycles to focus on a shared national vision.

"I invite every Kenyan to what I believe will become the most consequential national conversation since the adoption of our Constitution in 2010," Ruto said.

"A national conversation about Kenya's development. This conversation must rise above politics, transcend electoral cycles and unite us around a shared destiny."

The President acknowledged that while Vision 2030 had set an ambitious goal of transforming Kenya into an upper-middle-income country by 2030, the country remains off course to achieve that target.

"Vision 2030 set a target of Kenya becoming an upper-middle-income country by 2030. So far, we are off target. This is not a criticism of Vision 2030, nor is it a reason for disappointment; rather, it is an opportunity to learn from our successes proudly, reflect with honesty on where we have fallen short, and define together Kenya's next long-term vision," he said.

At the same time, Ruto announced that the government will formally launch a nationwide conversation on August 12 to develop Kenya's next long-term development blueprint as Vision 2030 nears its end.

"Accordingly, on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, we shall formally launch the National Conversation on Kenya's Future Beyond Vision 2030; the most consequential exercise in national reflection and public participation since the promulgation of our Constitution in 2010," he stated.

Ruto said recent economic reforms had laid a stronger foundation for future growth, citing improvements in key macroeconomic indicators.

"We have stabilized our currency, inflation has fallen, borrowing costs have declined, and investor confidence has returned," he said. "Last year Kenya attracted a record $3.2 billion in foreign direct investment, more than double the amount recorded in 2022."

He added that Kenya's improving investment climate had earned international recognition.

"The 2025 IMD World Competitiveness Ranking placed Kenya as the most competitive economy in Africa, reflecting the confidence our reforms have restored," Ruto said.

At the same time, Ruto also highlighted the establishment of the National Infrastructure Fund and the Sovereign Wealth Fund, saying the two institutions would help finance strategic investments while safeguarding the country's wealth for future generations.

According to Ruto, Kenya must now confront difficult questions about its development path to unlock its full potential.

"The question we must ask ourselves candidly and honestly is why other nations have fulfilled so much of their potential while we have repeatedly fallen short. What must we now do differently to ensure that the next chapter of Kenya's development story is fundamentally different from the last?" he posed.

He urged all Kenyans to help shape a new long-term national vision, saying the country's future depends on collective commitment rather than political divisions.

World.title: Lawyer seeks orders to suspend court boycott
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Advocate Adrian Kamotho argues that LSK's actions create the impression that court orders can be overturned through a boycott. [File, Standard]

A city lawyer has moved to the High Court seeking conservatory orders to suspend the Law Society of Kenya's (LSK) ongoing targeted boycott of judges and judicial officers.

In a petition filed under a certificate of urgency, Advocate Adrian Kamotho has sued LSK led by President Charles Kanjama, over its nationwide and targeted court boycott of Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Philomena Mwilu and other judges, arguing that the action is unconstitutional, undermines judicial independence and denies litigants access to justice.

"The LSK's actions create the impression that lawful court orders can be overturned through a boycott, setting a dangerous precedent to the rule of law and thereby undermining the proper administration of justice," Kamotho states in the petition.

The lawyer has named the Judicial Service Commission (JSC), Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Mwilu, several Supreme Court, High Court and Environment and Land Court judges, Court of Appeal Judge Sankale Ole Kantai, Kibera Chief Magistrate Stella Atambo and the Kenya Magistrates and Judges Association as interested parties in the case.

He is seeking orders to immediately suspend the implementation of the LSK's targeted boycott announced through statements and operational guidelines issued on July 17, July 20 and July 22, 2026, pending the hearing and determination of the petition.

"Pending the hearing and determination of this Petition, the court be pleased to issue a conservatory order restraining the LSK, whether by itself, its Council, officers, agents or any person acting under its authority, from implementing, enforcing or giving effect to the targeted boycott," Kamotho seeks.

According to the petition, the targeted boycott, which commenced on July 23, directs advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before judges listed by the LSK.

East Africa Law Society president Ramadhan Abubakar Mukira addresses the media on the court boycott outside the Supreme Court of Kenya in Nairobi on July 22, 2026. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

Lawyers are also required to seek adjournments, transfers or recusals of matters regardless of their clients' instructions.

"The Respondent has directed advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before the listed judges and judicial officers," Kamotho states.

He adds: "Advocates appearing before the targeted judges and judicial officers have been directed to seek the transfer, recusal or adjournment of pending proceedings, irrespective of their clients' instructions, the circumstances of the individual case or the applicable legal principles."

Kamotho further claims the society has threatened disciplinary action against judges, judicial officers and advocates who decline to implement the boycott.

"The LSK has further directed that any judge, judicial officer or advocate who declines to facilitate the boycott be reported to it for 'appropriate action,' including possible complaints before the Judicial Service Commission and such further action as its Council may deem necessary," he says.

According to the petition, every day the boycott remains in force exposes court users to delayed justice and unnecessary hardship.

"Every day that the targeted boycott remains operative exposes litigants and court users to adjournments, disruption of part-heard proceedings, expiry of interim protection measures, prolonged detention, additional expense and denial or delay of access to justice," Kamotho argues.

He also faults the LSK for allegedly including the late Supreme Court Judge Mohammed Ibrahim in its list of judges affected by the boycott.

"The targeted list of judges includes Hon. Justice Mohammed Ibrahim (deceased), demonstrating unconscionable casualness on the part of the LSK and apparent failure to verify elementary material facts before imposing measures of such gravity," the petition states.

Kamotho contends that the boycott creates an unlawful mechanism for exerting pressure on judges outside the constitutional framework.

He argues that the dispute raises fundamental constitutional questions, including whether the LSK has the legal authority to organise an indefinite boycott, compel advocates to withhold legal services from clients and determine which judicial functions judges may perform.

He maintains that the boycott threatens litigants' constitutional rights to equality before the law, access to justice, legal representation and a fair hearing, particularly in urgent and criminal matters.

In his supporting affidavit, Kamotho says advocates have been placed in an impossible position by the LSK's directives.

"The directions therefore place advocates in an immediate and irreconcilable conflict between their lawful professional duties and the Respondent's threatened enforcement measures," he says.

He further says litigants are innocent parties caught in an institutional dispute.

"The practical burden of the boycott consequently falls upon litigants and court users who are strangers to the institutional dispute forming the alleged basis of the boycott," he states.

Kamotho insists the conservatory orders sought are intended only to preserve uninterrupted court operations and judicial independence pending determination of the constitutional petition, arguing that the public interest favours continued access to courts and legal representation rather than disruption of judicial proceedings.

The petition is pending directions and hearing.

World.title: Ruto: Government will deal firmly with criminals
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto arrive for the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County on July 26, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has declared war on individuals who involve in violence, destruction of property and political intimidation.

He said people initially participated in anti-government demonstrations have "graduated from protesters to goons."

Speaking on Sunday during the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County, the President said the government would no longer tolerate criminality disguised as peaceful protests.

"They have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere," Ruto said.

President Ruto maintained that safeguarding peace remains the government's top priority while ensuring all leaders have the freedom to campaign without fear of violence or intimidation.

He argued that Kenya had previously experienced a rise in criminal activities, but efforts to deal with those responsible had been complicated by differing opinions over how security agencies should respond.

"We had a small problem earlier when crime issues increased and we did not agree on how to tackle the crime as a nation because sometimes we used to defend those who were hurting people and destroying property. We could say that they should not be touched because they are our children," he said.

"But now we have seen the repercussions because they have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere."

Ruto said the government had resolved to restore law and order, insisting that criminal gangs would not be allowed to disrupt peace under the cover of political demonstrations.

"We have agreed to discipline all the goons, and no one will be allowed to propagate crime and disrupt peace in our country," he said.

The President also sought to reassure Kenyans that the country would remain peaceful as preparations begin for the 2027 General Election, saying his administration would do everything possible to safeguard stability before, during and after the polls.

"I agree that peace is not negotiable. All of us, irrespective of who we are, our persuasion, our political leaning and whatever it is that we believe in, we must have a peaceful nation," Ruto said.

"I want to assure you as the people of Kenya that we will have peaceful elections next year because elections come and go, but this nation must remain firm, united and stable. We shall do everything possible to ensure that this nation is stable."

At the same time, the Head of State emphasized that every political leader should be free to campaign and present their agenda without intimidation, provided they conduct their activities peacefully.

"Every leader should be given a chance to give their opinion. Those who have an agenda or plan should be given an opportunity to explain it to Kenyans. Even those who have nothing should be given a chance to speak, but all of us must ensure that we are peaceful," he said.

The President's remarks come against the backdrop of heightened political tensions and growing concerns over violent disruptions at political gatherings.

Recent incidents, including the Ol Kalou by-election in Nyandarua County, saw armed gangs disrupt voting and terrorize residents, prompting renewed debate over the role of criminal groups in Kenya's political landscape.

The government has faced criticism from sections of the opposition, who have accused state agencies of sponsoring the gangs.

However, Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has rejected the claims, instead alleging that the groups were mobilized by allies of former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua. Murkomen has pledged decisive action against those behind the violence, regardless of their political affiliation.

World.title: Ruiru 'Vampire' arrested after lodging incident with woman
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The suspect was arrested after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents. [Courtesy, X]

Police in Ruiru have arrested a 35-year-old man believed to be behind a series of bizarre and violent attacks in which residents were robbed and bitten, leaving several victims nursing serious injuries.

The suspect, identified as Githaiga from Mugutha, was arrested on Saturday afternoon after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents.

Ruiru Sub-County Police Commander Charles Kibathi confirmed the arrest, saying the suspect was heavily intoxicated at the time and had allegedly bitten a woman who was with him, tearing part of her lower lip.

"The suspect and the female victim were taken to hospital for treatment as investigations continue," Kibathi said.

He added that detectives are investigating whether the suspect is linked to the earlier attacks reported in Ruiru and neighbouring Gitothua Ward.

However, some residents defended the suspect, claiming the altercation that led to the woman being bitten stemmed from a disagreement after the two emerged from a room where they had spent the night.

Kibathi assured residents that police are pursuing all leads to establish whether other people may have been involved in the attacks and pledged to intensify security operations in the area.

The arrest follows weeks of panic after several residents reported being attacked by a man who allegedly robbed victims before violently biting them.

Among the latest victims was Daniel Ndegwa, who was attacked on July 11 at about 9 p.m. while walking to a nearby shopping centre. Ndegwa told police he was confronted by a man demanding his mobile phone before a struggle ensued. During the confrontation, the attacker bit his finger and injured his left hand. A friend who was accompanying him was also reportedly bitten.

Residents said the attacks had become increasingly frequent throughout July, forcing many people to avoid walking outside after dark.

In one of the most shocking incidents, another victim reportedly suffered severe facial injuries after the attacker allegedly bit off part of his cheek.

The incidents have disrupted normal life in Ruiru town and Gitothua Ward, with many residents opting to remain indoors in the evenings for fear of being attacked.

Residents, led by Severino Githinji, criticized the security situation, saying families have been living in constant fear and called for increased police patrols and swift action against those responsible.

Police said the first official report of the attacks was made on July 11, and investigations are ongoing to establish whether the arrested suspect is responsible for all the reported incidents.

Kibathi urged members of the public to continue cooperating with investigators as detectives work to unravel the full circumstances surrounding the attacks.

World.title: Murkomen: Police no longer rely on Gachagua's 'gossip'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen during the official launch of the Multi-biometric Identification System (MBIS) and handover ceremony of ANSI National Accreditation Board Certificate at DCI Headquarters on July 23, 2026. [NPS]

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has accused former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua of spreading falsehoods, saying technology-driven policing has replaced "gossip-based" investigations.

Speaking during the handover of the ANSI National Accreditation Board certification to the Forensic Evidence Management Unit and the launch of the Multi-Biometric Identification System at the Directorate of Criminal Investigations headquarters on Thursday, Murkomen said the country has shifted from outdated investigative methods to science-based policing.

"We are moving away from gossip-based collection of evidence to science. I saw an impeached former leader claiming he is well connected to police officers and receives gossip every day because he is not busy unlike the President," said Murkomen.

He said the biometric system will strengthen investigations through science and technology, making unofficial information unnecessary.

"That is an old style of collecting evidence. We now have a modern police service driven by science and technology. We do not need his gossip to run the National Police Service," he observed.

Murkomen claimed the technology would make it harder for unsuitable individuals to rise through public office.

"If these systems had been in place many years ago, people like Gachagua would not have survived the system as habitual offenders until he slipped through to become Deputy President. Such things will never happen again with this technological advancement," said Murkomen.

The Interior CS defended Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja, saying he has the government's confidence and has discharged his duties professionally.

"I have full support and faith in the leadership of the Inspector General. He has carried out his duties with dignity, honour and respect for the citizens of Kenya and his office," noted Murkomen.

Murkomen also rejected Gachagua's criticism of police leadership, arguing that Kenya is recording fewer cases of terrorism, banditry, robbery and other crimes.

"There has never been a period when Kenya has recorded fewer incidents of terrorism, banditry, robberies and other crimes. Our security agencies are working together and have improved security," he said.

He also criticised remarks attributed to Gachagua warning tourists against visiting Kenya, saying they damage the country's reputation.

"For anyone to stand out there and say Kenya is not safe and tourists should not come to our country is very embarrassing," explained Murkomen.

Murkomen dismissed claims that 68 women were raped by police officers during the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election, urging anyone with evidence to report the matter to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority or the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights.

"If those incidents occurred, they should be reported so those responsible can be held accountable. If not, those making such reckless statements must also be held accountable," said Murkomen.

He accused Gachagua of making the allegations out of political desperation.

"I know why Gachagua speaks the way he does. It is because of desperation. Knowing that he cannot hold any office again in Kenya and can never be President of this republic, he wants to take the entire nation, including the economy, down the drain with himself. We will not allow that," he said.

Murkomen also urged media organisations to challenge politicians they host instead of allowing false claims to go unchecked.

"We should not feed Kenyans with lies. I want to tell media houses that when you invite such reckless human beings, please carry with you a lie detector. Otherwise you are going to mislead the people of Kenya and drive bad behaviour in our country," said Murkomen.

He maintained that intelligence gathering within the National Police Service follows lawful procedures and dismissed claims that private individuals receive confidential police briefings outside official channels

World.title: Gachagua: Why Ruto will not steal the 2027 General Election
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Righathi Gachagua during a live interview with KTN at his Karen home, Nairobi. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has claimed that President William Ruto will not be able to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 General Election, arguing that Kenyans have become more vigilant in protecting their votes.

Speaking during a live interview with KTN from his Karen residence, the former Deputy President said the recent Ol Kalou by-election had provided opposition supporters with a blueprint on safeguarding the electoral process.

"Voting is not enough; you vote and protect the vote. We now have a template from the Ol Kalou by-election," Gachagua said.

He urged Kenyans to remain vigilant during the next General Election, saying the alleged intimidation witnessed in Ol Kalou had failed to influence voters.

"They tried intimidating the people of Ol Kalou, but they did not succeed. We are celebrating what happened, and people from across the country are calling to benchmark on how it worked," he said.

Gachagua also questioned the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)'s ability to conduct a free and fair election, accusing the electoral body of failing to condemn alleged voter suppression and bribery during the Ol Kalou by-election.

"IEBC has not even condemned the wrongs that happened during the by-election in Ol Kalou. We lost two people who were actually protecting our votes," he alleged.

The DCP leader further renewed his criticism of President Ruto, accusing him of betraying voters from the Mt Kenya region despite earlier warnings.

According to Gachagua, the outcome of the Ol Kalou by-election should serve as a warning to the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He maintained that the by-election demonstrated that Kenyans could no longer be intimidated by the State and described the result as a preview of what to expect in the next national polls.

Gachagua also revisited the Mbeere North by-election, alleging that DCP lost because of widespread voter bribery, intimidation of elderly voters and failure by the party to adequately protect its votes.

"We lost the Mbeere North by-election because we didn't protect our votes properly. There was also massive voter bribery, and those who participated were allegedly given the balance of their bribe after showing a photo of whom they had voted for," he claimed.

The former Deputy President further argued that DCP would have secured an even larger victory in Ol Kalou were it not for what he described as voter suppression and police intimidation.



More to follow...

World.title: Charles Owino appointed as Government Spokesperson
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

President William Ruto has promoted Government Spokesperson Isaac Mwaura in a fresh round of changes within the Executive, while also making nominations to key constitutional commissions and statutory bodies.

In an Executive Order issued on Tuesday, Chief of Staff and Head of Public Service Felix Koskei said the Public Service Commission had approved promotions and redeployments affecting senior government officials.

Under the changes, Mwaura was promoted and redesignated as the Head of the Office of Diversity, Inclusion and Disability Rights in the Executive Office of the President.

Charles Owino Wahong’o was redeployed from the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy to the Executive Office of the President, where he will serve as Acting Head of Government Communications.

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

At the same time, Ruto also nominated new office holders to key constitutional commissions and approved changes within the senior ranks of the Executive in a fresh round of appointments aimed at filling vacancies and strengthening government institutions.

Among the nominees is Dr. Duncan Ojwang Oburu, who has been picked to serve as the Chairperson of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA).

Ruto also nominated Ms. Antonina Lentoijoni and former Kenya National Union of Teachers (KNUT) Secretary-General Wilson Sossion as members of the Teachers Service Commission (TSC).

Ms. Flora Mutua was nominated as a member of the Public Service Commission (PSC).

In the nominations, Ruto also named seven individuals to serve on the Intergovernmental Relations Technical Committee (IGRTC), subject to ratification by the National and County Government Co-ordinating Summit in accordance with the Intergovernmental Relations Act.

The nominees are Wilson Kuria Thuita (Murang'a), Silvya C. Apaa (Busia), Ahmed Kanyara Bishar (Wajir), Pascalyne Ntang'enoi Kimiriri (Laikipia), Ken Riaga (Migori), Evalyn Chepkirui Aruasa (Nakuru) and Mary Nanjala Kilobi (Nairobi).

World.title: Video: Amr Diab tops trending charts half an hour after releasing ‘Lola El Banat’ music video
World.content:
Renowned singer Amr Diab topped the trending charts on “X” (formerly Twitter) just half an hour after releasing the music video for his song “Lola El Banat.”

The artist released the official music video for “Lola El Banat” on his official YouTube channel and digital platforms, following the song’s massive success since its initial release as part of his latest album, Habetek. The track has dominated streaming charts and been widely shared by fans.

Directed by Tarek Al Arian, the video features a vibrant, summer atmosphere that complements the song’s fast-paced rhythm, delivering a visually energetic experience. “Lola El Banat” stands out as one of the highlight tracks from the album; it is written by Mostafa El Prince, composed by Amr Diab, arranged by Ahmed Ibrahim, and mixed/digitally mastered by Amir Mahrous.

Habetek marks the 36th album in Diab’s 40-year career.

The 12-track album features collaborations with a prominent group of lyricists, including Ayman Bahgat Kamar, Tamer Hussein, Mostafa Hadouta, Rozam, Amir Teima, Mostafa El Prince, and Menna El Kiey.

The album’s composers include Amr Mostafa, Mohamed Yehia, Ehab Abdel Wahed, Nader Nour, and Adham Bahgat Kamar, alongside arrangers Ahmed Ibrahim, Adel Hakki, and Osama El Hendy.

World.title: Egypt prepares for August heatwave with temperatures expected to peak at 47°C
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) has warned of the upcoming weather conditions and the continuation of high temperatures. This coincides with the arrival of the Indian Seasonal Low—nicknamed the “Summer Monster”—which significantly increases humidity levels, thereby heightening the sensation of heat.

The EMA announced the weather forecast for August 2026, predicting extremely hot conditions during the day across most regions, and hot, humid weather along the northern coast. At night and during early morning hours, the weather will remain moderately warm and humid.

Humidity levels will continue to rise, making temperatures feel 2 to 4 degrees Celsius hotter than the actual shaded readings. Weather maps warn of fog formation between 4:00 AM and 8:00 AM on select roads connecting to and from northern parts of the country, passing through Greater Cairo, the Canal Cities, Central Sinai, and Northern Upper Egypt, with fog potentially turning dense at times on certain routes.

Additionally, intermittent winds are expected from Friday through Tuesday across parts of the Northwestern Coast, Greater Cairo, Lower Egypt, and Southern Upper Egypt.

According to the EMA’s statement, maximum temperatures in Greater Cairo and Lower Egypt will range between 37°C and 39°C, with the apparent “feels-like” temperature peaking at 42°C on Sunday—the height of this extreme heatwave. Meanwhile, Southern Upper Egypt will record the highest overall temperatures during this period, with actual maximums ranging from 43°C to 46°C and feels-like temperatures reaching up to 47°C.

World.title: Egypt imposes departure fees on travelers
World.content:
President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi ratified Law No. 148 of 2026 amending certain provisions of Law No. 147 of 1984 concerning the imposition of a fee for the development of state financial resources. The law was published in the Official Gazette, taking effect on the day following its publication date.

The amendments replace the texts of items (5) and (19) under Article 1 of the original law, stipulating a fee collection of LE 100 upon departing the territory of the Republic.

Exemptions

The law exempts both Egyptian and foreign drivers of public passenger and cargo transport vehicles, as well as personnel operating on cross-border truck lines.

Cement production fee

The amendments also impose a fee of LE 35 per ton of produced cement across all types, obligating cement manufacturing plants to remit the due fees directly to the Egyptian Tax Authority.

World.title: Egypt to launch new e-visa system in August to hit 30 million tourism target
World.content:
Egypt is set to roll out a state-of-the-art electronic visa system, a strategic move aimed at sharpening the competitiveness of its tourism sector and accelerating national plans to welcome 30 million tourists by 2030.

Tourism and Antiquities Minister Sherif Fathy announced that the upgraded framework will transition from traditional visa stickers to dynamic QR codes. Speaking in a television interview, Fathy confirmed that the official launch is slated for August following the completion of final technical preparations.

Currently, travelers from 118 nationalities can obtain visas on arrival. The revamped system, however, will allow tourists to generate their digital entry passes up to 48 hours before departure—either via the official online platform, foreign travel agencies, or local host operators in Egypt.

Upon arrival, passengers will be able to finalize entry using electronic payment methods or self-service kiosks at Egyptian airports, RT Arabic reported.

Fathy clarified that the system distinguishes between visa-on-arrival and pre-issued e-visas, enabling visitors to complete most paperwork before stepping onto a plane and significantly cutting down waiting times at Egyptian ports of entry.

As part of broader efforts to expand visa flexibilities, the minister noted that adding new eligible nationalities involves careful evaluation across security, tourism metrics, and diplomatic reciprocity in coordination with relevant state authorities. He highlighted that between 170 and 180 nationalities currently benefit from various entry accommodations into Egypt.

To keep pace with anticipated growth, Egypt is aggressively expanding its hospitality footprint. The country’s current capacity stands at approximately 235,000 hotel rooms, with tens of thousands more in the pipeline. Industry projections suggest Egypt will need to reach 500,000 rooms to comfortably support its target of 30 million annual visitors by 2030.

These initiatives form a cornerstone of a sweeping government effort to revitalize tourism—a primary engine of foreign currency earnings and economic growth for the nation.

World.title: 18 dead, thousands massed: Inside the growing crisis at the Morocco–Spain border
World.content:
At least 18 migrants have died while attempting to reach the city of Ceuta, where Spain deployed military forces after thousands of people crossed the border with Morocco and streamed into the small Spanish enclave.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is expected to join Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska on a visit to Ceuta on Friday, as Rachid Sbihi—who heads a local association representing Civil Guard officers—described the situation as a “serious humanitarian crisis.”

“People are still coming in; the reinforcements that arrived are tasked solely with assisting the injured and supporting other humanitarian efforts,” Sbihi said, adding that “thousands of migrants—including unaccompanied children—have been left homeless, sleeping in parks and on sidewalks, while others wander the streets aimlessly,” characterizing the situation as “chaotic.” Sbihi clarified that many of the 18 victims drowned, while others were killed in stampedes while trying to cross the fence extending along the breakwater at Tarajal beach.

On Thursday, video footage showed crowds of people—the majority of them Moroccans—walking from the breakwater area at Tarajal beach toward local roads. Although most appeared to be young men, the crowds also included families accompanied by women and small children.

Some chanted “Viva España!” in front of a freelance photographer working for the Associated Press (AP), who observed crowds gathered on the Moroccan side of the border attempting to cross into Ceuta, as well as other individuals walking from Ceuta back toward Morocco in an attempt to return.

It remains unclear what prompted such a large number of migrants to cross into Ceuta, and Moroccan authorities have not issued any public statement regarding these crossings, nor has the Moroccan Ministry of the Interior responded to requests for comment.

Although the arrival numbers had been on the rise, the underlying reasons remain unclear.

This escalation at the border between Spain and Morocco follows a massive influx of migrants—most of whom attempted to reach the small Spanish enclave by swimming—on Wednesday.

Authorities in Ceuta had previously attributed this surge in numbers to a ruling issued by the Spanish Supreme Court earlier this month, which prevents authorities from immediately deporting migrants arriving by sea without following due legal process. This ruling does not apply to migrants who enter Spain by land, including those who scale the border fence; however, some activists in Morocco doubted that this judicial decision was the primary driver behind the wave, asserting that most migrants were unaware of such legal rulings.

The repercussions of this chaos extended to Italy, another major destination for migrants. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni threatened to suspend the Schengen Agreement (which allows free movement across open borders) with Spain in order to defend her country’s borders and ensure public safety, despite Italy not sharing a land border with Spain.

Spain serves as a primary entry point for migrants arriving in Europe, whether they are seeking better economic opportunities or fleeing violence in their home countries. To reach the city of Ceuta on the North African coast, migrants often swim from the Moroccan town of Fnideq, covering about 3 miles (5 kilometers) to reach Spanish territory, while others attempt to cross from the nearby town of Belyounech, where the distance is shorter.

World.title: Geographical analysis reveals attack scenarios on Egypt’s Damietta Port
World.content:
The fire that broke out aboard two FSRUs (Floating Storage and Regasification Units) at Damietta Port was not merely a passing incident; rather, it quickly turned into a regional event that drew worldwide attention—especially after the Cabinet announced that preliminary investigations indicated the fire resulted from a drone attack, while simultaneously emphasizing that investigations remain ongoing and that no official accusations have been directed at any state or organization.

While no group has claimed responsibility for the attack, the incident has opened the door to broad questions regarding its security and political implications, as well as its degree of connection to the military escalation unfolding across the Middle East—particularly given that the attack targeted a facility directly linked to Egyptian energy security and gas flows in the Eastern Mediterranean.

Damietta Port: A Location Beyond Geography

Damietta Port sits on Egypt’s northern coast at the heart of the Eastern Mediterranean, a location that grants it exceptional significance as a crossroads for international shipping lanes and regional energy networks. The port’s importance is not limited to its function as a commercial hub; it also houses infrastructure dedicated to receiving and regasifying natural gas. This makes it an integral component of the energy system Egypt relies upon to meet domestic demand and reinforce its status as a regional gas trading hub.

Energy security studies indicate that facilities tied to gas production, reception, or processing have become, in recent years, among the most sensitive targets in conflict zones. Modern warfare has demonstrated that targeting energy infrastructure can achieve economic and political impacts that sometimes exceed the effects of striking traditional military sites.

Geographic Framework of the Incident

Geographically, Damietta Port enjoys a position relatively close to several Eastern Mediterranean nations, while separated by larger distances from other countries in the region. This location places the port within a complex geopolitical environment where international and regional interests concerning energy, navigation, and maritime security intersect.

Approximate direct distances to Damietta, according to the geolocation platform Google Earth, are as follows:

Israel: 250–450 km

Libya (Eastern Libya): 900–1,200 km

Syria: 550–750 km

Iraq: 950–1,200 km

Yemen: 1,700–2,200 km

Iran: 1,500–1,900 km

These figures vary slightly depending on the assumed launch point, yet they are sufficient to evaluate operational feasibility and raise the pressing question: where did it come from?

Israel

From a technical standpoint, the distance is very short—estimated at roughly 250–450 km—compared to the capabilities of most modern military drones. According to a research paper published by the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, Israel possesses strategic drones capable of executing long-range missions via satellite communications, with the average range of strategic aircraft estimated at around 1,000 km or more depending on the mission and control system.

However, the political analysis is far more complex; Netanyahu’s clear desire to expand the circle of conflict has been reflected in public moves, actions, and statements, even though Al Arabiya TV reported that the Israeli military denied targeting the port.

Libya and Syria

Damietta Port lies approximately 700–1,200 km from eastern Libya—a distance within the range of certain long-range drones. However, one cannot speak of a unified “state capability” given that the available drones vary depending on the controlling faction and the foreign operator, though most operationally deployed drones fall within the 150–300 km range.

As for Syria, it sits roughly 550–750 km from Damietta Port, but the flight path would require crossing or nearing heavily monitored airspace, significantly increasing operational complexity.

Iraq

The distance between Damietta Port and Iraqi airspace is estimated at 950–1,200 km, making reach possible only through long-range drones. According to a recent study by the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS), Iraq is not classified among nations possessing an advanced domestic drone manufacturing or national program—unlike Iran, Israel, and Turkey—and capability developments in the region rely primarily on imports or foreign support rather than local R&D.

Furthermore, operational use within Iraq is heavily tied to factions supported by Iranian technology rather than the Iraqi military itself. As highlighted by the “Missile Threat” project—which monitors military activity, particularly Iranian drone capabilities in the region—certain Iraqi factions continue to maintain ties to Iranian-designed drones from the “Shahed” family, alongside reports detecting Iranian models inside Iraq.

Iran

The distance between Iran and Damietta Port is substantial, estimated at 1,500–1,900 km. Reaching the target would require extremely long-distance flights while maintaining strike precision, in addition to traversing or bypassing monitored air and maritime spaces belonging to multiple countries before reaching the port.

Iran possesses extensive long-range drone programs with average ranges spanning 1,200–2,000 km. However, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi issued media statements denying any targeting of Egypt, underscoring Tehran’s respect for Cairo’s sovereignty.

Yemen

The distance between Damietta Port and Yemen (specifically Houthi-controlled areas) represents the longest route, measuring roughly 1,700–2,200 km.

While the Houthis have claimed long-range attacks on previous occasions, reaching Damietta entails traversing a vast distance over the Red Sea, followed by the Suez Canal, or navigating alternative detour routes—a scenario that is far more operationally complex. Therefore, simply possessing a long-range drone does not automatically make this the most likely scenario. For its part, the Houthi-run Ministry of Foreign Affairs denied responsibility for the attack via the Yemeni news agency Saba.

What Has Egypt Announced?

In the initial hours, the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources announced that a fire had broken out aboard two vessels, confirming that emergency teams successfully contained the blaze, prevented its spread, and recorded zero casualties.

By yesterday morning, the Cabinet announced in a statement that preliminary investigations revealed the fire resulted from a drone attack. However, it emphasized that investigations remain ongoing and stopped short of attributing responsibility to any party—reflecting the authorities’ caution against preempting technical and security investigation outcomes.

The government also affirmed the continuation of measures aimed at safeguarding critical infrastructure and securing ports and energy-related facilities.

A Highly Complex Regional Context

The attack occurred at a time when the Middle East was witnessing escalating military and political tensions, accompanied by ongoing cross-border strikes across multiple regional theaters.

These developments have prompted several think tanks to warn that energy infrastructure has become increasingly vulnerable amid the expanding use of drones and long-range missiles in regional conflicts.

Meanwhile, regional security researchers believe that the expanding scope of conflict heightens the risk of energy facilities, ports, and civilian infrastructure facing indirect threats—even in countries not directly party to the conflicts—imposing additional challenges on critical infrastructure protection systems.

World.title: Egyptian fencing team defeats Israel to claim World Championship team bronze
World.content:
The Egyptian national sabre fencing team secured the bronze medal after defeating Israel with a score of 39–38 at the World Fencing Championships (Team Epee/Sabre) held in Hong Kong, marking a historic achievement.

The Pharaohs edged out their opponent 39–38 during the Senior World Championships hosted by Hong Kong from July 22 to 30.

The national team kicked off its campaign with a 44–33 victory over Portugal in the Round of 32, followed by a tight 36–35 win against Spain in the Round of 16.

Egypt then advanced to the semifinals after defeating Russia 45–35.

Although the team suffered a 41–32 loss to Kazakhstan in the semifinal round, they rallied to clinch the bronze medal by overcoming Israel 39–38 in the third-place match.

The Egyptian delegation is led by the President of the Egyptian Fencing Federation, Captain Tarek al-Hossainy, and the Director of National Fencing Teams, Ayman Ghoneim, who serves as administrative manager.

The medical staff includes Dr. Magdy al-Sabbagh as team physician, along with physical therapists Ahmed Abdel-Ghani and Ghada Atef.

Also accompanying the delegation is the Vice President of the Egyptian Fencing Federation, Ahmed Samir, upon an invitation from the International Fencing Federation (FIE) to attend the FIE Referees Commission meetings—in his capacity as Chairman of the African Fencing Confederation’s Supreme Referees Committee—as well as the IOC Safe Sport meetings held on the sidelines of the World Championship.

World.title: Amr Adib calls for ‘firm response’ to Damietta Port drone attack
World.content:
Egyptian TV host Amr Adib commented on the fire that broke out on two ships at Damietta Port following a drone strike, stressing that Egypt’s response to this breach must be firm and direct, RT Arabic reported.

In a post shared on his official X (formerly Twitter) account, Adib highlighted that the current situation demands a strict stance, writing: “Egypt’s must be strong, forceful, and clear. Those advocating for self-restraint should remain completely silent.”

He added: “Knowing the source of the drone is not impossible. A strike must be met with a harsher strike so we do not receive more drones. This is a case of self-defense, and no one can stop you or blame you under any law. Anyone who harbors ill intentions toward Egypt must pay a heavy price.”

Adib’s remarks follow an official statement issued by the Egyptian Cabinet, which confirmed that the fire aboard the two vessels at Damietta Port resulted from a drone strike, adding that no entity has claimed responsibility for the incident so far.

World.title: Copper Queens eye quarterfinals as Nigeria match looms
World.content:
The Copper Queens on Saturday night face defending champions Nigeria in their second Group C match of the ongoing 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) at the Al Madina Stadium in Rabat, Morocco. Kick off is at 22h00.

Zambia tackle Nigeria four days after thumping Egypt 6-0 in their opening Group C match. On the same night, the Super Falcons lost 3-2 to debutants Malawi.

Zambia top Group C with three points and a superior goal difference, while Malawi is second also on three points. Nigeria and Egypt are yet to open their accounts.

Victory over Nigeria will see Zambia advance to the quarterfinals with a game to spare.

Zambia coach Nora Häuptle said she is expecting Nigeria to be tough.

“Basically, we have a good mood in camp. Our opening game went well but we also know that the game against Nigeria will be completely different, so we keep our feet on the ground. We need to adjust against Nigeria. We are good to go tomorrow,” Häuptle told a pre-match media conference.

She said Zambia remains focused ahead of the match.

“We know that Nigeria needs to win this game or else they will be out. We are aware of Nigeria’s strength. We are fully prepared and expect Nigeria to come with their full stamina. We are focused on ourselves, we have a clear plan, and we discussed today how to execute our plan. My team Zambia never plays for a draw; our nature is to win. We can also surprise Nigeria. I have a lot of confidence in my team that we bring our performance on point. Every game is a challenge,” Häuptle said.

Nigeria coach Justin Madugu branded the game against Zambia as a must win for the Falcons.

“We are aware that Zambia’s confidence will be boosted by their victory over Egypt. We will also not want to approach the game in the manner that we will not be defeated. We know what is at stake, it is a must win game,” Madugu said.

Zambia forward Rachael Kundananji said the Copper Queens are itching to face Nigeria.

“The morale in camp is high and the team is ready. We understand that it is not an easy task ahead. It won’t be an easy game. We are looking forward to the game, and we want to do our best. The team is fully prepared for the game. Winning this match will be good for the team and the entire nation,” Kundananji said.

The top four semi-finalists at WAFCON will earn automatic qualification to the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil.

The Copper Queens are aiming to better their 2022 WAFCON bronze medal achievement won under the late coach Bruce Mwape.

World.title: Chipata Hospital records, 2, 500 pregnancies, 20 Ectopic pregnancies
World.content:
Chipata Central Hospital recorded over 2,500 pregnancies in the first quarter of 2026, with 20 cases identified as ectopic pregnancies.

This was disclosed by Chipata Central Hospital Registrar in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Bwalya Phiri, during the Zaumoyo Health Programme .

Dr Phiri said the hospital continues to attend to a high number of women seeking antenatal services, with concerns around teenage pregnancies and late bookings.

He explained that an ectopic pregnancy occurs when a fertilized egg implants outside the uterus, commonly in the fallopian tube, and can be life-threatening if not managed early.

“Between January and March this year, we managed 22 cases of ectopic pregnancy. Most of them came in as emergencies,” he said.

Dr Phiri explained that the causes of ectopic pregnancies are many but also includes Pelvic infections like Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID), often caused by Sexually Transmitted bacteria such as Chlamydia or Gonorrhea, that leave scars that block the tube.

He mentioned that other conditions that lead to the situation of a fertilized egg getting stuck and implanting outside the main cavity of the uterus are scar tissue from past surgeries and endometriosis.

Dr expressed concern that the majority of the 22 women that had ectopic pregnancies sought medical attention late, leading to doctors conducting emergency surgeries.

He urged women to begin antenatal care early and to seek immediate medical attention if they experience severe abdominal pain or abnormal bleeding during pregnancy.

Mr Phiri further called on families and communities to support women in accessing reproductive health services in order to reduce maternal complications and deaths.

According to health experts and reports by Cleveland Clinic, a woman can still conceive after ectopic pregnancy surgery, and statistics show that roughly 65% to 85% of women go on to have a healthy, successful pregnancy within two years.

World.title: Government launches strategy to formalise artisanal mining
World.content:
Government has launched the Zambia Artisanal and Small-Scale Mining (ASM) Strategy 2025–2029 aimed at transforming the subsector into a formal, productive and sustainable contributor to national development.

Speaking during the launch in Lusaka today, Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development Permanent Secretary Hapenga Kabeta said the strategy provides a unified roadmap to formalise artisanal mining and address challenges affecting the sector.

“This strategy compels us to sing from one hymn sheet so that we pursue one national vision for artisanal and small-scale mining,” Dr Kabeta said.

Dr Kabeta said government has prioritised formalisation through reforms, including the establishment of the Directorate of Artisanal and Small-Scale Mining under the Geological and Minerals Development Act No. 2 of 2025.

He further noted that government has completed 87.5 percent of the nationwide airborne geophysical survey to provide geological information that will support mineral exploration and investment.

“Execution, execution, execution is what makes the difference. We can have the best documents, but without implementation they will not achieve our objectives,” he said.

Dr Kabeta further urged artisanal miners to keep proper production records, embrace value addition and build stronger partnerships with large-scale mining companies to improve productivity.

Meanwhile, United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Resident Representative James Wakiaga, in remarks delivered by Programme Specialist Chali Selisho, described the strategy as a major milestone towards inclusive economic growth, job creation and poverty reduction.

Dr Wakiaga said the strategy provides a practical framework for formalising artisanal mining, promoting safer mining practices, strengthening environmental stewardship and increasing the participation of women and young people.

“UNDP remains fully committed to supporting the Government of Zambia in implementing this strategy and advancing a mining sector that is productive, inclusive, resilient and environmentally responsible,” he said.

He highlighted that UNDP, through the ACP-EU Development Minerals Programme, supported the development of the strategy, the ASM Training Manual and the ASM Digital System, while strengthening the capacity of miners and government institutions.

And Federation of Small-Scale Mining Associations of Zambia President Joseph Mwansa welcomed the strategy, saying it marks the beginning of a new era for more than 600,000 Zambians who depend on artisanal and small-scale mining.

“Formalisation means our miners can finally access finance, reach fair markets, adopt safer technology, protect the environment and add value to what we mine,” Mr Mwansa said.

The strategy is expected to strengthen governance, improve access to finance, technology and markets, promote environmental stewardship and increase the participation of women and young people in Zambia’s mining sector.

World.title: Zambia mints first two medals at Glasgow 2026
World.content:
Team Zambia on Friday secured its first two medals at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games from boxing after Catherine Mwape and Emmanuel Katema claimed bronze medals in their respective weight categories.

Mwape made history by becoming the first Zambian female boxer to win a Commonwealth Games medal, earning bronze in the Women’s 54kg category. Her medal is also Team Zambia’s first medal at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games.

Mwape settled for bronze after a spirited performance in the semi-final, where she was defeated by Preeti Preeti of India.

The National Olympic Committee of Zambia – NOCZ said throughout the tournament, she demonstrated courage, determination and skill to secure her place on the podium and write her name into Zambia’s sporting history.

“Despite falling to Preeti of India in the Women’s 54kg Semi-Final, Catherine displayed tremendous courage, determination and skill throughout the competition to secure Zambia another medal on the Commonwealth stage,” NOCZ stated.

In the men’s boxing, Katema added to Team Zambia’s medal tally by winning bronze in the 65kg category, becoming Team Zambia’s second medallist at the Games.

Katema’s campaign came to an end in the semi-final following a hard-fought contest against Patris Mughalzai of England.

His outstanding performances throughout the competition showcased his resilience, talent and determination, earning Zambia another place on the Commonwealth Games podium.

“Congratulations to Catherine Mwape and Emmanuel Katema for flying the Zambian flag high at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games,” NOCZ stated.

By Friday lunchtime, Zambia was number 26 on the overall medals table.

By news time, Australia was leading the medals table with 51 gold, 24 silver and 35 bronze.

Nigeria is so far the best performing African nation with 8 gold, 5 silver and 3 bronze.

World.title: The panic is showing – and it isn’t coming from Mundubile
World.content:
By Moses Kachali

There is a pattern worth watching as Zambia counts down to August 13, and it has less to do with what Brian Mundubile is saying than with how quickly his opponents feel the need to answer it.

Take the Solwezi episode. Mundubile links an alleged altercation involving musicians to the ruling party. Within hours, UPND’s media machine is out with a statement accusing him of “manufacturing lies and desperate tactics,” insisting the opposition is “panicked” because “defeat is imminent.”

Read that statement twice. It spends more energy describing the opposition’s supposed psychological state than addressing the substance of the claim. That is not the language of a campaign that feels safe. It is the language of a campaign that has noticed the ground shifting and wants to say so before anyone else does.

Contrast that with what Mundubile has actually been offering voters this week. In Kasisa, he is standing before a chief, promising to restore the ministry that traditional leaders say has fallen away, and putting a specific number on it: royalties from minerals extracted in their own chiefdoms. In Solwezi, he is not shouting slogans. He is naming Mufumbwe, Kikonge and Kasenseli by name, telling young miners who have faced guns instead of support that a government of his would organise, train and protect them instead of confronting them.

Whatever one thinks of the promises, they are promises about roads not yet built and mines not yet regulated. They are forward-looking. UPND’s response, by comparison, has been backward-looking, an accusation about intent, a demand that Mundubile hand over footage, a statement about who is “panicking.” When the incumbent’s loudest answer to a policy pitch is a character claim, it tells you something about which side feels it is losing the argument.

And there is a bitter irony sitting in plain sight for anyone tempted to trust the machinery of order over the substance of an argument. Mwala Yuyi was, until recently, the man in charge of policing an entire province, one of the very officers this government leaned on to keep the peace it now insists it has delivered. He is now charged alongside a magistrate, a clerk of court and fellow officers over copper cathodes that vanished from evidence and turned up at a private auction.

If the institution meant to guard against exactly this kind of decay could not keep its own house honest, voters are entitled to ask how much weight to place on assurances about who is “manufacturing” trouble and who is not. An accusation is cheap. A commissioner in handcuffs is not.

Zambians do not need slogans from either side over the next thirteen days. They need to see whether a party seeking a fresh mandate can make its case on delivery, and whether a party seeking to unseat it can make its case on specifics rather than grievance. So far, it is Mundubile naming mines, chiefs and mineral royalties by name. It is UPND naming Mundubile’s motives, while its own former enforcer awaits trial.

If the ruling party has done the work, that work will hold up without anyone needing to accuse the other side of panic first. Let the record argue for itself. Right now, the record includes a commissioner in the dock.

This is an opinion column. The views expressed are the author’s own.

World.title: UPND accuses Mundubile of politicising Solwezi musicians incident
World.content:
UPND accuses Mundubile of politicising Solwezi incident before police conclude investigations

The United Party for National Development (UPND) has accused National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) presidential candidate Brian Mundubile of attempting to politicise an alleged altercation involving musicians in Solwezi before police have concluded their investigations.

UPND Media Director Mark Simuuwe said Mr Mundubile’s public statements amounted to prejudging the matter and risked undermining the constitutional mandate of the Zambia Police Service to investigate criminal allegations independently and without political interference.

The remarks follow Mr Mundubile’s claims linking President Hakainde Hichilema and the ruling UPND to the reported incident in Solwezi, allegations the governing party has dismissed as unfounded and politically motivated.

In a statement issued in Lusaka, Mr Simuuwe said the opposition leader was seeking to exploit an incident that remains under active police investigation.

“Facing the overwhelming momentum of President Hakainde Hichilema’s nationwide campaign, a panicked opposition has realised that defeat is imminent and is resorting to manufacturing lies and desperate tactics. Zambia is a nation of laws. Let the police execute their constitutional mandate without political interference or pressure,” Mr Simuuwe said.

He maintained that the UPND government had dismantled political cadreism and violence in public spaces and did not shield individuals suspected of committing criminal offences, regardless of political affiliation.

Mr Simuuwe urged the Zambia Police Service in North-Western Province to carry out a thorough, professional and impartial investigation to establish the facts surrounding the reported altercation.

He also challenged Mr Mundubile to hand over any evidence in his possession to investigators instead of litigating the matter through public statements.

“Mr Mundubile asserts that his party possesses video footage identifying the alleged perpetrators. If he is sincere about seeking justice rather than orchestrating a political stunt, we challenge him to immediately submit this unedited footage directly to the police,” he said.

Mr Simuuwe said pursuing the matter through social media before investigations were complete risked undermining due process and inflaming political tensions at a time when the country was preparing for the August 13 general election.

He further defended the constitutional rights of artists, musicians and performers to freely associate with any political party or movement without intimidation, harassment or violence.

According to the UPND, attempts to implicate President Hichilema in isolated incidents ignored the Head of State’s repeated calls for peaceful campaigns and his consistent instructions to party members and security agencies to uphold law, order and democratic discipline throughout the election period.

Mr Simuuwe said assigning blame before police establish the facts served neither justice nor the public interest, adding that political leaders should allow law enforcement agencies to discharge their constitutional responsibilities independently.

He urged all political parties to focus on issue-based campaigns rather than exploit unverified incidents for political gain, saying Zambians expected leaders to present practical solutions to the country’s challenges instead of heightening political tensions through speculation.

“UPND remains committed to a peaceful, issue-based campaign and calls on all stakeholders to safeguard the peace and unity that Zambia is known for,” Mr Simuuwe said.

He added that since assuming office, President Hichilema’s administration had taken deliberate steps to eliminate political violence and restore law and order, reaffirming the government’s commitment to peaceful democratic engagement.

Police have already opened investigations into the reported Solwezi incident, with authorities expected to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged altercation before determining whether any criminal offences were committed.

World.title: Samukonga qualifies for 400m final
World.content:
Sprinter Muzala Samukonga has qualified for the men’s 400m final at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games.

Samukonga put himself in the right position to defend the title he won at the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games after a semifinal triumph.

He finished second in his semi-final after clocking 45.95s.

UK’s Thomas Reynolds won the race after clocking 45.63s.

Samukonga’s compatriots Patrick Nyambe and Kennedy Luchembe also recorded impressive results in their respective men’s 400m semi-finals. Nyambe clocked 46.50s while Luchembe clocked 46.60s.

In the women’s 400m semi-final, Niddy Mingilishi clocked 55.10s.

Despite their determined performances, Nyambe, Luchembe, and Mingilishi did not progress to the men’s and women’s 400m finals.

The trio will now shift focus to the 4x400m mixed relay, where they will join the rest of Team Zambia’s relay squad in pursuit of a strong performance.

Samukonga remains Zambia’s sole representative in the men’s 400m final as he bids for a medal.

Meanwhile, the National Olympic Committee of Zambia – NOCZ has applauded the performance of boxer Albert Ngulube despite his elimination from the Commonwealth Games.

Ngulube was eliminated from the Men’s 60kg category at the quarter-final stage.

“The young Zambian boxer earned widespread admiration for the spirited performance he delivered against defending Commonwealth champion Jude Gallagher of Northern Ireland. Ngulube pushed the experienced champion all the way in a closely contested contest that was decided by a 2–3 split decision, highlighting the determination, skill and composure he displayed on one of boxing’s biggest stages,” NOCZ stated.

“Making his Commonwealth Games debut, Ngulube proved he belongs among the elite, giving Team Zambia and the nation plenty to be proud of. His courageous display has marked him as one of Zambia’s exciting boxing prospects,” NOCZ added.
